There’s no _system_ for brand, and nothing can actually _call_ it, and so most of what gets shipped is off-brand by default.

We think brand is becoming infrastructure: one canonical source of truth that any system can query. Bloom is that brand layer - we’re creating the systems to make brand as wieldable as code.\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CpmsCzswCSY>

**How it works**

1. **Ingest.** Point Bloom at everything that defines your brand: website, decks, Figma, socials, codebases, and more.
2. **Systemise.** Bloom unifies it into one brand system - a canonical ontology of your brand.
3. **Deploy anywhere.** Call that system from every surface and generate every asset you need - ads, social, product shots, mockups, and full campaigns.

**Built for agents** \
Bloom is designed to be used by agents, rather than humans. The primitives (API, MCP, and soon CLI) have excellent _agent ergonomics_ making your brand callable from everywhere:

* **Agents:** marketing agents running campaigns, coding agents creating landing pages, e-commerce agents running brands - all calling Bloom over MCP.
* **Products:** use our API as the brand layer for any products that require brand context or assets for their customers.
* **Brand and marketing operations:** agencies and marketing teams call Bloom to automate on-brand asset creation inside their existing stack.
* **Claude:** use the Claude connector to create on-brand assets with all of your existing context.

**Traction** - We launched v1 in December and went [viral](https://x.com/rincidium/status/1995946528343818656?s=20). Since then we’ve generated over 175,000 on-brand assets for our customers.

name: Carrot Labs
long_description:
The problem: 
AI has quietly become one of the largest and fastest-growing line items for companies. Spend is scattered across a dozen provider consoles that each show one number at the end of the month and nothing about why it moved. There's no unified view, and no way to trace a dollar back to the customer, feature, team, or even the pull request that caused it.

Which customers are unprofitable once you subtract their AI costs? Which feature is quietly burning your Anthropic budget? Is this week's spike a runaway loop or real growth? How much did that AI-written PR actually cost to ship?
Today teams reverse-engineer answers by exporting CSVs from each provider and stitching them together in a spreadsheet, and by the time they do, the money is already spent.

What SuperPenguin does: SuperPenguin tracks AI spend across 14 providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AWS Bedrock, Azure, Modal, Cursor, OpenRouter, and more).

* Zero-code setup: connect an API key and costs sync automatically with model-level breakdowns, trends, and forecasts
* Per-request attribution: add two lines with our Python or TypeScript SDK to tag every AI call by customer, feature, team, or environment (or any other metadata).
* AI coding cost per PR: connect Cursor to see engineering spend attributed to each pull request, repo, and developer, so you know what it actually costs to ship.
* Alerts on budget thresholds and spend anomalies, delivered to Slack, email, or Discord.

Most teams are set up in under five minutes. We help companies see where their AI money goes and whether it's worth it.
one_liner: AI Cost Management: Track and attribute AI spend across every provider

launches.tagline: Your model is your moat. Stop renting your intelligence and start growing it.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Carrot Labs helps you build models for your agents that are faster and better, forever. Use our platform to build proprietary models using open source that progressively improve.

[**Our Launch Video**](https://youtu.be/Qiw-HG14AVE)

## **The Problems:**

Frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google are constantly pushing the boundary of intelligence further, but great quality comes with high latency and cost. Smaller models are fast, but can't get the job done right.

So you start modifying system prompts. It takes you far enough, but at some point you hit a ceiling. And every time a new model comes out, your prompts don't work the same way anymore! (just February 2026 alone, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 from Anthropic, Gemini 3.1 Pro from Google, GPT-5.3-Codex from Open AI, Qwen 3.5 from Alibaba came out to name a few.)

## **Solution:**

We build you a proprietary model tuned to your tasks so you always have access to the most performant model for your agent.

Our platform records your agent’s activity and tunes an optimized model from an open source base model. Once it's ready, swap out the frontier model for yours. That's it. As new production data flows in, we continuously evaluate and retrain your model to boost performance. What you get is a model specialized to your tasks that outperforms frontier.

## **Why this matters to your startup:**

In the short run, you need your agent to be faster and more accurate, and prompt tuning will only get you so far. We are the fastest way to get there.

In the long run, every company building agents is using the same frontier models. Your competitor has the same intelligence you do. The thing that differentiates you is the knowledge you distill into your own model. Your model is your moat.

## **Team:**

Chris led AI at Skylo Technologies, the world's largest commercial direct-to-device satellite network that provides satellite communications services to Google, Samsung, and Garmin devices.

Yuta was a senior data scientist at Snowflake where he developed financial forecasts through ML that supported the company's hypergrowth from pre-IPO to billions in revenue.

## **How you can help:**

If you are building agents or know anyone building agents who would appreciate a model that outperforms frontier on their tasks, let us know at [contact@carrotlabs.ai](mailto:contact@carrotlabs.ai).

Our self-serve agent eval SDKs are available. Feel free to use it! You can sign up from here: <https://platform.carrotlabs.ai/login>.

Shofo is building the largest index of videos.

<https://youtu.be/C0c3Q3MsRUg>

### **❌ The Problem**

AI labs require massive, high-quality video data to train multimodal models, but clean, custom video datasets cost millions and take months to collect.

### **✅ Our Solution**

We're building the world's largest library of videos by combining public videos collected from the open web and private videos aggregated from thousands of different sources. OpenVector is already live and seeing use cases across security, retail, manufacturing, and logistics. We are tracking production cycle efficiency directly from existing CCTV, ensuring good-manufacturing-practices, and catching physical design errors.

launches.title: Cardinal: The Most Accurate Document Intelligence API
launches.tagline: Cardinal turns unstructured, messy documents into perfectly structured data, instantly and with unmatched accuracy.
launches.body:
**Hey everyone – Devi and Jianna here** 👋🏼

We met while studying at MIT and Harvard, and our last company processed utility data at scale. The biggest bottleneck? OCR. It was terrible - especially for complex documents where preserving structure was critical. After years of wrestling with these OCR limitations, we decided to build something better. That became Cardinal.

📃 **The Problem**

 Most enterprise knowledge is trapped in PDFs and other unstructured formats -  medical forms, contracts, invoices, insurance claims, financial statements, packing slips, etc. 

OCR is _not_ a solved problem:

* LLMs hallucinate and can fabricate data
* Annotations, checkmarks, and handwritten notes get ignored
* Tables, charts, and images are dropped entirely
* Layouts are mangled, breaking document structure and making the output unusable for code, retrieval, or downstream automation. Preserving the semantic meaning of the document is nearly impossible.

\
🚀 **Our Solution**

Cardinal has 2 finetuned models. The first model, _Document-to-Markdown_, accurately converts even complex documents into clean, structured Markdown. The second model, _Markdown-to-Code_, then turns that Markdown into ready-to-use HTML, preserving the original formatting and hierarchy exactly.

Put simply, we can help you:

* Reliably extract structured data from the most complex PDFs
* Preserve exact layouts for retrieval, search, and downstream LLM workflows
* Convert charts into data, summarize images, and parse complex tables
* Run natural language extractions for any field without brittle regex or templates

Full Demo video: [https://youtu.be/RouYM1cKGXI](https://youtu.be/RouYM1cKGXI?feature=shared)

## <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yOKcdERZe9w>

## The Problem

Ops, procurement, and customer-service teams at manufacturers spend the majority of their week on coordination that is clearly defined but never automated:

* Chasing suppliers for ETAs
* Processing incoming RFQs
* Routing PO approvals
* Monitoring order exceptions
* Following up on stale opportunities

Every person on one of these teams could write down the exact steps for the task, and yet nobody has built the thing that runs those steps reliably at scale.

The tooling around this problem is stuck in a half-finished state:

* ERP-native AI answers questions about ERP data; it doesn’t execute the multi-step workflows that sit between the data and the work getting done.
* Middleware and iPaaS connect systems but don’t make decisions.
* Systems integrators custom-code workflows that take quarters to ship and break when a process changes.
* BPO adds variable cost and leaves the underlying coordination fragmented.

When a manufacturer adds a product line, a new region, or a new supplier tier, the coordination load scales linearly, and so does the headcount requirement.

## What We Built

Atlas generates autonomous coordination agents on top of the ERP systems manufacturers already run: SAP, NetSuite, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Odoo, and more.

A workflow that today takes a quarter to custom-code or an ongoing BPO contract to staff is, on Atlas, described in plain English and stood up as a running agent in hours.

## Workflows We’ve Deployed

### Procurement & Supplier Coordination

Chases supplier responses, confirms ETAs, routes PO approvals, and escalates exceptions before they become missed deliveries.

### RFQ to Quote

Parses incoming RFQs from email or portal, prices against history and current cost, drafts and routes quotes for approval, and tracks through to response.

### Order & Exception Handling

Monitors order status across ERP and transport systems, surfaces exceptions before they escalate, and maintains a complete audit trail.

Turn any manual process into automation simply by prompting an agent.\

launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re Charles and Dean - cofounders of Stage.

**👉 tldr:** Drowning in AI generated PRs? Tired of using GitHub? Us too. Stage is a code review platform designed to help you understand and review changes 5x faster.

<https://youtu.be/EjMjGAqSLvo>

**💻 How to get started**

Try it out today at[ https://stagereview.app/](https://stagereview.app/) - all you need is your GitHub account.

It’s free for your first 14 days, and then you can use _LAUNCH_ to get 25% off for 3 months :)

Other ways to try it out:

* Try our demo on any public GitHub PR [here](https://stagereview.app/try)
* Download our open source CLI [tool](https://github.com/ReviewStage/stage-cli) - runs locally and works with any coding agent

**❌ The Problem**

Engineering teams are shipping faster than ever, but now they’re drowning in an endless backlog of PRs to review. The bottleneck isn't writing code anymore, it's reviewing it.

This leads to:

* PRs being rubber stamped without getting closely looked at
* Unexpected behaviors slipping through to production
* Your engineers merging changes they don’t really understand

Code review bots are great at catching surface level bugs but don’t solve the root problem.

Engineers need a faster way of understanding changes and giving meaningful feedback, and GitHub’s UI hasn’t changed in over a decade.

**🧠 How it works**

We’re redesigning the code review experience around the way that engineers naturally read PRs.

* When you open a PR or push a new commit, Stage groups your changes into small logical “chapters”
* These chapters get ordered in the way that makes most sense to read
* For each chapter, Stage tells you what changed and specific things to double check
* Once you review all the chapters, you’re done reviewing the PR!

Everything is synced seamlessly with GitHub (commenting, approving, etc) so it fits right into the workflows you’re already used to.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101617&key=user_uploads/327595/5004c374-be1f-47fa-a182-638252d50cf6)

**❤️ Why did we start Stage?**

We're two engineers who got frustrated with using GitHub for code review. 

As coding agents started taking off, we saw our PR backlog pile up faster than we could handle. Not only that, the PRs themselves were getting larger and harder to understand, and we spent most of our time trying to build a mental model of what a PR was actually doing.

We built Stage to make reviewing a PR feel more like reading chapters of a book, not an unorganized set of paragraphs. We use it every day now (not just to review each other's code, but also our own!) and at this point we can't really imagine going back to using GitHub.

**👋 About Us**

Charles and Dean met in their very first class at Stanford freshman year, and have been best friends ever since.

They ended up taking every class together, worked at the same quant trading firm after graduating, and were roommates in New York before joining YC. They saw firsthand how AI caused code review to break down and started Stage to rebuild the experience for how teams operate today.

# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR:** AI marketing service for product-led software companies. We produce marketing artifacts at the same time you ship code. We turn your real product into social posts and demo videos in your voice automatically. Think of it as a clone of you that's also marketing your company at the same time.\
\
<https://youtu.be/qAfRjaRQw3g>

**We'd love to meet:**

    **•    Technical founders who want to build in public** 

    **•    Devtool/B2B SaaS teams** where features ship weekly but marketing ships quarterly. We close that gap.

    **•    Operators who've run GTM for devtools at scale** — we'd love to hear what worked and what didn't.

Reach out: [maanav@trymemoir.ai](mailto:maanav@trymemoir.ai) · [jason@trymemoir.ai](mailto:jason@trymemoir.ai) · DM on Bookface · <https://calendly.com/maanav-memoir/30min>

**Why this exists**

The technical teams who build the best products are often the worst at marketing them. Not because they don't care, but because the existing marketing stack is built for someone else. Demo tools cost $30K/year and require sales calls. Social tools want briefs and brand guidelines. Agencies want six-week timelines. Meanwhile, the engineer-founder ships features into a void.

Now that the cost of development is so low, the biggest differentiator is no longer product, its distribution and how well you can capture your target audience. This only happens if you build in public.

The gap isn't talent or budget, it's that marketing infrastructure hasn't caught up with how technical teams actually work.

Memoir is one system. It reads your repo, drives your live staging app with an AI agent, generates branded demo videos with synthetic data so dashboards look real and narrates them in a voice cloned from yours. Then it drafts posts for X / LinkedIn / HN in your writing voice (learned from how you've posted before) and ships them to your audience after you approve them. The output is indistinguishable from how you'd write and record it yourself, if you had the time.

**How we got here**

Jason and I met as interns at IMC Trading. We both wanted to build in devtools, and our first attempt was Memoir as an AI company brain, a knowledge base that synced with your code so internal docs stayed current. Real problem on paper, and people nodded when we described it. But nobody felt urgency about it. Stale docs are annoying, but they don't make you feel like you're losing

What we kept noticing while building that, though, was a different pain that _did_ make founders feel like they were losing. We kept hearing the same thing from every successful founder and mentor: build in public, share your product, post consistently. And we kept failing to do it. Not because we didn't want to, but because we'd rather keep building than figure out what to post.

We watched it happen around us. The teams getting real inbound weren't always the ones with the best product, they were the ones whose founders showed up online. Jason had run a reselling business in high school and scaled multiple social accounts to real followings, so he'd seen distribution work firsthand. I've always been obsessed with marketing strategy, partly because my dad's in the space, partly because I've watched so many teams get ahead of others because of their marketing.

**What's there today**

We ingest code changes to post product updates, create custom demo videos, and turn relevant current events into advertisements. We currently handle X, Linkedin, and Hackernews posting.

**Why us**

Two technical founders who got tired of watching engineering-led companies stay invisible. If you've watched a great product fail to find its audience, or you're running one right now and feeling that exact thing, reach out.

launches.body:
Hi there, I'm Connor from [Replicas](https://replicas.dev/) :)

Recently, you might have seen Stripe and Ramp release blogs outlining their in-house background coding agents. This showed us that background agents, with the proper tooling, can be relied on to ship critical production code.

Replicas is a background coding agent that can run your codebase locally.

We’re used by 20+ YC startups at all team sizes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/b35f4253-6fd0-478b-a04f-26f73a18b625)

**The Problem**

Background coding agents are a huge productivity boost for clearing tickets and shipping faster.

The existing solutions - CC/Codex on Cloud, Cursor Agents - lock you into one harness and give you **no control over the environment**.

This defeats the entire point of "background" agents. A powerful background agent should run everything locally, verify its work, and iterate until it's satisfied.

**How Replicas Works**

**Replicas** helps you delegate to as many background agents as you need:

\- Bring your own Claude/Codex credentials

\- Each agent gets a sandbox VM with your code cloned

\- The agent installs deps, spins up databases, runs services, and verifies its work locally

\- When it's done, it opens a PR for you to review

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/e20b6968-523d-4376-a05c-ba175cc61611)

Replicas can be triggered from Slack, Linear, GitHub (PR reviews, CI/CD failures), the Dashboard, or API.

The biggest difference is **Environments**. You can configure the following:

\- Files

\- Env vars

\- Start hooks

\- Warm hooks

\- Skills/MCPs

It's built so that its flexible to any kind of codebase, allowing Replicas to run everything locally just like a human engineer would.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/df185d7b-b90e-455f-9ff7-10dcefcfd8c7)

Replicas can also create **Previews**:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/7be01ba9-b653-43f2-975d-234002802e15)

Meaning you can check out services (e.g web app on `3000`) running on the sandbox's VM from your computer with just a click :)

Check out this writeup for Replicas V1 for more details:

<https://www.replicas.dev/notes/replicas-v1>

**Demo Video**

<https://youtube.com/watch?v=uyH77T-pcXc>

**What's Next**

\- **Automations + API**: Improving our API and adding an automations menu, e.g having Replicas run every night.

\- **Recursive**: Replicas can break down super complex tasks by creating more Replicas instances.

\- **Lowering Latency**: For larger teams, improving our warm pool and snapshotting infrastructure to make spinning up Replicas feel _instant_ (more than it already does)

\- **Long-term Memory**

\- and what our customers ask for :p

**What I'm asking from you**

\- Sign up (<https://replicas.dev>) or reach out ([connor@replicas.dev](mailto:connor@replicas.dev))

\- Check out \[this writeup\](<https://www.replicas.dev/notes/replicas-v1>) for Replicas V1

\- Upvote if this resonates with you!

[Palette](https://palettelabs.com/) is an AI-native media platform built by MIT computer scientists and multimodal researchers that unifies the creative workflow into a single generation engine. We eliminate tool and context fragmentation for creative teams in enterprises and allow content creators to transform static assets into controllable, repeatable workflows in one conversation.

Check out our demo [here](https://youtu.be/xKibxXF9pGw)

**The Problem**

Today, in order to deliver high-quality, tasteful content, individual content creators and enterprise teams struggle with a heavily fragmented landscape of separate, disconnected applications for multimodal content production. launches.title: Scope - The Agent Experience Platform
launches.tagline: We help companies understand and improve how AI agents discover, choose, and use their product
launches.body:
Hey everyone! I’m Anand, founder of Scope.

**Problem**\
More and more products are now being used through Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and similar agents. If your product is accessible to an agent, the agent can now decide which product to use, how to set it up, and whether it keeps using it after that. Most companies still can’t see that process clearly.

That means they often do not know when an agent is choosing them vs. a competitor, where it is getting stuck, or what part of the product or docs is causing the problem.

**Solution**\
That’s what Scope is for.

We run real workflows across agents and show teams:

* when the agent chooses them vs. a competitor
* where it breaks
* where docs or product surfaces confuse the agent
* what to change to get better results

A simple example: a company thinks their product works well with agents, but on a real task the agent picks a competitor, gets stuck during auth, or goes down the wrong path because the docs are unclear. Scope shows the trace, where it failed, and what to change.

We’re already working with Blaxel and a decacorn.

**Demo video:**\
<https://youtu.be/OqtaJbjMbiQ>

**Why I’m working on this**\
Before Scope, I did interpretability research on closed-source models at Princeton, then worked as an ML engineer on GEO / AEO. I kept seeing the same thing: these systems were starting to shape product discovery and product usage in real ways, but for companies, the process was still mostly a black box. I wanted to build something that makes that behavior visible and useful to the teams trying to fix it.

**Ask**

* If you’re building a product that can be used by an agent, an API, an infra product, a CLI, or an MCP server, I’d be happy to run Scope on your product and send you what we find.

**TL;DR: Marker partners with execs, learns how their organization actually works, finds the highest-impact problems, and solves them by** **shipping custom AI agents into production on the Marker platform in weeks. Each agent deepens our understanding of the business, so the next agent launches faster. We stay embedded until the business is rebuilt.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O829Y4wlKvk>

We’re Will Drevno, Richard Berwick, and David Pastewka, the founders of Marker. We’ve built together for 15 years. Our last company, Drapr (YC S20), was acquired by Gap Inc., and Richard went on to found Gap’s Office of AI.

## **Why we built Marker**

Inside Gap, we saw firsthand how much leaders wanted to transform their businesses with AI and how hard it was to turn that ambition into production systems that actually changed how their organizations worked.

**95% of AI initiatives still fail. Ours don’t.**

The hard part is understanding how work happens across people, systems, and teams; choosing the opportunities that matter most; and getting solutions into production.

## **How Marker works**

We embed with each company and lead the transformation end to end:

* **Understand the organization.** We listen closely to leaders and frontline teams, learn their systems and ways of working, and map the processes that usually live in people’s heads.
* **Find the biggest opportunities.** We identify and prioritize the problems where AI can have the greatest impact on cost, capacity, speed, or growth.
* **Build and ship.** We create custom agents and automations around the company’s real workflows and systems. The agents we deploy run on the Marker Command Center and go live in production within weeks.
* **Compound.** Every agent we deploy deepens our understanding of the company. That helps us launch the next one faster and makes Marker increasingly integral to how the organization operates.

## **Who we’re working with today**

We’re rebuilding companies from mid-size through Fortune 500.

## **Why us**

We’ve sat on every side of this: founders selling into enterprises, operators transforming one from the inside, and executives responsible for enterprise AI. Marker is the company we wish we could have hired at Gap.

**If you are (or you know) a leader looking for real AI transformation—not another pilot, deck, or self-serve tool—please send them our way.**

long_description:
Lightsprint is a collaborative software factory for product teams to plan visually, preview live and ship with an army of cloud agents. Your whole team, including non-engineers, can now ship end to end reliably.

The company is founded by Ben Ong, an AI investor who previously scaled AI products at SEA Group (NYSE: SE) and Temasek ($300B fund), Benedict Chan who was VP Engineering at Chainlink and CTO at BitGo (NYSE:BTGO), and Heng Hong Lee who built Facebook Messenger in 2013 and was Director of Engineering at Fazz (YC S17).
one_liner: Software factory for product teams

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Product changes (a copy tweak, a pricing page update, a new business logic update) often wait behind an engineering sprint. The PM files a ticket. Follows up in standup. Two weeks later, it ships.

Coding agents like Cursor and Claude Code made engineers 10x faster, but that speed never reached the rest of the product team. The PM still files a ticket and waits. The tools pitched at "non-technical builders" - Lovable, Replit - only spin up new prototypes from scratch. None of them touch the product you actually run.

Each of us hit this from a different side. Ben saw this bottleneck from the investor seat through his portfolio companies and during his time at SEA group as a PM. Heng Hong saw it from inside engineering: engineer time burned on changes anyone should be able to make. Benedict saw it from infrastructure: the plumbing to let non-engineers ship safely didn't exist yet.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Every person at a company will be able to ship product changes, not just engineers. The barrier between having an idea and shipping it disappears.   

PMs won't file tickets. Designers won't hand off mockups and wait. Founders won't choose between learning to code or hiring an engineer for a copy change. Engineering backlogs will shrink from bottleneck to review queue. Review comments get aggregated and fed back to the agent, which self-heals before an engineer steps in.

Engineers will focus on architecture, infrastructure, and the hard problems - while everyone else ships the changes they're closest to the customer to make. Software development becomes a team sport. We think this is as big a shift as when spreadsheets let non-finance people work with data, or when Canva let non-designers create graphics. Product agents will do the same for software.

**tldr:** We are building a collaborative platform for software teams to plan visually, preview live and ship with an army of cloud agents. Your whole team, including non-engineers, can now ship end to end reliably.

<https://youtu.be/P9e-5Mg72fc>

**The problem**\
Software is built by teams. But AI coding agents run alone on one developer’s IDE or terminal.\
The result: teammates are out of sync, planning stays buried in docs, and reviewers approve changes with little context. Execution has never been faster. But coordination has never been more painful. \
\
The SDLC was built around coding. Coding has changed, and the SDLC must be updated.\
\
**The solution**\
Lightsprint makes agentic software development collaborative. It completes the entire AI loop - not just code gen, but the full cycle from requirements to shipped code, with your whole team in the game.

1. **Visual Plan Mode**: Write a simple requirement. Lightsprint breaks it into a structured plan with tasks, dependencies, and visual options to choose from. Your whole team collaborates with the agent on the plan: see it, annotate it, and approve it. No more blind execution.
2. **Infinite Parallel Cloud Agents**: Hit execute and Lightsprint spins up multiple agents working your codebase simultaneously. One’s building the frontend component, another is building a dashboard, a third is writing tests. Anyone can steer the agent. What takes a team days gets compressed into hours.
3. **PR Preview Environments**: Every PR automatically gets a live preview URL. Not a diff. A running instance of the code. Your designer clicks through it and says “yes, ship it” or “change the layout” without reading a single line of code. Everyone on your team ships code now.

We’ve been using Lightsprint to build Lightsprint, and it has dramatically increased our engineering velocity. Lightsprint is also mobile-friendly so you can fire tasks from wherever you are. That has been a game-changer for us!

\
**About Us**\
The team is made of Ben Chan who was the previous CTO of Bitgo (NYSE: BTGO) and has led engineering teams of 300; Heng Hong, an engineering leader from Meta who built FB messenger; and Ben Ong, an ex VC who was part of the venture building arm at Temasek (300B AUM fund) and led products at SEA group (NYSE: SE).

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Saffron gives candidates a real codebase and ability to use any AI tooling they'd use on the job. We capture every prompt, diff, and decision in a sandboxed environment that gets scored automatically. Teams can now get structured metrics on how candidates actually build, not just whether the final output compiles.

Book an onboarding call here: [**https://trysaffron.ai**](https://trysaffron.ai)

**Our Launch Video**

<https://youtu.be/pJHXqTKKMRQ>

---

**The Problem**

AI coding tools have finally gotten good enough to actually change how engineers work. But the way companies evaluate SWEs hasn't changed at all.

Now, interviews are testing the wrong thing and candidates are passing every round of your hiring process, before showing up on the job unable to build a single feature without AI doing the thinking for them.

On the flip side, companies are missing out on engineers who actually know how to use AI to be ten times more efficient.

We know because we've been on both sides. As candidates, we realized how how much potential there was to become 10x with AI. As founders, we’ve heard the same story from dozens of teams: "They crushed the interview. Two weeks in, they couldn't ship anything independently."

---

**Our Approach**

We’ve built an assessment that embraces AI and measures how efficient an engineer is. Candidates get a real codebase, AI tools they’d actually use on the job, and a task that simulates engineering work. We capture the full process and evaluate it automatically.

---

**⚙️ How It Works**

**Step 1: Create an assessment in under 5 minutes.** Point us at your GitHub repo or choose a question from our bank, configure AI agents, and invite candidates.

![uploaded image](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=100291&key=user_uploads%2F2767627%2F8e7827fe-4250-4411-b495-f0b5d2dbbd18&variant=large)

**Step 2: Candidates build in a fully managed environment.** They get an online IDE that they can customize, a timer, and a real task. No setup required on their end. After coding, they answer debrief questions about their own implementation — and we verify their answers.

![uploaded image](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=100291&key=user_uploads%2F2767627%2F9e27fefd-a405-4ae1-859c-5b83c72af8e0&variant=large)

**Step 3: Review results without reading a single line of code.** AI review agents score the submission across dimensions you configure with specific evidence from the codebase. We show you detailed metrics like prompts, AI reliance percentage, or tool calling, and give a deterministic score on how well the candidate did.

![uploaded image](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=100291&key=user_uploads%2F2767627%2F3645c5c3-534f-4a40-a8d9-d662bd13a0e9&variant=large)

---

**Why Us**

We’re Robert, Jerry, and Kazuma. We met in high school, started building together, and have been close friends ever since. Robert studied at MIT and was at Jane Street. Jerry studied at Stanford and was also at Jane Street. Kazuma studied at Harvey Mudd and was published in NeurIPS and ICML.

All three of us were CS students recruiting for SWE jobs the entirety of our first semester of college. And after noticing how much our coding workflow had changed with the introduction of better and better models, we knew that assessments had to catch up.

---

**Our Ask**

* **Hiring SWEs?** We'll set up your first assessment for free, configure it to your codebase, and work with you 1:1 to build out whatever you need. We're early and hungry. Book a call: [**https://trysaffron.ai**](https://trysaffron.ai)
* **Know an engineering lead, head of talent, or recruiter** who's frustrated with their current process? We'd love an intro.

Can't wait to hear your feedback!

\-Robert, Jerry, and Kazuma

# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR**: Chert provides the infrastructure for teams to send, receive, and automate conversations over iMessage using APIs. We’re already working with B2C startups, customer experience teams, and sales teams to reach end users through trusted and conversational messaging.

**Ask**: If you’re interested in integrating iMessage into your customer conversations, or know someone who is, we’d love to talk: <https://cal.com/team/chert/chert-call> 

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g0BYKdbaNFo>

**The Problem**

iMessage is one of the most trusted and widely used messaging channels in the US. People use it every day to talk with friends, book appointments, coordinate plans, and have conversations. 

But for businesses, iMessage is still very difficult to automate programmatically. 

If a business wants to build on iMessage today, they would have to set up phone lines, manage devices, monitor line health, and connect everything back into their existing tools. 

**Our Solution**

Chert lets teams build agents that can send and receive iMessages directly through our API.

Using iMessage as the communication channel has a few major advantages:

1. **Higher trust and visibility**: while green-bubble SMS and RCS messages get ignored, people open and read blue-bubble iMessages 
2. **More expressive conversations**: Typing indicators, reactions, stickers, attachments, images, and videos make conversations feel more human than standard SMS or email.
3. **Better response loops**: Because iMessage is a channel users already check constantly, teams can create faster and more continuous conversations with prospects, customers, and users. 

We can also integrate natively into calendars (Calendly, [Cal.com](http://Cal.com), etc), CRMs (Hubspot, Salesforce, etc), and internal tools to add logging and structure into conversations.

Our top customers told us they literally cannot train planners fast enough to keep up. The cognitive load burns most planners out within 18 months. We realised the problem wasn't missing features. It was that humans were being asked to do work they physically cannot do reliably. In January 2025, we pivoted to Dayjob: autonomous AI workers that plan and execute operational decisions in real time.

launches.tagline: Run all your operations end to end across every tool in your stack.
launches.body:
Hi, we’re [Lodovico Benvenuti](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lodovico-benvenuti-11678224a/) and [Jan Sahagun](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jan-sahagun-escosa?utm_source=share&utm_campaign=share_via&utm_content=profile&utm_medium=ios_app), and we’re building Trellis, AI agents that run operations for short-term rental property managers.

Our Launch Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zki0_icE3Xw>

### The problem

Short-term rental operations break as companies scale.

As you add listings, coordination explodes across guest messaging, cleaning, maintenance, and homeowners. Work ends up spread across 5 to 10 disconnected tools, duck-taped together by burnt-out teams, constantly firefighting issues, with information inevitably falling through the cracks.

Quality drops, reviews follow, and growth stalls.

This is because managing a property is complex. Let’s say the guest calls about a broken shower. The operator has to identify the reservation in the PMS, search a separate knowledge base for context, collect photos, and create a task in another system.

Then check a workforce tool for availability, reprioritize tasks, dispatch a technician, follow up with the guest, and later log costs, update accounting, and notify the homeowner. All this across 5-10 systems of record.

The core issue is simple: no software has full operation context to control operations end to end.

### What we built

Trellis provides AI agents that run operations across the entire stack.

The agent communicates with guests, dispatches and coordinates cleaners and maintenance, files claims and costs, and follows up until issues are fully resolved.

It connects to PMSs, messaging channels, and internal tools, but more importantly, it maintains full operational context: who the guest is, what property they’re in, what the issue is, what’s already been tried, who is available, what tasks are in progress, and what needs to happen next.

Instead of passing information between tools, the agent owns the entire workflow from first message to resolution and reporting.

When agents take over operations, execution becomes consistent and verifiable. That shifts control of the guest experience from marketplaces back to operators, who can now deliver reliable service at scale, build real brands, and own demand.

### Our background

Before Trellis, Lodo built AI customer service agents for short-term rentals at Conduit (YC W24). He also scaled a property management company to \~$2M revenue and 150+ listings. With trellis we are now running their operations with 1 person.

Jan spent years in the trenches of the STR industry: leading early sales at multiple AI tools for property managers, building an STR tech media platform (STR Tech Report), consulting across the space, attending 20+ industry events, and speaking with thousands of property managers along the way. That journey earned him deep trust and relationships throughout the STR world.

---

If you run a property management company, we’d love to show you Trellis.

launches.body:
Hub provides real-world training data to frontier AI labs and robotics companies. We went to 7-figure revenue agreement on data delivery during the last weeks, working with some of the biggest names in AI and robotics.\
\
**Why now**

The gap between frontier models is closing, and internet-scale data is largely exhausted. The only edge left is real-world data that humans have to produce. Every lab now wins or loses on its edge cases, and edge cases need specific data captured by specific people: data that doesn't exist anywhere online. Whoever can go collect the right data first ships the better model first. Human labor is half of global GDP, and almost none of it has been recorded yet.

**What Hub does**

We capture this data through a global network of humans, across all continents. We route and activate the exact people who fit a lab's brief and deliver in days, not the months it takes to source a generic dataset off the shelf. Because we collect the data ourselves, we can attest its provenance, which you can't do for data you didn't capture. Our ML and QA pipelines then verify and enrich it, so we meet the hardest dataset requirements labs throw at us. The moat isn't the data, it's how fast we can go get it.

**Traction**

From 5-figure to 7-figure in revenue agreement on successful data delivery. We now work with some of the biggest frontier AI labs and robotics companies in the world.

**The ask**

Two asks: —> You're building frontier models or robots and data is your constraint. \
—> You're a top robotics engineer, a PhD whose research touches robotics or egocentric data, or someone with deep experience at a leading robotics lab, we're hiring. \

Today, we provide remote services such as XCode, iOS & Android simulators to enable coding agents running in any sandbox to be able to build and iterate over mobile apps, too.

Replit, Rork, Momentic, Minitap and more agent companies have built mobile development and testing experiences on Limrun platform. Coconote (Quizlet), SorceJobs (W25) and more companies with mobile apps use Limrun with their cloud agents, merging PRs without having to check out the code locally.

launches.title: Limrun - Your cloud agent can build mobile apps now
launches.tagline: Extend your cloud agent with XCode, Android and more
launches.body:
TLDR; We provide remote XCode, iOS & Android Simulators and more to extend cloud agents’ capabilities. Replit, Rork, Momentic AI, x1 and many others built on our cloud and now we open it up to all mobile dev teams so you can use your favorite cloud agent for iOS and Android apps too.

If you have a mobile app, let’s talk! <https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud>

<https://youtu.be/fYkRpsyPLkQ>

---

When code is written by humans, it lives on our laptops and PCs, but that's changing now that teams of agents are writing code alongside us. Today, code written by agents is moving to the cloud: Cursor Cloud, Devin AI, Codex Web, in-house solutions with sandboxes and more.

Now the problem is that all these cloud agents have Linux-based sandboxes as opposed to our laptops that we bought specifically for coding. If you want to use sandboxes for iOS development, you don’t have XCode. If you have an Android app, no emulator that works well. There’s no properly priced GPU option for running Unity either.

Limrun is building a cloud that provides these apps as remote services running in the environments they were designed to while letting your agents use them remotely from your favorite sandbox. All you need is a single skill file to teach your agent how to use our remote services. That’s it. No change of sandbox or agent.

Today, we provide 3 services:

* XCode: With a single CLI call, your code is synced, a build is triggered and your agent gets the logs to iterate.
* iOS Simulator: Your agent can request a simulator to test the app with built-in AX tree or your favorite framework like Appium/Maestro/Detox etc.
* Android Emulator: Similarly, it can request an emulator that will be proxied via an “adb” tunnel so it’s as if locally running.

These are not full sandboxes. We provide the highest level interface so your agent can orchestrate what it needs remotely and we optimize the heck out of the rest; hardware encoders for streaming, warm NVMe caches for building, below 1s boot times, on-demand recording, asset storage and more.

Here is an example flow where Cursor Cloud (or an agent in E2B/Daytona/Docker etc) builds an iOS game in Swift:

* Agent takes the issue from Linear and spins up its sandbox.
* Writes the Swift code and calls the “lim xcode build .” command, streaming logs back.
* Iterates over compiler errors.
* Requests an iOS simulator with “lim ios create” and attaches it.
* Plays the game with batch actions that provide millisecond precision.
* We return the recording that it reviews, sees the bugs, implements the fixes.
* Finally, records a demo video and constructs a preview link to drop on the PR.

It goes from Linear issue to a fully tested PR with demo and preview link that opens in the browser with realtime streaming or you can install to your device over WebUSB without downloading anything.

If you have a mobile app, let’s talk\![ https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud](https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud)

launches.title: Superlog: The self-installing observability tool that fixes your bugs
launches.tagline: A wizard sets up your telemetry every day. An agent investigates incidents and ships mergeable PRs.
launches.body:
Hey YC! We're Nicolò and Arseniy, co-founders of Superlog ([superlog.sh](https://superlog.sh/)).

**TL;DR:** Superlog is the observability tool you're not supposed to open. A wizard scans your repo and instruments it with OpenTelemetry, and re-runs daily to keep your logs, alerts, and dashboards in sync with your code. When something breaks, an agent investigates with full context and posts one mergeable PR per incident into Slack.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AeX3pnHCMHg>

## **The Problem**

Arseniy spent years at Datadog, getting paged during the night to debug production incidents. In our first startups, we tried Sentry, Datadog, Grafana, Dash0, and nothing was good enough. 

* **Setup never ends.** Proper telemetry takes days of manual work and breaks the moment you ship new features. Half the dashboards end up empty or outdated.
* **Alert fatigue is constant.** Sentry floods Slack with duplicates and no context. The Saturday #ops ping is the worst feeling of the week.
* **The bill climbs.** Datadog invoices keep growing while engineers still spend hours configuring dashboards, chasing three AWS metrics that disagree, and copy-pasting stack traces into Claude at 11pm.

## **Our Solution**

**1. Telemetry that sets itself up.** Tell your agent:

```
Run npx skills add superloglabs/skills --all and use the skills to install Superlog in this project
```

This skill instruments your code with native OTel SDKs: proper semantic conventions, service and environment tagging. We cover all failure modes, endpoint performance, usage per tenant, and LLM/upstream cost (by callsite, tenant, and model). We run observability check-ins that keep adding logs, alerts, and dashboards as your code grows.

**2. An agent that investigates and ships PRs.** Errors get prioritised and grouped into incidents. The agent investigates with full context (logs, traces, metrics, recent deploys) and either produces a short tested PR, or posts its findings and pulls in the engineers who own the system (based on docs, prior investigations, Slack threads). One mergeable PR per incident in Slack. Merge it, ignore it, or open it as a Claude Code/Codex session and tweak.

**3. No alert fatigue.** Our custom eval setup makes sure incident summaries in your #ops channel are dense and correct, with severity and impact upfront. Every LLM-enhanced metric ships with a confidence score, so wrong guesses don't get boosted.

The telemetry you get is vendor-neutral: you keep all the OTel logs, metrics, and traces we install, even if you choose to switch providers.

## **Where We're Going**

Every engineering team in the world burns nights and weekends debugging production. We want to delete that loop. Observability should install itself, alert intelligently, and fix what it can.

## **About Us**

* **Nicolò (CEO)** — ex-BCG, math olympiad winner, scaled two startups to millions in ARR, with international enterprise contracts at Bluco (McDonald’s, Volkswagen, Dufry, etc).
* **Arseniy (CTO)** — coding since 12yo, won school olympiads, worked on high-performance data systems at Datadog and built engineering teams from scratch at Bluco.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101239&key=user_uploads/1660276/b630a0c3-d186-4f4c-95c0-6832f7893f47)

We'd love intros to:

* Engineering leaders drowning in Sentry alerts or Datadog bills
* Startups that rolled their own observability and want to throw it away

**Try it:** [superlog.sh](https://superlog.sh/)\

**tldr:** LLMs are built for human-in-the-loop tasks which are highly non-deterministic in nature. We built an AI model for tasks that require high accuracy and verifiable data you can build workflows around.

Interfaze is an AI model built on a new architecture that combines specialized DNN+CNN models with transformers for developer tasks that require deterministic output and high consistency like:

* Vision (OCR, Object detection, GUI) 
* Structured web extraction
* Audio (STT, Diarization, Audio semantics)
* Classification (Image, Text)
* Web search and more

**Try here:** <https://interfaze.ai>

If you’ve ever tried to build a production application using LLMs for tasks like OCR, web scraping, or strict structured data extraction, you already know the pain: hallucinated keys, broken JSON, hidden inaccurate data and massive latency spikes.

You usually end up chaining multiple open source models together just to get a reliable result but face challenges with scaling or being stuck with outdated models from providers like AWS, Azure and GCP.

**The Problem**

Imagine running a store where 4 out of every 10 customers walk up, find the door locked, and leave.

That's how restaurants operate today.

40% of incoming phone calls go unanswered. Emails sit for days. This leads to high-value bookings getting lost: large groups, private events, special occasions, corporate dinners. The bookings that fill slow Tuesday nights and turn an average month into a great one.

Restaurants run on thin margins and one missed call can mean a €2,000 group booking lost to a competitor. Over a year, the average mid-sized restaurant leaves more than $100,000 on the table simply because no one answered in time.

Yet the entire industry still relies on waiters manually handling calls and emails during service. Staff get overwhelmed, emails get buried, and the reservation systems on the market do nothing to fix it. They're glorified calendars.

**The Solution**

Elyra is the AI reservation system for restaurants. Three things, working together:

* **Voice agent:** Answers every phone call. Handles all reservations, modifications, and questions about the menu, dietary requirements, and policies.
* **Email concierge:** Replies to every email instantly, in the restaurant’s tone of voice. Large groups, special requests, and follow-ups handled.
* **Smart table allocation:** Fit more guests in the restaurant. Optimizes table placements in real time while placing guests at the tables that fit them best.

Every call, email, and booking becomes a data point that makes the next visit better, turning first-time guests into regulars.

**Why It Matters**

Here's what our users say:

_"Some regulars thought we hired a new waiter."_

_"We made back a year's cost in two weeks."_

_"Aha, this is what AI should feel like."_

Waiters can finally focus on the guests in front of them instead of a ringing phone. Managers see the bookings they used to lose close automatically. Owners get empty tables filled, margins back, and guests returning.

Elyra is already live across multiple restaurant groups, with new venues seeing record occupancy within weeks of launch.

name: qomplement
long_description:
qomplement is the agentic ERP for retail and logistics companies.

Retail and logistics are the industries with the highest volume of transactions in the world. POs, freight invoices, inventory updates, and shipment confirmations. Every single one still requires a person to process it manually. Their only solution has been hiring more people.

Legacy ERPs were built for humans. qomplement is the agentic ERP that cuts 95% of manual work and handles 100x more transactions with the same headcount. We give procurement and operations teams superpowers: automating purchase order intake, vendor onboarding, item master updates, freight order processing, carrier invoicing, three-way matching, and inventory reconciliation.

Headquartered in San Francisco.
one_liner: The Agentic ERP for supply chain operations

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
Kerim and Andres met in college studying computer science. They became friends trying to track a jaguar near their city. They placed cameras across the mountains, collected more than 15,000 minutes of footage, and quickly realized there was no way to review it all manually. That was their first real problem to solve with AI.

They spent the next few years building AI systems together at their university's research lab.

qomplement started with a phone call. One of the largest oil and gas companies in the world reached out with a problem that seemed almost too simple: they had more than 30 people whose entire job was moving data between systems all day.\
Kerim and Andres flew out immediately. They rented an apartment next to the client's office and spent a full month doing the work themselves. Every purchase order, every ERP update, every vendor portal, every email. They wanted to feel the problem before building anything.

That month became the foundation for qomplement.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
The global economy is roughly $100 trillion. Around $30 trillion of that is the physical economy, the movement of goods across retail, logistics, and supply chains. Yet this entire part of the economy still runs on legacy ERPs, spreadsheets, and large operations teams.

The problem is that these businesses scale by adding headcount. Every new PO, every invoice, every shipment confirmation requires a human to process manually. As headcount grows, human error compounds, processes slow down, and operations become a bottleneck to growth.

We discovered this firsthand. We flew out to one of the largest oil and gas companies in the world, rented an apartment next to their office, and spent a month doing the work ourselves. Every PO, every ERP update, every vendor email. 30 people whose entire job was moving data between systems all day. That month became the foundation for qomplement.

\
**What we're building**

qomplement is the agentic ERP for retail and logistics companies. We replace NetSuite and SAP with an AI-native system where agents handle the full workflow end to end, procurement, inventory, freight, and finance, without human input.\
We land with one high-pain module, prove value in weeks, and expand until we replace the entire ERP. Full migrations take 2 months instead of 12. Same team, 100x more transactions.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
SAP and NetSuite have dominated enterprise software for 30 years. Every company moving physical goods has built entire departments just to keep those systems running.

We're on a mission to end that. A world where no one hates their ERP. Where one person processes what used to take entire departments. Where the system does the work instead of just recording it.

qomplement is the agentic ERP replacing Oracle and NetSuite, built from the ground up for AI agents, not humans.

Antinuous is building autonomous research agents to help people in research, development, discovery, and knowledge work do faster, more accurate research end to end without a human in the loop.

We believe humans should be able to ask a single question, and no matter how simple or complex, agents should look at the question, break it down, research the answer, test new ideas, simulate new environments, and repeat autonomously using as much or little compute as necessary elastically.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
We started as Salesgraph, building agents and workflows for enterprise sales teams.

In enterprise sales, there are four bottlenecks: pipeline, execution, internal, and implementation

Pipeline: how can I do effective outreach to more people.

Execution: how can I boost deal win rate.

Internal: how can I make CPQ, deal-desk, approvals, and negotiations fast.

Implementation: how can I get new customers onboarded smoothly post-sale to avoid clawback.

We were working on execution first, because we solved that internally at Mintlify. After we started tackling pipeline generation, we realized that pipeline generation tools make great primitives for all research.

To build pipeline, you need to create tables of people and companies that you want to sell into. From those tables, you create primitives to dive deeper and do more specialized research to then build automations off of.

What if you want to do deeper research? Learn the industry that your pipeline is built on, map vertical bottlenecks to your solution, go deep on each person to see how they relate to you? Now, you’re going the extra mile to partner on a solution to a business problem with each client, not just features.

But what if you expand this past sales?

What if you’re in manufacturing and want to map supply chain bottlenecks to do better capacity planning?

What if you’re in finance and want to see what data-center construction is doing to grid prices in Texas and Louisiana?

What if you’re in R&D at a biotech and want to run virtual simulations overnight without hooking it up to your lab equipment.

This tool that we built for a niche use case of account research and pipeline generation turns out to be the perfect primitive for all research.

What if we built the best tools for agents to be able to run simulations, experiments, and research in collaboration autonomously.

We can then build the most intuitive way to give humans info from that research in a way they can digest and build a better flywheel.

We quickly went from asking how good can we make sales outreach more effective to asking how many people we can reach who have a question they can’t answer because they don’t have the tools or knowhow.

From building the tools to close revenue more effectively, we realized there's a much larger opportunity to build better tools for agents to answer any question.

As Antinuous, we are building an autonomous research platform where people can investigate their hardest questions and turn what they learn into action.

Hey we’re [Ruhan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ruhanponnada/) and [Ricardo](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ricardonunez-01/) - engineer turned seller, and seller turned engineer.

**Offer:** Get a free [GTM Audit ](https://www.salesgraph.com/gtm-audit)on your company or prospects + if you intro us to a closer, for a meeting booked, get free Lulu merch!\
\
**TL;DR** Salesgraph automates deal context and collateral for enterprise sales teams, so every rep walks into every call prepared and leaves every call with clear next steps. We're a headless UI, starting with a Slack-native experience that integrates with your CRM, calendar, call recordings, docs, blogs, case studies, and research.

<https://youtu.be/fO6c2wIPwIw>
\
**The Problem:**
Sales reps have too much on their plate: back-to-back meetings, Slack messages from prospects, follow-up emails, and coordination with SEs. The best reps balance this. The rest forget to follow up, come to calls unprepared, and lose deals at pricing because they can't value sell.\
\
This gets harder when you're selling a technical product as a non-technical rep. You can't articulate value if you don't fully understand what you're selling, so reps default to features, line items, and discounts.\
\
**The Result:** enterprise deals die in procurement. \
\
When reps walk in without a clear business case, procurement has all the leverage. Deals stall on price, ACV gets discounted away, or the deal dies entirely.

We lived this at Mintlify. Reps looked great on paper, but folded under pressure. The truth is, sales is as much nurturing as it is selling. The best reps act like consultants, not order takers.\
\
**Our Solution:** At an internal Mintlify hackathon, our Head of Sales paired with Ricardo to build an internal tool: a value case generator trained on call recordings, past deals, case studies, ROI calculators, and the MEDDIC framework. The output was a 3-page business case our champions used to sell Mintlify internally — driving higher ACVs and helping us close millions from enterprise logos.

Why can’t we evangelize every GTM team to close deals at higher ACV through encouraging value selling? \
\
We took those learnings to build Salesgraph.

In Slack, reps get proactive context 5 minutes before every call — triggers from background agents, key notes from previous calls, and what to cover next. After every call, they get a DM with strengths, gaps to address, and next steps.

We integrate with major call recorders and ship our own ambient recorder (a sales-focused alternative to Granola), **free for founders and teams under 3**.\
\
**Why this matters for everyone, not just reps:**

* **Sales managers** query deal state directly in Slack, no more reading low-quality opp notes or meaningless health scores
* **SEs and FDEs** stop watching call recordings at 2x speed; they just ask in Slack
* **Customer success** sees what was actually promised vs delivered

\
Every rep should sell like your best rep. \
\
Try us out <https://www.salesgraph.com/>.

launches.body:
**TLDR:** Andco's AI agents run the entire pre-litigation workup for personal injury firms across every channel they use: fax, email, mail, web, SMS, and voice - so they can scale their firm without overhead.

**The first 24 hours of a case, with Andco**

The moment a PI firm signs a new client, a race starts. Police reports need to be pulled, insurers need to be called, medical providers need to be faxed (yes, still faxed). Our agents go off across all channels in parallel: requesting the police report, opening claims with carriers like Geico and Progressive, identifying UM/UIM coverage, engaging adjusters, requesting records and bills from every treating provider, and running follow-up cadences until everything lands. Roughly 8 hours of legal staff work, done before anyone at the firm sits down at their desk.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100597&key=user_uploads/1126674/72f429e1-75ec-45b9-8481-5fac0d0dce5a)

**The Problem**

Personal injury is a $50B+ industry, and firms live or die on pre-litigation workup speed. The problem: every case requires chasing dozens of documents from police departments, insurance carriers, and medical providers — most of whom still run on fax, mail, and phone. Firms have two options today

1. Hire armies of legal staff + paralegals (expensive, high turnover, caps your caseload)
2. Outsource to point-solution retrieval vendors (slow, opaque, expensive per-request)

Legal tech built for this has historically been document and case management systems — great for storing things, terrible at actually doing the work. Meanwhile AI tooling in PI has mostly focused on downstream workflows like medical chronologies and demand drafting, which still depend on someone else getting the case context in first.

**The Solution**

Andco runs the pre-lit workup end-to-end. We're the system that actually does the work of getting the context. Our agents operate across fax, email, mail, web, SMS, and voice - the same channels your legal staff uses, plus a few they can't scale on. We're live with PI firms across the US and are exploring pilots with the world's largest injury law firms.

Early results:

• 8 hours saved in the first 24 hours of a case

• 24+ hours saved between intake and demand

**About Us**

We're a team of repeat founders, ex-lawyers, and builders.

**Ryan Xue (CEO)** — previously founded Layup (W23, exited to Whatfix). Before that: Origin, McKinsey, Google.

**David Lee (CTO)** — 2x founder/CTO. Previously NoxuData and Seek.

launches.title: Arga Labs: Real-world sandboxes for multi-app agents and software
launches.tagline: Production-mirror sandboxes with digital twins of every SaaS integration
launches.body:
**tl;dr:** **become a 100x tester** with Arga by giving your agents staging environments scoped to a change. We spin up twins of your integrations (Slack, Stripe, etc.) and dependencies (DB, Redis), and deploy only the services that were changed. Everything else is routed to prod.

Launch Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OzEk5pYTvak>

**The problem: You’re a 1x tester**

* You don’t have staging :(
* You have staging, but it’s different from prod, and things still break after testing
  * You mock integrations, which can be inaccurate
  * You use real accounts to test integrations, but you hit rate limits, can’t clear states between tests, and can’t test at scale
* You have staging, but your agents can’t automatically test changes so you’re stuck at being a 1x tester despite being a 100x engineer
* You have staging, but it’s difficult to merge concurrent changes without breaking something (for larger teams!)

**Our Solution**

We spin up a temporary staging of your app every time you open a PR. Only the services you change are redeployed; all other services are routed to prod. Your dependencies are deployed as in-memory sidecars, so nothing corrupts prod data. For example, you can configure the tests to read from the prod database and perform all write commands to the sidecar; you can also configure everything to be routed to the sidecar.

We also spin up twins of services your app uses: Stripe, Slack, GSuite, Hubspot, and more, so you don’t hit the real API. This lets you test more thoroughly: **you can catch weird edge cases, simulate failure modes, and run tests in parallel without worrying about rate limits.** All twins are fully compatible with any SDK, expose the same API endpoints, and support webhook events. You can seed any twin in natural language, or select from our pre-set scenarios.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99708&key=user_uploads/3010892/cf335c26-a032-4a1d-bcc1-6c4863946abc)

Demo of Github, Slack, Stripe twins on the Arga app: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3ZPrIdGvPoo>

You or your agent can prompt Arga via web, API, CLI, or MCP to **automatically generate tests for your PR, run them, and stream the results and logs back**. This allows them to know what was tested, what broke, and which calls/functions caused the failure. They can use this information to go back and fix the code, so you’ll have a fully-tested and passing PR before you look at it.

Validation report:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99708&key=user_uploads/3010892/81258740-df00-46e1-9ba9-b2bbfd7a4572)

Claude Code using arga CLI to read logs & test results:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99708&key=user_uploads/3202471/286496d9-28f2-4c01-a186-35235ed55189)

**Our ask**

Try us out! We’re live at [www.argalabs.com](http://www.argalabs.com) and you can get access to limited features for free. \
If you like our stuff, book a demo here (<https://cal.com/phillip-li/30min>).\
If you know any teams that struggle with testing and use lots of external integrations, send them our way.

**The Team**

Akira and Phillip met each other in first-year calculus at UBC. At the time, Akira was 14 and Phillip was studying neuroscience to pursue research in human biology. Within a year of pivoting to CS, Phillip built a dev tool at Amazon that saved 10 weeks / year of engineering hours as an intern. While interning at Stripe, Akira realized that a high-fidelity “staging” was the key to unlocking dev productivity and was surprised that most companies don’t have proper staging that actually mirrored prod. Now they’re solving that problem.

launches.tagline: AI voice agents for enterprise contact centers running on legacy phone infrastructure
launches.body:
Hey YC,

We are Haithem and Chehir - co-founders of  [Callab AI](https://callab.ai/). 

**The problem**

The global call center industry is worth $400B, and about 58% of it still runs on on-prem PBX infrastructure like Cisco UCM, Mitel, and FreeSWITCH. These systems have been in place for 20 years, with millions invested in deploying and maintaining them. They work, and they're not going anywhere.

AI voice agents have been built on top of cloud telephony providers, which means every solution on the market today requires the customer to already be on cloud phone systems. If you're running on-prem, you're locked out. The only option is a full migration to cloud, which typically takes 12 to 18 months, costs a fortune, and frequently fails. Meanwhile, these same companies are dealing with 30 to 40% agent attrition rates, rising labor costs, and customers who won't tolerate hold times. They want automation but they simply can't access it.

That's a massive segment of a $400B market sitting there with no solution available to them.

**What we built**

Callab AI is a cloud-based AI voice platform that connects directly to on-prem PBX systems via SIP trunk integration. The phone system stays exactly where it is, calls get routed to our AI agents, handled, and returned. No rip-and-replace, no migration, and we go live in one week.

We automate up to 70% of inbound call volume across use cases like call routing, appointment scheduling, order status, and customer inquiries. The hard part is the integration layer itself, which requires going deep into legacy telecom infrastructure that most teams don't want to touch. We built it to work with any telephony stack, and that's what makes this possible.

We're YC P25 and currently expanding into the US, focused on hospitality, logistics, retail chains, and property management. Healthcare and financial services are on the roadmap once we complete HIPAA compliance.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101754&key=user_uploads/1938837/5d95733e-2ac9-45b4-8f2b-5ef8a8a3b8ca)

**How we got here**

We didn't set out to become the on-prem PBX company. We started building AI voice agents in the Middle East and Africa, where cloud telephony providers don't operate, SIP trunks are state-regulated, and every contact center runs legacy infrastructure. We had no choice but to build our integration layer to work directly with whatever phone system was already on the ground. After plugging into old telecom stacks, we realized the problem we solved out of necessity in MEA is the exact same problem sitting untouched in the US. The constraint that shaped our product in a harder market turned out to be a global advantage.

**How you can help**

If you know anyone at a company running a legacy phone system or on-prem contact center, we'd love an intro. Hotels, restaurant groups, logistics operators, large retail, or property management are all ideal. Also happy to connect with anyone who's worked with managed service providers, value-added resellers, or sold into enterprise telecom IT. Drop me a note.

Hey everyone 🙂

We’re [Tim](https://www.linkedin.com/in/timzinkl/) and [Matthias](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthias-wolf/), co-founders of Pairio

**TL:DR:**

**Machine downtime in manufacturing is expensive. Pairio helps technicians and operators resolve faults faster with voice AI.**

4 plants in Germany are already using Pairio to reduce equipment downtime.

**Ask:** Can you introduce us to plant and maintenance managers at US manufacturing firms? Contact us at [tim.zinkl@pairio.com](mailto:tim.zinkl@pairio.com)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kmUBOkAU33M>

**The Problem**

Unplanned equipment downtime costs global industries over $1.4 trillion every year – and the root cause isn't broken machines. It's broken knowledge transfer.

* When a machine fails, resolution speed depends almost entirely on whether the one guy who's seen this before is working that day
* Valuable technical clues are buried somewhere across 400 pages of OEM manuals or locked in outdated software
* After spending 6 hours getting the line back up, the last thing a technician does is sit down and write a detailed fault report to institutionalize their knowledge

With the average technician in the US now 50 years old, knowledge is literally walking out the door, further compounding the problem for years to come.

**Our Solution**

We have shown at 4 factories in Germany that removing these barriers can lead to higher equipment uptime – and the effect compounds with every fault processed with Pairio.

With our voice-first approach we empower technicians and operators to:

* Simply ask and instantly receive any available technical clue
* Speak and let Pairio structure their learnings into reusable know-how
* Use photos and videos to capture even more contextual knowledge

By focusing on capturing the reality on the shop floor we are building the foundation for agentic workflows that eliminate off the wrench time and optimize equipment uptime.

launches.tagline: The Fastest Way to Generate Whiteboard Explainer Videos from a Single Prompt or Documents
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Simi is the fastest, easiest, and most cost-effective way to create whiteboard explainer videos. You give it a prompt or a document. It writes the script, draws the illustrations, animates them, adds narration, and hands you a finished video in seconds. Anything from a one minute short to a full hour, in one shot, in 80+ languages. Built by Lamina Labs (YC P26). Use it through the app or the API for training, onboarding, product walkthroughs, sales, marketing, and education at <https://laminalabs.ai>.

Here is an explainer video about Lamina Labs: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RLuOCdamcHE>

## Why we built this

AI video right now is built to look like a movie, not to explain something.

But most of the video people actually need at work is the boring kind. A training module. An onboarding flow. A walkthrough of the feature you shipped last week. And making one of those is absurdly slow. You either pay an agency thousands of dollars and wait weeks, or you sit in a template editor dragging boxes around for an afternoon and it still looks like you dragged boxes around.

That is fine if you need one video. It falls apart the moment you need a hundred. A course. Every feature documented. Onboarding in every language your customers speak. Anyone who has priced that out knows the math does not work.

## How it works

You type what you want. Simi writes the script, draws and animates it, and gives you a properly narrated video in seconds.

That is the whole thing. No storyboard, no timeline, no boxes to drag. Type "explain how photosynthesis works," or hand it a long compliance doc, and you get a finished video, not a draft. And it does not choke on length. One minute to a full hour, generated in a single shot.

If your team makes videos, you should be using this.

## What people make with it

Training and onboarding videos from the docs you already have. Product walkthroughs, one per feature, updated as fast as the product changes. Sales and marketing explainers, in every market you sell into. Course and lecture videos in the Khan Academy style. Faceless YouTube channels and localized social video at volume. Agencies run it through the API to produce explainer videos for their clients.

## What makes it different

An agency gives you a video in weeks for thousands of dollars. Simi gives you the same video in seconds for a fraction of that. That is the whole pitch, and it is enough.

A few things worth knowing beyond speed. It generates anything from a minute to an hour in one shot. It speaks 80+ languages, so you write once and localize everywhere. And it is built to plug in. Use the app, call the API from your own product, or run it inside agent frameworks like OpenClaw and Nous Research's Hermes.

## Who we are

We are Sudip and Kartikesh, the founders of Lamina Labs, and Simi is the first thing we have built. We are both from Nepal. We met at MIT and started building together there. We are the first Nepalese founding team to go through YC.

Simi is named after Simikot, the Himalayan village where Sudip grew up. We started with education because that is where this problem hurt us personally. But it is everywhere. Any time someone needs to turn an idea into a clear picture, that is us.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104668&key=user_uploads/2592448/ddd4246e-1dae-4302-8e33-7c51d0264d6b)

## Our asks

If your team spends real money or real time making explainer, training, or onboarding videos, talk to us: [founder@laminalabs.ai](mailto:founder@laminalabs.ai)

We would love intros to L&D leaders, to agencies making video at volume, and to founders who want video generation inside their own product through the API.

And if you just want a video explaining your own startup, **try it:** <https://app.laminalabs.ai> \
