# **BentoLabs AI: the monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents**

**TL;DR**: BentoLabs AI is the monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents. We detect when agents silently fail or drift from the user's goal, system prompt, or tool contracts, show affected users and root cause, and suggest the prompt, skill, or harness fix. Run 101 is measurably better than run 1.

<https://youtu.be/nu6Oir3OGSM>\
\
Hello everyone, we're Abhinav and Kaushik, co-founders of BentoLabs AI.

After spending two years at Emergent (YC S24), building and operating production coding agents used by 5M+ users, helping scale from 0 to $100M ARR and topping SWE-Bench twice. We realised as more teams deploy agents, keeping them reliable, observable, debuggable and continuously improving in production becomes mission-critical. Most teams don't have a system for it. They have engineers.

### **The Problem:**

Most production agents fail silently. You have 10,000 traces a day and zero visibility into reasoning drift until a support ticket pops up. That's the easier half! The harder problem is that nothing your agent figures out on one run carries into the next. An agent might solve a complex edge case on run 47, but because nothing carries forward, it burns your budget rediscovering the same fix on run 48.

This makes production teams spend hours reading logs in one tab just to manually patch prompts in another, on a loop that never closes.

### **The Solution:**

**BentoLabs AI** The monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents.

**Monitoring:** BentoLabs finds every failure instance across your production traces, classifies it, and tracks it before the support ticket pops up.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/55f2be9c-2363-4f4d-b3cc-98e803c9dbe6)

**Learning:** BentoLabs captures what your agent figures out on every run and makes sure it carries into the next one. Recurring failures get fixed once and stay fixed. Hard-won solutions become reusable. Run 101 starts from everything runs 1 through 100 learned, not from zero.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/84d43836-11f5-4684-9465-8b02ab715a52)

### **The Proof:**

**Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Internal Run):** we validated our recursive learning engine on Terminal-Bench 2.0, one of the most demanding agentic-shell benchmarks in the field today. Where the official Claude Sonnet 4.5 baseline scores 42.2% pass@1. Our agent scored 52.4%, with the same agent, same model, same budget.A +10.2 percentage-point lift, statistically significant (p < 0.05), with 13 tasks showing wins ≥ +20 pp and only 3 showing losses ([Deep Dive](https://bentolabs.ai/blog/tb2-recursive-learning-lift))

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/016f2897-dcb5-4137-a658-98e0e7ccf525)

\
**ARC-AGI-3 (Internal Run):** To see our engine in action, we took on ARC-AGI-3 (25 interactive puzzle games, the hardest agent benchmark we could find). While frontier models score 0.2–0.3% out of the box, 3 games the agent had never solved across \~30 prior runs were cracked for the first time. ([Deep Dive](https://bentolabs.ai/blog/self-learning-ai-agents-arc-agi))

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/3c51a5a5-c620-41f6-9ae0-23d9f3dda903)

**Why we're building BentoLabs**

We were the engineers who were the fix for the last 2 years at Emergent, where we spent thousands of hours staring at traces, and watching teams burn hours of their best engineers' time on patching prompts, correcting tool definitions and experimenting with different skills, hoping something will stick. We are building [BentoLabs AI](https://bentolabs.ai/) to move past this repetitive cycle.

We're already working with teams at unicorn scale. Every conversation with a team running agents in production confirms the same thing: the problem is universal. BentoLabs gives them the operational leverage to scale their agent ecosystems without scaling human firefighting alongside them.

If your engineers are doing the logs-and-patches rotation or your agents keep hitting the same failures, let's have a [chat.](https://cal.com/team/bentolabs-ai/platform-demo?overlayCalendar=true) Or Email: [abhinav@bentolabs.ai](mailto:abhinav@bentolabs.ai)/ [kaushik@bentolabs.ai](mailto:kaushik@bentolabs.ai)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/712dcafd-cfe4-42ab-8af8-30aadcbf545d)

launches.body:
Enterprise software takes months to go live after the sale. Imagine paying for an app on the app store but not being able to use it for 6 months. [Lab0](https://lab0.ai/) solves exactly this.

We’re building an AI FDE that automates entire post-sales delivery for software companies - all from discovery, solution design, config, to testing and go-live. We’re currently working with Adobe and a couple of system integrators.

The future of enterprise software is self-serve, where enterprises buy a product, and it gets configured by agents.

[Lab0](https://www.linkedin.com/company/lab0-hq/) is the AI FDE making that real: 6 months → 10 days.

<https://youtu.be/UDrqfnYWlLI>

# **The problem**

If you've sold to an enterprise, you know this already.

A $200K contract lands. Hand off to post-sales. On a deeper technical discovery of your client’s processes, you realize you need a lot of custom changes to serve them.

That's the hidden tax on every enterprise sale, 3 months of bespoke FDE / Solution Architect’s work, rebuilt from scratch for every customer. That’s 3 months of lost value for the customer.

Either you wait months to start billing, or somehow show enough ROI in the remaining duration of the contract to get a renewal.

# **What we built**

[Lab0](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/lab0) is the AI FDE for your (AI?) B2B SaaS. It joins discovery calls and tells you what to ask, generates handoffs, design documents and test plans. It even configures the product, writes custom integrations and tests all the workflows before signing off.

_Six months of services work, done in days._

# **Who we are**

[Onkar Borade](https://www.linkedin.com/in/onkar-borade/) , CS grad from IIT Bombay, saw the problem from inside Oracle, where the implementation team was bigger than the dev team.

[Lakshya Gupta](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lakshya-gupta-0030771ba/) , also CS from IIT Bombay, was an early engineer at Emergent Labs where he scaled the Agent platform from 0 to $100M in ARR with over 5M users.

[Sujay Srivastava](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sujaysriv/) , quantum computing grad from IIT Madras, was building an AI startup for BFSI, where every rollout felt like its own custom project.

We've sat on every side of an enterprise deployment, and [Lab0](https://www.linkedin.com/company/lab0-hq/) is the software we wished we'd had on every one of those projects.

# **Our ask**

**1. Are you a company selling to enterprises where implementation is eating your team's time?** We'll take one of your hardest customer deployments and run it end-to-end; you'll see the value firsthand.

**2. Intros to Professional Services leaders / Customer Success / Solutions Architects** at enterprise software companies with 20+ person implementation teams. If you've seen this pain from a previous job - even from across the aisle in a product or engineering role, a warm intro goes a long way.

Drop an email at [founders@lab0.ai](https://mail.google.com/mail/?view=cm&fs=1&to=founders@lab0.ai)\
or\
Book a call at [Lab0-Calendly_Link](https://calendly.com/d/ctzx-ndw-n8b/office-hours-with-lab0)

Gojiberry is building the AI GTM team for B2B companies.

We start with outbound: Gojiberry finds buyers showing intent, enriches them, reaches out, follows up, handles replies, and books qualified meetings.

Companies use Gojiberry to replace the old way of doing outbound: buying tools, hiring SDRs & agencies, testing lists, writing messages, and guessing what works. Gojiberry turns it into one AI team that finds buyers and books meetings.

Every campaign makes Gojiberry smarter. It learns which buyers convert, which signals matter, which messages get replies, and which actions create revenue. Over time, Gojiberry uses what works across similar companies and industries to help every new customer get better results from day one.

Long term, Gojiberry will become the system that finds every revenue opportunity and acts on it: outbound leads, website visitors, inbound leads, old CRM leads, replies, meetings, CRM updates, new campaign ideas, and account expansion.

The goal is to make every B2B company able to run a high-performing GTM team without hiring one.

We grew from $0 to $2.5M ARR in 10 months, are growing 30% MoM, profitable, and used by 2,000+ customers.

Customers get 2-5x more positive replies than traditional outbound.

That’s exactly where our GTM Brain comes in to fix this.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
Max led process optimization at Porsche. David built data pipelines in finance. Leon built AI automations at consultancies. They all noticed critical knowledge is trapped inside people's heads and never reaches the people who need it.

The team then felt inspired to work on the problem after a tour to Stockholms fastest scaling startups organized by Max, where all three decided to quit their jobs and start a company.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Every company already has the answers to most of the questions leadership is asking.

The problem: those answers are scattered across hundreds of people, and there's never been a practical way to ask every single employee.

So leaders make crucial decisions with partial information or spend months and millions on external consultants to retrieve what the org already knows.

**What we're building**

Ontora is an AI agent that has a real conversation with every employee in your company within hours.

It learns, follows up, and surfaces what people actually do and where they get stuck.

We deliver two things: a synthesized answer to the specific question leadership couldn't crack in their last business review (themed insights, process maps, automation roadmap with ROI), and a continuously refreshed operational context that humans and AI agents can both reason over.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Answers in hours instead of months. We imagine truly intelligence native companies that unlock the last proprietary data source left in the enterprise: operational knowledge living in your employees heads.

Enabling cost reduction, post-merger integration, and AI transformation… within hours and at a fraction of the cost of traditional consulting.

# **One month ago we launched Ontora. Here's what happened**

### Our progress

\- 5 enterprise customers as design partners (many more to come ;)\
\- 150+ inbound demo calls — we didn't do outbound, they came to us\
\- $700K raised before officially opening our round\
\- 80+ inbound VC calls already lined up for our fundraise

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vI8shNqqmRE>

And we released our product live with our first customers !

**1. Why companies are banging down our door:**

Every company we talk to has the same story: they bought Claude licenses for their teams but merely use it to rewrite emails. The AI transformation stalled because nobody mapped what to actually automate.

That's the real bottleneck. Not code. Context.

A 800-person European media agency flew to San Francisco to meet us after realizing they'd need 4-5 months and a team of consultants just to understand their own operations. With Ontora, they can map their entire company in days.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102685&key=user_uploads/1178744/2bd9ca28-443a-46ef-af8c-ad76dd2d6a9f)

**2. What Ontora does for your company:**

Ontora deploys AI agents that interview every employee in your company -- not once, but continuously -- to map out how work actually gets done. We turn that into a living context layer that your AI agents can act on.

What used to take a consulting firm 4 months and 50-100 manual interviews, Ontora does in days. And because interviews run continuously, your context layer never goes stale. Your organization keeps learning about itself.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102685&key=user_uploads/1178744/56b07749-ae1e-4244-9064-d1dd122baecc)

Here's how it works:

1. **Deploy** -- Ontora's AI agents reach out to employees across your org through async interviews, meeting them where they work
2. **Map** -- Every interview extracts processes, decision rules, tools used, handoffs, and tribal knowledge into structured operational maps
3. **Act** -- The living context layer feeds directly into your AI agents and automations so they have the real-world context they need to perform

<https://youtu.be/Culdmbt9uPE>

**3. Who's already using Ontora:**

* **A PE firm in San Francisco** -- deploying Ontora across portfolio companies to drive operational efficiency at speed no consulting firm can match
* **A major European media agency (800+ employees)** -- building their corporate memory to manage enterprise customers like Volkswagen and Bosch
* **A 1,000-person European roll-up** -- mapping what their remote workforce actually does day-to-day to build a concrete AI automation roadmap
* **A US facilities maintenance marketplace** -- extracting the proposal rules and customer preferences locked in their sales team's heads to build the context layer for their AI automations

**4. We want to hear from you:**

* If your mid-market company (200-2,000 employees) is planning AI transformation...
* If your PE/VC firm wants to drive efficiency across portfolio companies...
* If your company spent 6 figures on consultants to map processes...

...we need to talk.

launches.title: Oddpool: The institutional data layer for prediction markets
launches.tagline: Bringing the power of prediction markets to Wall St
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're **Avi** and **Ritesh** — co-founders of **Oddpool**.

**TL;DR**

Oddpool helps quant and institutional desks harness the power of prediction markets. We make it easy to access, search, and analyze every venue from one place with the depth and history serious desks need.

**Ask:**  If you're a quant fund, prop shop, market maker, or hedge fund using prediction markets data (or thinking about it), we'd love to talk. Reach us at [founders@oddpool.com](mailto:founders@oddpool.com)

<https://youtu.be/dSG7gVU1M7w>

**The Problem**

Data is the lifeblood of modern finance. Every desk, every strategy, every edge starts with it.

Yet prediction markets, one of the fastest-growing asset classes in the world, still lack the tooling that makes every other asset class easy for desks to adopt, leaving anyone trying to use this data stuck with three major pains:

1. Fragmentation across venues with no shared symbology
2. No tick-level history to backtest against
3. Weeks spent normalizing data instead of generating signals

These compound the moment real money tries to enter, leaving a glaring problem to be solved.

**Our Solution**

Oddpool provides a frictionless experience to start pulling, backtesting, and building on prediction market data from day one.

We focus on two core capabilities:

1. Universal symbology that maps every market across every venue to one canonical identifier. 

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101199&key=user_uploads/1189439/52942888-443a-4724-8f78-a11827fcee9f)

2. Tick-level history with full orderbook depth, every trade, and every delta, ready to backtest against 

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101199&key=user_uploads/1189439/3a45c427-444d-42fc-a3c7-06479f623cf2)


Our mission is to drive the institutional adoption of prediction markets, so the world's most accurate signals can finally be used by the desks that move it.

👉 If you resonate, please reach out to us here: [founders@oddpool.com](mailto:founders@oddpool.com)

❤️ Check out our website: <https://www.oddpool.com>

launches.tagline: Sidekick gives frontline workers an AI assistant they can text, with no app, login, or training.
launches.body:
**Hey everyone 👋**

I'm Justin, founder of Sidekick.

**TL;DR** Sidekick is an AI assistant that frontline manufacturing workers use over text message. They text a number and it answers from the company's own documents, creates and routes work orders, and syncs with the software the company already uses. No app, no login, no training. I built Sidekick for my dad's manufacturing shop. It’s now live at facilities across the globe.

**_Ask:_** Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility? I'd love an intro! Email [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick).

Check out our launch video:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yxwq5ZAojXg>

## ❌ The Problem

I grew up in my dad's manufacturing plants and spent summers working on the factory floor at EDS Manufacturing.

Here's what I watched happen repeatedly. A machine goes down, everyone's waiting, and the person who can help is in a meeting or on another line. Half the time the answer already existed. Nobody could get to it.

Why it keeps happening:

* **No computer access.** Nobody on that floor has a company login or an email address, so none of the plant's software reaches them.
* **The answers are scattered.** An SOP in a binder, a manual on a shared drive few have permissions to, a safety procedure someone printed and taped to a wall in 2019.
* **The best answers were never written down.** Thirty years of tribal knowledge lives in one guy's head, and when he retires it leaves with him.
* **So the same questions get asked over and over.** Shift after shift, and every one of them costs somebody their afternoon.

There are 239,000 manufacturing plants in the US, and only 29% of the people working in them have advanced digital skills. Any tool that requires a download, a login, and training makes adoption difficult.

## ✅ Our Solution

Workers text the Sidekick phone number. Problems, photos, voice memos, in any language. No app to download, no account to create, nothing to learn. Every worker on the floor already knows how to send a text, which is why adoption isn't a fight.

* **Answers from your own documents.** SOPs, manuals, safety procedures, tribal knowledge. Sidekick responds in the worker's language, in seconds.
* **Creates and routes the work order.** The issue gets logged and sent to the right person, without anyone needing a laptop.
* **Syncs with the software you already run.** Sidekick pulls from and writes to your existing systems instead of replacing them, and integrates directly through PLC and SCADA systems so the floor and the software finally see the same thing.
* **Captures tribal knowledge.** Every exchange builds a searchable knowledge base the company owns, so the know-how stays when the veteran leaves.

Here's a full walkthrough:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a5zBRSXi-90>

## 👤 The Team

I'm Justin, founder and CEO. I'm the third generation in a manufacturing family, and I've been around plant floors since I was a kid. I studied Computer Science at the University of Pennsylvania, worked in finance at Arm, and left both to build Sidekick after watching the same problem play out on every floor I'd been on.

## 🙏 Our Ask

If you answer "yes" to any of these, I'd love your help:

* **Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility?** Even a name and a "you two should talk" goes a long way.
* **Have you sold software into manufacturing?** I'd love to hear what actually worked and what didn't.

Contact me at [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo here**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick)**.**

launches.body:
Hi there! I’m Gustav, and together with Tine and Marc we’re building AI infrastructure that automates compliance for global retailers.

If you sell physical products across markets, compliance is brutal.

Every country has different requirements. Documentation is fragmented. Regulations change constantly. Most teams still manage it in spreadsheets, consultants, and shared drives. And every product launch becomes a fire drill.

Our users are:

\- Enterprise retailers with thousands of SKUs

\- Compliance, quality, and sourcing teams

\- Companies launching across multiple EU and international markets

They don’t want to just be compliant. They want to ship products fast and never think about compliance again.

**How we got here**

Just one month after Tine and I met back in May 2024, we made a deal with Flying Tiger Copenhagen (a 1,000+ store global retail chain, similar to a European Five Below) and forward deployed ourselves in their offices, working directly with their compliance, packaging, and sourcing teams for over a year.

We had no idea how much manual work we were about to witness.

Regulations are dynamic. Products change. Data is messy. Requirements depend on category, market, material, packaging, claims, and more. Most existing tools treat compliance like static storage.

So we built an AI-native system that:

\- Maps products to relevant regulatory requirements across markets

\- Transforms messy product data into structured, audit-ready compliance records

\- Automatically generates legally required outputs — including translations, warnings, labels, risk assessments, declarations, and technical documentation

\- Propagates updates when regulations or products change, so documentation stays compliant without manual rework

Today we manage 100k+ products, work with large retailers across Europe, and are growing \~45% MoM

If you know large retailers selling across markets, tell them they can save millions in yearly compliance costs - while launching more products in more markets, faster.

And if you’re building or operating in retail, import/export, or compliance infrastructure, we’d love to compare notes!

Demo: [**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4omoq7tcU88**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4omoq7tcU88)

Hey YC!! Faiz and Saheed here from Minicor ([minicor.com](http://minicor.com))

**TLDR;** AI companies selling into healthcare, automotive, financial services, and logistics can't go live because their customers run on legacy desktop software with no APIs. <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nzH4ekkaA2c>

**The problem**

Our customers selling into legacy industries can't go live because the systems of record their customers use (EHRs, ERPs, DMS) are Windows desktop apps with no APIs. The only way to read / write is through UI automations, but desktop RPA at scale breaks constantly. Even small error rates become hundreds of failures a day, and every one needs manual intervention.

They're signing customers but don't have capacity to integrate because they're too busy fighting fires with existing RPAs; or their prospects are blocked because they need "proof" they can write back to their systems, and spinning up a desktop automation POC takes too long.

**In production**

We're live right now processing thousands of workflows a week across healthcare EHRs and other legacy systems. Our agents write AI-generated data into desktop apps in real-time. We went live with a customer in 3 weeks post POC.

**How it works**

1. Install our Desktop Client on the machines running the legacy software.
2. Speak the automation into existence - either through your favourite coding agent via our MCP, or to us directly. You get an API endpoint to trigger it.
3. Minicor handles everything after that. Only pay when the data gets in

launches.body:
It has never been quicker to build. Most companies are putting out new features or bug fixes daily. But do your users actually know what you shipped today?

\
Building has never been faster, but telling people about it hasn't kept up. Marketing what you shipped is slower than shipping it: record the demo, fumble fifteen takes, design the post, edit the video, get it on-brand, publish. An afternoon gone for twenty seconds of footage. So most teams skip it, and their best work ships to silence.

tday.com closes that gap. Connect your GitHub repo or point us at your site, and every release turns into a complete launch package: a demo video that shows how the feature works, a feature showcase built to sell it, and on-brand graphics for every placement, published to social automatically.

There are two ways in, and both produce both outputs. Connect your repo and tday spins up an isolated sandbox, captures the exact change in each pull request before it even merges, and posts the assets back to the PR to review or auto-publish. Or hand us a demo account set up exactly how you want to be marketed, pick the feature, and tday signs in, drives the real flow, and records it.

What makes it different is that everything is grounded in your real product and brand. tday already knows your colors, fonts, and voice, so output is on-brand every time, and you can tweak any line, scene, or image from the platform without re-recording the source. Ship a new version and the demo re-records itself: it captures a capability, not a one-off moment.

The creative we generate is already running at up to 8.3% CTR in early paid tests, several times the typical benchmark. Paid campaigns inside tday are next, and from there, marketing that scales at the speed you ship: hundreds of thousands of on-brand, hyper-targeted assets, generated and published automatically.

launches.body:
### Credentials

We’ve spent years working together building large scale distributed systems that run on hundreds of thousands of machines and serve billions of users. **Every time you leverage your network for a warm intro on LinkedIn, you use three databases that we’ve built: [Venice](https://venicedb.org/),[ Liquid](https://www.linkedin.com/blog/engineering/graph-systems/liquid-the-soul-of-a-new-graph-database-part-1), and[ Espresso](https://engineering.linkedin.com/teams/data/data-infrastructure/storage-infra/espresso).**

After LinkedIn, **we were tech-leads of [Ray](https://github.com/ray-project/ray)**, the leading open-source compute platform used by companies such as xAI, Cursor, Bridgewater, P72, Man Group, Two Sigma, and others. Ray has [\~12M](https://pypistats.org/packages/ray) weekly downloads and is part of the PyTorch Foundation.

### Product

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C6tl8Fr8t2I>

We’re building large scale high performance computing (HPC) clusters for **quantitative trading firms** to run **parallel simulation workloads such as backtesting.** 

The scale we’re targeting is

* 100 to 50,000 nodes of mixed hardware (CPUs and GPUs) on hyperscalers and neoclouds.
* up to 5,000,000 parallel tasks.
* spot instances for cheaper compute across multiple availability zones, hyperscalers, and neoclouds.
* < 50ms overhead for task dispatch and scheduling.
* run the compute in your cloud or on-prem environment to keep your alpha secure.

Our goal is to **make testing trading strategies fast, cheap, and reliable.** 

### Vision

We know that existing solutions do not handle this scale, do not have first-class support for spot-instances, and will not match our low-latency and high throughput performance. 

Our technology generalizes to other large-scale compute workloads such as

1. **post-training and reinforcement learning (RL)** for frontier and applied AI labs
2. **massively parallel robotics simulation and sim-to-real training** for robot foundation model teams
3. **virtual screening and molecular dynamics** for techbio and pharma R&D
4. **scientific simulation** (CFD, climate, seismic, FEA) for HPC teams looking to move beyond MPI and SLURM.

### Ask

Reach out if you

1. Are running simulation workloads that require lots of computation at a quant trading firm.
2. If you need HPC for a different use-case.
3. Want to grab a beer and talk about distributed systems or HPC.

Cheers!

Ibrahim and Zac

Hey everyone, we’re [Theodore](https://www.linkedin.com/in/theodore-otzenberger-895345131/) and [Louis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/louis-scremin/) - Co-Founders of [Armature](https://armature.tech/) 👋

### TL;DR

**Armature helps companies monitor, analyze, and optimize how AI agents experience their products.**

* We discover your product through MCP and CLI, **run the real workflows your customers’ AI agents do** and let you finally see your customers’ agents thinking **traces**.
* We provide analytics, run **benchmarks**, and turn this into **concrete actions** to improve your MCP and CLI.
* This is only the beginning: we are reinventing the building blocks of the ~~User~~ **Agent Experience**.

**_The Ask:_** _If you are building a product that is increasingly used by AI agents or if you want to ensure agents can use your product but don’t know where to start, we’d love to hear about your challenges! You can also try our product self-serve **for free** directly at [armature.tech](http://armature.tech)._

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Gtc5RzGxJ0>

### ❌ The Problem: The Missing Agent Experience (AX)

We have 30 years of tooling to optimize User Experience (UX), from session replays and funnel analytics to live support chat. But as products are increasingly operated by **AI agents** rather than humans, we lack the equivalent tooling for **Agent Experience (AX)**.

Right now, companies have **zero visibility** into how each agent (Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenClaw, etc.) interacts with their products. And when a bad AX causes an agent to fail silently, the end-user simply churns.

But it goes deeper. As agents become the primary users, the fundamental mechanics of software products simply stop working. Because if a human isn’t looking at the screen:

* _How do you upsell a premium feature to an AI?_
* _How do you build brand loyalty with a user that doesn’t feel emotions?_
* _How do you offer customer support when an agent fails?_

We are building Armature to solve these exact problems and so many more questions related to this shift!

### 💡 Our Solution: Armature

Armature helps companies monitor, analyze, and optimize how AI agents experience their products.

**What we do today:**

* **Automated testing:** We run complex sessions against your MCPs/CLIs across all major harnesses and models to catch broken workflows before your users do.
* **AX analytics & benchmarking:** No more black boxes. We trace agent sessions to show you exactly what the model "thought", what context it missed, and why it failed. We measure your AX against competitors to ensure you remain the preferred platform for agents to use.
* **Auto-remediation:** Our MCP lets your internal coding agents plug into Armature to autonomously fix your product's AX based on our run data.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101594&key=user_uploads/3408440/5642c5dd-a3b1-46e1-865d-a0425ceba1d5)

**Our vision for tomorrow:**

Reaching full understanding of how agents use your product and how you can improve it is only step one. 

The next step is to provide the **foundational infrastructure for the Agent Experience**, powering agent-native revenue, lifecycle marketing, and customer support for the next generation of software.

### 🙏 Our Ask: If you’re building apps for agents, let’s talk!

1. **Audit your MCP or CLI:** If you are building for agents, you can start by running your first audit & benchmark on [**armature.tech**](http://armature.tech) **for free** to see how they actually experience your app.
2. **Let’s chat:** If you are facing challenges to make your app usable by agents or optimize the agent experience, please reach out to [**founders@armature.tech**](mailto:founders@armature.tech). We’d love to discuss and help you with this!

### 👬 The Team: why we are working on this

Before founding Armature, Louis scaled **AI agents at Joko, a 6M user consumer app**. Theo was a **FDE at Palantir** and then built petabytes-scale **observability** from scratch as a Founding Engineer at Tsuga, a Datadog spin-off.

**Blindly shipping a self-tested MCP to 6M of edge cases drove us crazy so we decided to build the solution.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101594&key=user_uploads/3408440/bdb32e65-c048-467e-aa62-0e67c8f1fff7)

Hey everyone 👋

We're[ ](https://claude.ai/cowork/LINKEDIN)Nikolas and Lukas, co-founders of Walter. 

### **TL;DR**

Walter is an AI employee for the manufacturing back office. Instead of building yet another integration, we gave Walter a login. He signs into SAP, Microsoft Dynamics 365, or Oracle the way a new hire would, works out of Teams and email like the rest of the team, and takes over the manual work no one wanted: entering purchase orders, ordering from suppliers, catching pricing errors before they ship. A purchase order that used to take 15 minutes now takes a few seconds.

### **The Team**

* Nikolas Keller grew up across four countries, started to cook in French, Italian and German fine dining kitchens at 18, then flew to San Francisco with a duffel bag and talked his way into a manufacturing AI startup backed by Neo & GC.
* Lukas Postulka paid for TU Munich by living in a monastery in exchange for cleaning. Got a job at  PwC by mailing them a portfolio they never asked for. Landed a job as quant trader by scoring first on technical trial.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102405&key=user_uploads/3097279/555d91df-f392-4137-ae2a-d5816f70df7b)

### **The Problem**

We talked to more than 100 manufacturers and heard the same story every time. For thirty years, every vendor sold them the same fix and none of it worked.

* Better integrations, cleaner APIs, a newer ERP: all sold as the answer, none of them the problem.
* The real bottleneck was never the software. It was that a person had to sit there and operate it, one purchase order at a time.
* So the back office stays buried in manual data entry, supplier emails, and pricing mistakes caught too late.

The work is repetitive, high volume, and expensive to staff. Every factory has it. No one has solved it.

### **Our Solution**

We stopped trying to replace the software. We gave Walter a login instead.

Walter logs into the systems a factory already runs (SAP, Dynamics, Oracle, Teams, Outlook and Gmail, etc.) the way a new employee would. Same screens, same buttons, no integration project, no rip and replace. He reads the orders, enters them, places supplier POs, and catches the pricing mismatch before it becomes a costly mistake. 

What used to take a back office team now runs on its own.

We start with packaging and industrial manufacturing, where the ERPs are oldest and the manual load is heaviest. The endpoint is bigger: once Walter runs the workflows, the software underneath becomes a database he operates in.

### **Our Ask**

If any of these are you, we'd love to talk:

* Manufacturers drowning in back-office data entry across SAP, Dynamics, or Oracle.
* Operators and heads of digitization who want to see Walter run on their own ERP.
* Anyone who knows a factory still doing this work by hand.

launches.tagline: Staging environment for enterprise AI agents
launches.body:
TLDR; 

**Chronicle Labs is a staging environment for enterprise AI agents: we capture every event the agent sees in production and replay it, so customers can deploy new behaviors quickly without breaking anything.** 

<https://youtu.be/LdpAPgGYL1E>

Hello Bookface! My name is Ayman, and I’m the CEO of Chronicle Labs.

For the past 10 years, I’ve been building autonomous systems. I’ve had the chance to work on the Mars Rovers and the James Webb Space Telescope at NASA JPL, and throughout my career, I’ve been able to build autonomous systems from day one without ever having to physically touch the robots,  thanks to the power of logs that replay state like a time machine.

Think tools like [Rerun.io](http://Rerun.io) or ROS bags. These tools are incredibly powerful because they capture the full state of a robotic system at a slice in time, which can then be replayed down to the microsecond to understand what actually happened.

AI agents are the autonomous systems of businesses.

But if you want to develop an AI agent for your business, it’s rare to have a structured slice of logs that you can replay to prove your agent will actually work. Teams can vibe-deploy, but testing on your users is a bad idea, especially for enterprises that are risk-averse.

Today, most teams try to solve this by hand-building evals. That works for a bit, but it doesn’t scale, and honestly I’ve seen many teams skip evals entirely. More importantly, as your business grows, your operations keep changing. Small nuances, edge cases, and workflow drift will always start to trend away from a static eval set.

My co-founder [@Rowan Zyadeh](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1599381) and I built Chronicle to give teams the ability to backtest their agents against their actual operational reality. Chronicle takes your existing operational history and turns it into seeded sandboxes with scenarios based on how your business really works.

Book a demo: <https://chronicle-labs.com/book-call>

If you’re building agents and you’re sick of vibe-deploying, or you feel like your eval suite is lacking, we want to talk to you.

name: Tasklet
long_description:
AI chatbots can answer questions, but they can't do your work — they aren't connected to your tools, can't take actions, and stop running when you close the tab. Meanwhile, knowledge workers are still spending most of their day switching between dozens of SaaS apps, manually stitching together workflows that should be automated.

Tasklet is the AI agent that actually does the work. It connects to every tool you use — via thousands of built-in integrations, any HTTP API, or MCP servers — and takes real actions on your behalf: pulling reports, updating CRMs, triaging emails, processing data, and more. When it needs a UI, it generates one on the fly. When it needs to crunch numbers or do bulk operations, it writes and runs code in a cloud sandbox. When it needs to interact with a website that doesn't have an API, it uses a real browser. And because it runs in the cloud 24/7, you can set up triggers to have it take ongoing responsibility for workflows — not just do something once, but handle it going forward.

The product is deliberately simple: a chat interface where you talk to an extremely capable agent. But underneath that simplicity is a cloud-native agent runtime, best-in-class context engineering, a universal connections layer, and multi-model support that keeps us on the frontier as AI improves. 

We think legacy SaaS is being unbundled by agents, and Tasklet is the operating system that ties it all together.
one_liner: Agents that own the work

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer: We met at Firebase and continued working together at Google after the acquisition. In 2020 we left to start a company together, initially building an email client called Shortwave. While adding an AI agent to Shortwave in late 2024, we noticed something surprising: some users kept asking for the agent and integrations without the email client. They wanted a general-purpose AI agent that could connect to all their work tools — not just email. So in 2025 we made a bold bet, building Tasklet as a standalone cloud AI agent for knowledge work.

question_answers.question: What's the history of your company from getting started until the present day? What were the big inflection points?
question_answers.answer:
We founded the company in 2020 as a team of ex-Firebase/Google engineers. We initially built Shortwave, an AI-powered email client. After ChatGPT launched, we went all-in on AI and built a conversational assistant for email that showed real traction.\
\
In fall 2024 we shipped a full AI agent inside Shortwave — and growth accelerated. We started adding integrations with CRMs, project management tools, and messaging apps, and were among the first products to support MCP. That's when something unexpected happened: users started telling us they wanted the agent and integrations but didn't care about the email client.

So in 2025 we made a bold move — we built Tasklet, a standalone cloud AI agent for knowledge work. We went from idea to first user in under 6 weeks, and it was a massive hit. Each new capability we shipped (v2 agent architecture, sandbox, computer use, triggers) accelerated growth further, and by January 2026 Tasklet alone was adding more monthly revenue than Shortwave had in its first 4 years.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
AI chatbots can answer questions, but they can't actually do your work. They aren't connected to your tools, they can't take actions, and they stop running the moment you close the tab. The result is that knowledge workers still spend most of their day switching between dozens of SaaS apps — pulling data from one, updating another, copy-pasting between tabs, and stitching together workflows manually.\
\
We're building the AI agent that replaces all of that: one app that connects to every tool you use, runs 24/7 in the cloud, can use a computer, and can take ongoing responsibility for entire workflows.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
In the long run, we believe most knowledge work will be done by AI agents, not humans. Tasklet is the operating system for that future — the place where you manage, direct, and collaborate with agents that handle your work across every tool.

If we truly succeed, the average knowledge worker will 10x their output not by working harder, but by delegating most of their routine work to agents that run 24/7. Legacy SaaS apps will fade into background infrastructure that agents access via API, and the human's job shifts from doing the work to directing it. We think this is as big a shift as the move from desktop software to cloud — and we're building the platform that makes it happen.

launches.tagline: Permissioned tools, cloud agents, automations, and shared workflows for the AI apps your team already uses.
launches.body:
Website: <https://www.watolabs.com>

**TL;DR: Wato is a shared AI workspace for teams.** It helps companies keep their AI workflows, company knowledge, integrations, agent sessions, and agent-generated work inside the organization instead of scattered across individual chats, local files, or personal AI accounts. All of this is done via one, unified MCP.

**Ask:** If your team is using AI agents for engineering, ops, sales, research, finance, support, or internal workflows, we’d love to see how we can help. We’re especially interested in teams setting up MCP/tools, sharing prompts or workflows internally, launching cloud agents, or trying to preserve useful agent context across the company.

**The problem:** Teams are already using AI for real company workflows: debugging production issues, preparing sales calls, analyzing customer data, updating models, drafting client deliverables, and searching across internal systems.

But the work usually disappears into individual tools and accounts. The context, prompts, decisions, files, and tool setups that made the output useful are hard for the next teammate to find, trust, or reuse.

**What Wato does:** Wato gives each team a shared, permissioned AI workspace.

Teams can connect approved integrations and MCP tools, build shared memory, publish reusable skills, run collaborative cloud agent sessions, host live artifacts and dashboards, and trace tool calls across the organization.

The goal is simple: **when one person or agent learns something useful, builds a workflow, or creates an artifact, that knowledge should stay with the company and become available to the right people.**

**What’s included:**

\- **Team memory** for durable company knowledge agents can reuse

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/64ae52b1-6599-49c7-9e99-297e4e71a9ae)

\- **Approved MCP tools and integrations** with org, team, per-user, and tool-level permissions

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/e8673b85-1e38-456a-ad60-d5d90ed2fe80)

\- **Reusable skills and workflows** library so teams don’t prompt from scratch every time

\- **Cloud agent sessions** that teammates can view, continue, and collaborate on, with access to a desktop, computer use, filesystem, and environment set up.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/b3da2993-c84f-4347-ad8a-46fea54ee809)

\- **Automations** that can be created from connector triggers or run on a specific cadence.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/edc32ad1-ae2e-42ef-9014-0782e8112464)

\- **Live artifacts and dashboards** that can use approved company data

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/700f9d35-6150-4012-b58c-e56b54b39c30)

\- **Tool-call tracing and audit logs** so teams can see what agents accessed and produced

Wato also works with the AI tools teams already use, including Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, and other MCP-compatible environments. You add the Wato MCP once, authenticate with your company account, and your agent gets access to the right team memory, skills, and approved tools.

**Backstory:** We started working on Wato after seeing the same problem across institutions adopting these tools like Claude or Codex. A super user would figure out a great workflow, debugging process, research method, client-prep flow, or tool setup, but the useful part would end up stuck in a chat thread, local file, or personal account. Then the next person would start over.

At the same time, companies didn’t want every employee independently managing MCP configs, tool permissions, prompts, and scattered agent instructions. They needed a shared layer between the company and the AI tools its people use to normalize AI use.

That became Wato.

**We’d love to talk to teams who are:**

\- **using agents** across engineering, ops, sales, research, finance, support, or internal workflows

\- setting up **MCP servers or internal tools** for agent use

\- trying to **share prompts, skills, playbooks, or workflows** across a team

\- creating AI-generated **dashboards**, docs, reports, or **artifacts** that need to be shared securely

\- worried about **company knowledge** disappearing into personal AI accounts

\- thinking about **permissions**, **review**, **tracing**, or **governance** for agent work

If this sounds familiar, and I’m guessing it does for a lot of you, we’d love to show you Wato and get feedback.

**How did we get here (the problem)?**

Ardent was a reaction to the failure of our last product - an AI Data Engineer. It was a coding agent that generated data pipelines, wrote migrations, backfills and other things you’d expect of a data engineer.

While the code _looked_ great we had no way of testing generated code. Writing to prod was out of the question and dev environments were never in sync, shared amongst devs which caused write clashes between agents, and was a huge pain to manage. **_What we needed was a ephemeral DB sandbox per agent of the user’s DB._**

Because of how hard testing was, generated code would never be tested and was too unstable to put in production. Database failures almost always mean downtime, a risk both we and customers were obviously not willing to take. We churned almost 200K in ARR

This problem exists with any coding agent today. We’re shipping 100x more DB code to production and we mostly just hope to god it works the same as dev.

**Ardent - Isolated <6s database clones that let you test agent code:**

Ardent solves the DB sandbox problem by letting you create 6s clones of ANY postgres DB regardless of size, allowing you to give every developer and every agent a full copy of production or dev to test against.

Clones autoscale to zero when not in use, use copy on write for massive storage efficiency and can be loaded with a single CLI command (zero infra management)

You can see the exact results of any code run against the DB in a perfect 1:1 reproduction and don’t have to change your DB provider.

The entire thing runs as a CLI that feels exactly like git. Cloning is as simple as “ardent branch create <name>”

This means you can spin up instant environments to test _every_ line of DB code with none of the overhead

**Asks**

**Use Ardent at your company to go faster by let agents work safely at the DB layer and prevent regressions:** <https://cal.com/vikram-chennai/yc-reserved>

**Introduce me to series A-C engineering leaders (Founders, CTOs, VP of Eng):** Many of the later stage startups we’ve talked to have the majority of their engineers shipping with claude, codex or cursor on migrations, backfills and pretty much any code that hits the DB. They will eventually crash their production DB unless they’re rigorously testing. I’d like to prevent those crashes :)

Contact me: [vikram@tryardent.com](mailto:vikram@tryardent.com)

launches.title: Silmaril: Self-healing Prompt Injection Defense
launches.tagline: Block 2x more attacks with 10x lower latency.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Silmaril is the first self-healing prompt injection defense for AI native applications and agents. It understands application context to **block 2x as many threats** as current SOTA defenses with **10x lower latency**. Customers plug us into frameworks like LangChain with **5 lines of code**.

We’re working with the top productivity, analytics, and legal companies in the world and would love to protect you as well!

Our Launch Video: <https://youtu.be/95VAZSvIsLA>

**Ask**: If your AI systems ingest external data or you’re concerned about prompt injection, set up a[ 15 minute chat](https://cal.com/silmaril/15min). If you know security or AI leaders (Director+) who could benefit from stopping prompt injections please reach out at [aum@silmaril.dev](mailto:aum@silmaril.dev).

**Problem**

Attackers are using AI to create and experiment with more sophisticated techniques at scale, making them **4.5x more likely to succeed**. The AI security tools enterprises rely on today were not built for this.

Existing guardrails treat malicious inputs as the unit of security. They pattern-match against known bad prompts and require constant manual policy tuning. Against real-world contextual and emerging threats, leading guardrails **blocked only 61% of attacks**. That's barely better a coin toss.

This leaves security teams stuck in an **endless loop**: triaging alerts, tuning policies, and chasing attackers who move faster than they can respond.

**How it works**

Most AI security tools ask "does this input look malicious?" We ask "does this execution lead to a harmful outcome?" That distinction is what makes Silmaril work against attacks that guardrails completely miss.

The system has three layers:

**1. Agents hunt for attacks and generate threat intelligence.** We reverse-engineer your application and deploy autonomous agents that continuously probe it. These agents find and verify attack chains that combine individual vulnerabilities for a larger impact such as data exfiltration and privilege escalation. They surface novel threats tied to your application logic, far more useful in simulating AI enabled attackers than historical prompt injection lists.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99681&key=user_uploads/2524062/1eabf307-2ebb-4b76-883c-ba1f8e0c2fd2)

**2. A classifier model that blocks attackers in real time.** The firewall integrates directly with your orchestration framework via our SDK, letting you control exactly when it runs. In LangGraph, for example, you can add it as a callback handler that fires before/after tool calls and model inference. Because Silmaril reasons over application snapshots rather than input patterns, it catches emerging, contextual, and multi-turn attacks that single-input classifiers miss entirely. Latency overhead is 20ms.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99681&key=user_uploads/2524062/b631db01-cdd7-4727-a01c-3471c385244f)

**3. A self-healing retraining loop.** Verified exploits from threat hunting and production traffic feeds back into the model continuously. The firewall retrains and deploys updated weights automatically within an hour. No manual policy tuning required.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99681&key=user_uploads/2524062/60e34848-7ebc-4733-b231-4da711b0bfd9)

Against a dataset of real-world contextual and emerging threats, **Silmaril blocked 96% of attacks**. Leading guardrails blocked 61%.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99681&key=user_uploads/2524062/b538fcdf-509e-4345-9eb4-399728ea5abe)

**Why us**

Eduardo and I spent 10+ years building security and AI. I built security frameworks protecting AWS’s AI infrastructure. Eduardo developed hardened models and agents for Amazon's homepage. We drove **$2.2B in savings and new revenue**.

After leaving, we became whitehat hackers and hacked OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft **15 times in two weeks**. We saw firsthand how far ahead attackers already are. That's why we built Silmaril.

# **Hey 👋** We're Edward and Jennifer, founders of **Saudara AI**.

**TL;DR:** We're an AI broker connecting American brands with the world’s best international factories. Saudara is built by a third-generation manufacturer and an Amazon supply chain veteran, two people who've spent their careers on both sides of this problem. 

We don’t just sell software, we sell outcomes and services. Real humans do the work, supercharged by AI, at 10x the speed and a fraction of the cost of traditional sourcing agents.

International sourcing is hard. We make it easy.

<https://youtu.be/tna8cqJsfok>

**❌ The Problem**

Sourcing overseas should be straightforward. It never is. Five traps catch almost every foreign buyer, and most never see it coming.

* **Trust** — Suppliers overpromise, cut corners on mass production, and go quiet after the deposit clears.
* **Price** — Unbeatable quotes hide lower grade materials, hidden fees, and cost hikes once you're locked in.
* **Timing** — Missed deadlines kill holiday season sales, trigger chargebacks, and derail launches.
* **Payment terms** — New buyers pay 100% upfront. Established buyers get net-60. The playing field has never been level.
* **Scalability** — A supplier that works at 500 units may fall apart at 50,000.

**✅ Our Solution**

Saudara means "family" in Indonesian. Jennifer's family has spent 50+ years building relationships across Asian manufacturing. We don't blindly search for suppliers. We have their personal numbers.

We're a broker, not a marketplace. You tell us what you need, we deliver it. Our relationships get us into factories that don't take cold inquiries. Our AI handles the rest, vetting, benchmarking, negotiation support, QC tracking, and logistics, end-to-end.

* **Trust, protected** — Our AI flags supplier inconsistencies and tells you when something looks too good to be true.
* **Price transparency** — Every quote benchmarked against real market data. You always know what's fair.
* **Specs, timelines, and QC** — Spec sheets locked before approval, milestones tracked proactively, quality checked from raw materials to shipment.
* **Better payment terms** — We negotiate 30/70 and net-60 on your behalf. The terms established buyers take for granted, available from day one.
* **Suppliers that can scale** — Matched to your volume today and where you're going tomorrow.

**🌿 Starting With Indonesia?**

We're starting with Indonesia because it's where we're from, and because most of it is still inaccessible to Western buyers without the right relationships. We have them.

Palm oil, vanilla, nickel, rattan, patchouli, charcoal briquettes, handcrafted furniture from Jepara, and one of Southeast Asia's strongest apparel manufacturing bases. Resource-rich, largely untapped, and relationship-gated.

**👫 The Team**

**Edward** **Haryono** — Grew up around Indonesian logistics. Amazon supply chain background. President of IABA-PNW (Non profit promoting Indonesia and Pacific Northwest Economic Relations)

**Jennifer Prasetyo** — Third-generation Indonesian manufacturer. Nationally trusted sourcing expert behind [@jenandtech](https://www.instagram.com/jenandtech/) (95K+ followers across all socials).

Stop gambling on suppliers. If you or someone you know is sourcing products internationally, send them our way. Start with [Saudara.](https://saudara.ai)

launches.body:
Hey 👋 We’re Raphaël and Alexandre, co-founders of [Foaster](https://foaster.ai).

# 

# **TL;DR**

Our agents run **AI-led interviews** **across your entire company** to map how work actually happens, identify the **highest-impact AI opportunities** in just a few days, and support execution through **adoption tracking, personalized upskilling, and expert guidance.**

Book a demo [here](https://foaster.cal.com/raphael.dabadie/30min).

# 

# **❌ The Problem**

Most companies confuse AI adoption with AI transformation.

**AI adoption** is giving employees better tools: ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, internal assistants.

That can make individuals faster. But the company itself often stays the same: same workflows, same meetings, same approval chains, same bottlenecks.

**AI transformation** is different. It means redesigning how work happens around what AI now makes possible.

The problem is that this transformation is broad, fast-moving, and continuous. It touches **every function, every workflow, and every role**, while tools and capabilities keep evolving.

**Traditional methods cannot keep up.** Workshops, consulting projects, and static roadmaps are too slow, too generic, and too disconnected from day-to-day operations.

# **✅ The Solution**

Foaster combines AI agents and human experts to help companies make AI transformation scalable, continuous, and personalized.

### 1. Mapping the company

We run **30 to 45-minute AI-led interviews** across the organization.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100799&key=user_uploads/3198551/2ee984d6-7f59-4b8a-9541-fc5ee33eaaef)

Agents collect **the context that usually stays trapped in people’s heads**: workflows, tools, handoffs, bottlenecks, dependencies, informal habits, and repetitive tasks.

The result is **a granular map of how the company actually works**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100799&key=user_uploads/3198551/5f0f7cd9-27f6-4558-b8b2-4e193bd13569)

### 2. Turning the map into a roadmap

Agents reason over that map to **identify where AI can have the highest impact**: what should be automated, redesigned, augmented, or improved first.

Our **human experts review the findings**, bring business judgment, and help leadership prioritize the roadmap based on impact, feasibility, and company goals.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100799&key=user_uploads/3198551/b404941d-2f4f-41e6-a966-bfb809830afc)

### 3. Keeping the transformation alive

Foaster keeps the map updated over time, tracks adoption, detects where teams are stuck, and generates **personalized upskilling for each employee** based on their role, tools, workflows, and level.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100799&key=user_uploads/3198551/9791493a-e960-496a-b416-0593848b3691)

Agents handle the scale, follow-up, and personalization while human experts bring judgment, expertise, change management, and implementation support when needed.

The goal: **help the whole company move in one direction while supporting every employee at individual scale.**

# [**👬**](https://emojipedia.org/men-holding-hands) **The Team**

We spent the past year working as AI consultants and saw firsthand how broken the old model was.

We also did AI research and built two benchmarks that got widely shared: [The Werewolf Benchmark](https://werewolf.foaster.ai), notably shared by Greg Brockman, Clément Delangue, and Thomas Wolf, and [The Political Gap Between AIs and Citizens](https://llm-politics.foaster.ai), shared by Elon Musk and viewed over 12 million times on social media.

At the same time, we watched models get really good at knowledge work. It became obvious that AI could do a large part of what AI consultants were doing, but at much faster speed and scale.

## **📣 Our Ask**

We’d love intros to enterprises or mid-market companies trying to figure out what AI transformation should look like in practice.

If you know someone leading AI transformation, AI enablement, operations, or process improvement, we’d love to talk.

👉 [**raphael.dabadie@foaster.ai**](mailto:raphael.dabadie@foaster.ai)

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋! We're [Kareem Selim](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kareem-se1im/) and [Hassan Mostafa](https://www.linkedin.com/in/h4ss4nmostafa/), co-founders of [RASPIRE](https://www.linkedin.com/company/raspire/).

**TL;DR:** RASPIRE is an AI runtime security layer for mobile apps. It protects applications every time they run, automatically detecting and responding to attacks in production while giving security teams real-time visibility into threats across their applications. Already protecting apps used by 20M+ end users across banking, fintech, healthtech, and e-commerce.\
\
**Our Launch Video**: <https://youtu.be/uggwRzCNs88>

\
**Ask**: Building a mobile app or already have one? We'll help you secure it. Book a demo: [cal.com/raspire/demo](https://cal.com/raspire/demo)

**The problem**

Building and shipping a mobile app has never been easier.

But security still requires complex integrations, code changes, and months of work.

Existing solutions often requires SDK integrations, configuration, and security expertise to operate but developers shouldn't become security experts just to ship an app.

As a result, security is often overlooked or assumed to be handled by app stores.

it's not…

and as AI accelerates app development, the attack surface is growing faster than security can keep up.\
\
**The Solution**

If you can build an app in one click, you should be able to secure it in one click.

RASPIRE is making securing mobile apps as simple as building them. We protect Android and iOS applications without writing a single line of code.

Simply upload your compiled app, and RASPIRE automatically applies the right protections in minutes, from anti-fraud and app integrity to reverse-engineering and API protection.

Unlike code scanners tools that stop before release, RASPIRE protects applications every time they run, automatically detecting and responding to attacks in production while giving security teams real-time visibility into threats across their applications.

**How it works**

Upload your compiled app (APK/IPA). We harden it automatically. No SDK. No code changes. No config files. No workflow changes. Done in minutes. Plugs into your CI/CD pipeline. Cloud or on-prem, your call.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102582&key=user_uploads/3400512/3f3b04d5-4b8a-4357-b2ac-09e039c8ac59)

**Full visibility into your app's security**

Once shielded, you get real-time visibility into everything happening inside your app. Security events flow into your existing SIEM or your application monitoring platform (e.g. Sentry/DataDog).

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Mentlio is the engineering intelligence platform for the AI-coding era. We help engineering organizations cut AI costs by up to 30% and finally see what ROI that spend is actually producing. All without ever collecting your prompts or source code.

**Launch Video**

<https://youtu.be/-28j9HvTYV0>

**Problem**

Every engineering org is now an AI org. Token usage is growing exponentially, and so is the bill. The following questions have been largely unanswered:

* How can we cut our usage-based AI spend without bottlenecking usage or efficiency?
* What ROI are we getting for every dollar of AI spend?
* To what extent is AI-generated code creating quality debt?

Brian Armstrong recently laid out how Coinbase is reducing AI spend while token usage grows exponentially on X: better defaults, smarter routing, cache awareness, lean context, and full visibility into usage and impact. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111055&key=user_uploads/2693539/7bf48740-dd37-4015-9da9-ec0f9bd900ed)

Coinbase built a custom harness, LLM gateway, routing, and usage visibility internally. We believe they have the right thesis, but most engineering orgs don’t want to run on a custom harness. **Mentlio gives every eng team a better version of those savings & visibility without changing any workflows.**

**Solution**

Mentlio gives you:

1. **ROI.** We translate every PR into normalized units of work: Delivery Points. We consider associated spend, code reusability, and historical patches to turn "we spend $X on AI"  -> "we spend $X per impact point.” compared to industry data. 
2. **Cost intelligence + optimization.** See exactly where AI spend goes across teams, tools, and models. Optionally catch and cut waste across cache misses, oversized models on trivial tasks, bloated context and cut it without capping/bottlenecking accuracy. 
3. **Quality signal.** AI-assisted code that ships fast but breaks later isn't a win. We connect AI usage to delivery and quality outcomes so you can see the full picture

We’re the only platform with the above capabilities that never collects prompts or source code.

**Our Asks**

If you are or know a Head of Eng, VP Eng, CTO, or platform lead at a 15+ engineer org with real AI spend, reach out! You can book a demo at[ mentlio.com/intro](http://mentlio.com/intro) or reach us at [founders@mentlio.com](mailto:founders@mentlio.com).

**The Team**

Ashank and Ahmet met while studying Computer Science at Caltech while they were working part-time Founding Engineer roles at Series A and Seed stage startups. Ashank previously researched generative image AI & graph deep learning for pathology, genomics, and drug design at Dartmouth & Purdue and won internationally at the International Science & Engineering Fair & Junior Science & Humanities Symposium. Ahmet previously published his research in transformers and AI in IEEE, BMC AI, and ACM and also won internationally at the National AI Olympiad, International Science & Engineering Fair, and was named a Top 300 Science Scholar by Regeneron.

* **Lack of knowledge and capacity to adopt AI effectively.** Most companies can't identify which workflows should be automated, let alone build a production-grade system to do it. The engineers who can do this work are scarce and concentrated in a handful of frontier firms.

* ⚙️ **Ops agents** that keep internal systems in sync without anyone asking.

**Hey everyone 👋**

We're Amin and Imad, cofounders of Amboras.

**TL;DR** Amboras is an AI native platform that puts the entire e-commerce stack on autopilot. Bring an existing store or start from scratch. It learns how your customers buy and autonomously ships the changes that make your store sell better.

Merchants get into e-commerce to build a business. Instead they're stitching together a dozen apps, paying a CRO agency on retainer, and burning weeks with developers and analytics tools just to figure out what their customers actually want. Most stores plateau at a 2% conversion rate. What about the other 98%?

Amboras is making margins possible that weren't possible pre AI.

**Our Launch Video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xr0VEaJPJow>

Ask: Do you run an ecommerce store, or know someone who does? I'd love to speak to them directly: <https://cal.com/imad-mokadem/amboras-team>

**Problem ❌**

Ecommerce is a $30T+ global industry, still running on tooling that predates AI. Every layer of the stack is static and manual, so nothing a merchant learns ever compounds into a better store.

It comes down to four things:

1. **Static offers & storefronts.** Stores should learn from every interaction and adapt to every ICP. Today they don't.
2. **Slow A/B testing.** Finding a winning storefront and offer means designers, CRO experts, developers, and weeks of waiting, just for a single test.
3. **No agentic layer.** No platform is built for the coming age of agentic purchasing.
4. **The plugin and agency tax.** A dozen apps charging you monthly, a CRO agency taking a retainer, and on top of that a cut of every conversion uplift they ship.

We built and grew our own educational board game brand to $200K/month, and watched our margins get eaten by exactly this overhead.

**Solution ✅**

Amboras is an AI native commerce platform. You run your store by talking to AI, and it runs itself on autopilot, getting better every day, hands free.

**Part 1: Build or rebuild your store**

No dashboards, no apps, no code. You tell Amboras what you want and it does it: generating or rebuilding your storefront, adding products, creating images and copy, testing offers, launching price changes. Building the store is simply the first thing you ask it to do. In the demo below, every action is done by AI. (If you already have a store, we can A/B test Amboras with your current setup, without any risk)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101666&key=user_uploads/1449044/2414f82e-a13e-428c-b752-a3346d7bbd42)

Every session feeds Amboras a richer picture of your customers, and the agent translates that picture into a constantly expanding test queue as your store scales. It autonomously ships offer tweaks, layout changes, and copy variants that compound your CVR, retention, and AOV, while learning about your ICP deeper with every visitor, all working toward the real goal of maximizing lifetime value per visitor. While you focus all your efforts on driving traffic to your page, your store keeps improving on its own, getting sharper the more it sees. Our A/B testing engine is in beta, and early merchants are already seeing over 80% CVR lift on the first version Amboras puts live.

launches.body:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V-sLwzskvqE>

When I was 18, I joined Magic, a frontier lab working on 100M token context coding models, as a reinforcement learning researcher.

While I worked there, I gradually grew more drawn to autonomous research. I truly felt that this could automate all the work I was doing at Magic, so in January, I left to start my own lab.

Introducing Aster — a major breakthrough for research.

Aster isn’t a single agent. It is the first autonomous lab orchestrating **thousands of research agents in parallel.**

We pointed Aster towards ProteinGym, a benchmark that measures how accurately models predict the effects of protein mutations. It set the world record in **30 minutes**.

And it did it efficiently:

    •    57x faster than single agent systems on the same task.

    •    One-third the cost for the same result.

But here’s what we realized: measurable problems are only a small sliver of research.

The hard ones were never measurable.

At Aster, we’re on a mission to automate open-ended research, research that defines its own problems before it can answer them.

The future doesn’t wait to be defined by benchmarks. Neither do we.

Read our research writeups at <https://asterlab.ai>.

launches.title: Infinity — A New Computation Layer
launches.tagline: Months of work, done in days. Every app gets its own GPU, in one browser tab.
launches.body:
Hey YC 👋

We're Rounak, Bishal & Sourya — co-founders of ProjectX (P26). Today we're launching Infinity.

\[<https://youtu.be/ZYf2vdWMkDk>\]

### TL;DR

**Infinity is a new computation layer — a web-based OS where every app you open runs on its own independent compute and GPU, inside one shared workspace.** Open Blender, Unreal, Isaac Sim, DaVinci, VS Code in the same browser tab. Each app is its own machine with its own GPU. They share one filesystem and one terminal. Windows and Linux apps run side by side. Runs on any browser, on any device. Open fifty apps at once — nothing slows down.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/28491e87-8d68-4bd0-b0ea-860d2d7d1825)

### Problem

The apps people actually use to build the future — Blender, Unreal, Isaac Sim, Houdini, the CAD/CAM/CAE stack, ML pipelines — still need a $5K workstation under your desk. The cloud was supposed to fix this and didn't. Renting a cloud GPU means hours of driver installs, version matching, container debugging before you do any actual work. Streamed desktops (Citrix, Paperspace, Shadow) give you one VM with one GPU — built for one user running one app at a time. Open Blender and Unreal at the same time and you're fighting yourself for resources.

It's hitting agents too. Claude Cowork runs on your laptop, sharing your GPU with everything else. Manus runs in a CPU-bound microVM that can't open heavy apps at all. Claude can drive Blender via MCP, but Blender still runs on your machine — the agent just borrows your compute.

### Solution

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/281d546a-52f7-4932-b92e-30608f83f249)

Infinity makes every app its own computer.

Open Blender, you get a machine with a dedicated GPU. Open Unreal in the next window, that's a second machine with its own GPU. Open Isaac Sim, that's a third. They share a filesystem and a terminal so the workspace feels like one computer, but underneath they're independent machines. Open fifty apps, you have fifty machines. Nothing slows down. Runs entirely in a browser tab — Chromebook, iPad, five-year-old laptop, doesn't matter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/971299ab-663b-4181-ae7e-64ed286ecda2)

\
Every Infinity workspace comes will soon ship with a built-in computer use agent that can access run applications without being constrained by compute, no matter how many applications you run or how heavy the workflow is. Tell it what you want, and it spins up the apps, drives them, hands files between them, and finishes the work. You can drive Infinity with a mouse and keyboard, or you can drive it with a prompt.

A concrete example. You prompt: _"Make a 90-second product launch video. Write the script, generate the voiceover, edit in DaVinci, render the 3D logo in Blender, post to YouTube."_

Six apps spin up at once:

* Claude writes the script
* ElevenLabs generates the voiceover
* DaVinci Resolve edits the cut
* Blender renders the 3D logo
* Chrome uploads to YouTube
* VS Code writes the publish script

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/fc66db17-d35b-4f3d-8459-cec58a4cebc2)

They share a workspace. They hand files to each other. **One finished video in an hour, not three days.**

### Where we are — 15 days in early preview 

* **20,000+ builders** signed up
* **1,160% growth** in the last 14 days
* **20M+ impressions** on X and Instagram
* **10,000+ signups** in the last 7 days
* **Out of server capacity** — rate-limiting new signups while we scale

Our first public demo crashed our servers at midnight; we scaled the infra live at 3am and woke up to inbound from 50+ enterprises.

Once every app has its own compute, agents stop being a separate problem.

A computer-use agent is just another app — except the agent drives itself. Because every agent gets its own machine on Infinity, ten agents work in parallel without stepping on each other. The thing that's impossible today — ten parallel cursors, ten parallel renders, ten parallel models — is the default on Infinity.

We're shipping the multi-agent runtime next. One prompt, a mother agent plans and coordinates, child agents execute on dedicated hardware — each routing through Claude, GPT, Gemini, or any MCP tool. Same substrate humans use, given to agents.

If you are, or know any of the following, we want to hear from you:

**Heavy-GPU teams.** Robotics, Physical AI, 3D/VFX, ML, post-production, CAD/CAM/CAE. If you're buying workstations or wrestling with cloud GPU setup, let's talk.
