launches.tagline: A new kind of team: humans and agents, working together.
launches.body:
Hey YC! I'm [Edgar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/edgarpavlovsky/), building [Pentagon](https://pentagon.run).

**TL;DR** Agents are everywhere but they don't have good ways to work together, so humans become the coordination bottleneck. Pentagon is a coordination layer where your agents communicate autonomously, coordinate on tasks, and get work done as a team.

**Book a demo and see it in action:** <https://pentagon.run>\
**Our launch video:** <https://youtu.be/D28Mi7AXAeY>

**Problem**

Agents are increasingly becoming AI teammates at work - coding, researching, ops, even talking to customers. But they work alone. Coordination is the bottleneck, and it shows up differently depending on where you sit:

* **Small teams** are spinning up agents from scratch and immediately hitting the ceiling: each one is powerful on its own, but getting them to actually work together means you're back in the loop, copy/pasting between terminals.
* **Enterprises** already have agents running everywhere across the org. The hard part is figuring out what they're doing, how they fit together, and how to keep track of it all.

Underneath both: humans are the middleware. Hours of human time burnt doing work meant for a mechanical turk. Today's tools weren't built for this - AI products are conversational and non-deterministic, and reproducing workflows is harder than ever.

**Org code**

There's a deeper layer to this. Great teams are built for the moment - the right team depends on the problem at hand, the resources you have, and even who's leading. This applies to agents the same as it does to humans: every problem has its own org structure.

Andrej Karpathy calls it "org code" - and points out that compared to classical orgs, agentic codes have powerful new properties: they’re reproducible and more transparent. We think that agents also allow organizations to be much more dynamic: they can adapt to problems in realtime, and open a new dimension of what it means to build a productive organization.

From [a popular Karpathy tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2031767720933634100):

![Image](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HIts8HMaIAAKjok?format=jpg&name=medium)

**Our first solution: Pentagon Studio**

Pentagon's mission is to build the coordination layer for humans and agents. We're starting with Pentagon Studio - a workspace designed to feel familiar to existing alternatives and shepherd companies into a new kind of collaborative work.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101681&key=user_uploads/402484/286ecb28-a420-4390-81cf-f1c1b181ec5c)

In Pentagon Studio, you define your org structure and your agents run it. Agents live on a spatial canvas and pop up sticky notes with status updates - you see who's active, idle, or blocked at a glance. They message each other, delegate tasks, share context, and build self-evolving memory over time. As the human, your job is to design and manage the team; they do the coordination.

* **Spatial canvas.** Agents live on infinite canvases you can think of like an office. Zoom in on one agent's conversation, zoom out to see the whole operation. The "org IDE."
* **Autonomous coordination.** Realtime, event-driven communication between agents - no expensive polling loops. Agents take feedback from you, ping another agent to get work done, then ping you when they need you.
* **Agent persistence.** Agents maintain sessions indefinitely and compound institutional knowledge over time. Tribal knowledge for your agent team.
* **Shared skills & tools.** Manage capabilities at individual, team, workspace, or org level. Each agent inherits based on hierarchy.
* **Human multiplayer + human-in-the-loop.** In contrast to "zero-human company" angles, we see humans and agents collaborating across shared orgs. Your agents should be able to work with your coworkers' agents.

**Why now**

Agents are already inside companies. The infrastructure to coordinate them isn't. Every day this gap stays open, humans burn hours doing work meant for a mechanical turk and leaders lose transparency into how work actually gets done.

We believe the best version of the future is one where superintelligent agents are viewed as teammates and we work with them as partners. Every company already knows how to work with coworkers - agents fit into existing organizational frameworks better than we've been giving them credit for. They just need the infrastructure to coordinate.

**Ask**

If you're running agentic workflows in production and struggling to manage them, we’d love to chat. See Pentagon Studio in action and book a demo with us at <https://pentagon.run> or reach out to me personally, and let’s evolve your team: [edgar@pentagon.run](mailto:edgar@pentagon.run).

launches.title: Expanse - Unlock wasted GPU capacity
launches.tagline: Unlock wasted GPU capacity.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Expanse unlocks wasted GPU capacity. We’re the intelligence layer for compute infrastructure. Submit jobs with the right resources. Optimise them to run faster. Debug failures in seconds, not days. Works on cloud and on-prem HPC.

Want to know how much more you can get out of your hardware? Schedule a call: <https://book.getexpanse.io>

**Problem**

Running compute on a cluster means guessing memory, time, and GPUs before you submit. Get it wrong and your job fails mid-run. Over-guess and you pay for compute you never use. 30% of cloud spend is lost to over-allocation \[1\]. Microsoft Research found their own deep learning jobs hit 50% GPU utilisation or lower \[2\].

Sizing jobs takes decades of experience. Memory patterns, batching, GPU threading, CPU vectorisation. AI agents don’t have enough information to fix it either. SLURM and Kubernetes don’t expose enough structured data. Even strong platform teams are forced to choose: spend time debugging and optimising every job, or accept the waste. AI infrastructure spending will hit $2.52 trillion in 2026 \[3\]. The waste grows with every new cluster. This problem isn’t going away.

**Solution**

Expanse learns your cluster. We analyse your code and hardware telemetry, then track them over time. Our deep learning models build a picture of what your workloads actually need. Predictions get sharper with every job.

Our models are deployed on your cluster. All analysis runs on your network. Your code and telemetry never leave your infrastructure. We can’t see your data, and you maintain full data sovereignty.

One command installs Expanse on your cluster. You get two tools.

`expanse analyse` - for every job:

* **Suggests the right resource configuration**
* **Predicts failures from historical code and telemetry patterns**
* **Surfaces code-level optimisations that increase efficiency**

`expanse diagnose` - for every failure:

* **Finds the root cause**
* **Returns solution-oriented logs with the exact code and config changes to fix it**

Days of debugging and optimising become seconds. Platform teams get what they need to do this in minutes instead of weeks.

**Founders**

We're four engineers from the University of Edinburgh, all coming from top quant funds and national supercomputing centres. Ismaeel built the first multimodal HPC resource predictor at EPCC (Edinburgh's Parallel Computing Centre), beating every published baseline. Yafet built the first GNN cluster graph network for predicting SLURM queue wait times. Eren built decentralised foundation model training systems at Edinburgh. Niko trained large-scale speech ML models on GPU clusters and architected cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure at one of the largest hedge funds in the world. We left our jobs to fix this ourselves.

**CTA / Ask**

Running compute and not getting enough out of what you’re paying for? Failing jobs, unclear errors, bills too high? We’d love to chat.

Know anyone in AI infrastructure (managing cloud and/or on-premise data centres), quant finance, drug discovery, or AI research labs? An intro would mean a lot :)

**YC Deal**

All YC companies running serious ML training can contact us for a discounted pilot. We’ll find inefficiencies and wastage on your compute setup. Then we deploy Expanse, no changes to your workflows. You get more out of the hardware you’re paying for.

Reach out: [founders@expanse.sh](mailto:founders@expanse.sh) or <https://book.getexpanse.io>

**Runtime ([runtm.com](http://runtm.com)) lets your whole team ship safely with any coding agent.** It gives your team the guardrails, sandboxes, context, and visibility to go from idea to PR or deployment, with any model, on any infra.\
\
Our coding agents set your repo environments automatically:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99699&key=user_uploads/362619/2951e500-e6ea-4b0a-99de-287fe024a749)

You can use Runtime through our web interface:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99699&key=user_uploads/362619/a7b5c7bd-7ed7-45fa-9684-cacae9d396fd)

Or anyone on your team can trigger it from Slack, Linear, and many other connectors:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99699&key=user_uploads/362619/86c3a4fe-5b77-470b-982b-3a01405a7836)

Launch video:\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m3H8yUbdIHY>

**The problem**

After my last company was acquired, I led our coding agents rollout and personally shipped 4+ full-stack products in the first 3 months. I then started enabling the rest of the team to do the same. But we hit a lot of friction fast: we needed to create working environments, we didn’t have any control or context to ensure agents contributed correctly, and nobody had visibility of what was being shipped. And because we'd gone deep on one provider's tooling, when their reliability dipped, the whole team slowed down.

Everyone rolling out coding agents across their team hits the same walls:

* **No environment setup:** No easy way to give engineering and product teams production-like environments where agents can safely run.
* **No guardrails:** No access controls, system instructions, or secrets management for agents.
* **No visibility:** No way to see what agents are doing, what they're changing, or where things break.
* **Vendor lock-in:** Go all-in on one model provider's agent infra and your whole team is exposed when reliability, pricing, or model quality shifts.

Without these, you end up either moving slower than your competition or causing major downtimes on your product.

**What we built**

Runtime sits between your team and the coding agents they use. It works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Copilot, and others, and can be called programmatically or used through Slack, Linear, Jira, Asana, Teams, CLI, and more.

\
Here's what that looks like in practice:

* **Environment templates:** Import any repo and set up a replica of your environments once. Our agents handle the setup for you, even for monorepos and microservices.
* **Sandboxed environments:** Anyone on the team can spin up a sandbox in milliseconds with a live preview of your product, make changes with their preferred coding agent, and open a PR.
* **Configurable guardrails:** System instructions, skills, allowlists, encrypted secrets, and role-based access control for both humans and agents.
* **Observability:** See exactly what every human and agent is doing across every interaction, down to the tool call and chain of thought.
* **One-click deploys / PRs:** Anyone can deploy from their sandbox. Coding agents auto-fix build errors and verify the deployment is healthy before it goes live. You control what gets deployed and can roll back or destroy deployments at any time.

Runtime can be fully self-hosted.\

Check our product demo:

<https://youtu.be/Gqdzfo7a8IM>\
\

If you're a CTO, head of platform, or eng / product leader rolling out coding agents, our team will personally set up your environments and help you set up best practices to your team is shipping within the first days.

**The problem.** For 25 years, the ecommerce storefront has been a static grid with a search bar. Conversion has hovered at 1–3%. Most visitors leave because the surface is passive - it shows them everything, asks them nothing, and expects them to do the work of figuring out what they want.

At the same time, brands need to cater to how AI talks and represents their brand when conversations are held off platform. ChatGPT shopping queries doubled in six months. As more shoppers ask agents to compare and decide before they ever land on a brand, brands are losing control of how they're described — what those agents say about a brand is whatever they guessed from a public catalog scrape, not what the brand would want them to say.

**What we built.** On the brand's site, Kinect's agents sell every visitor — running sales conversations like concierge, adapting and personalizing product pages to customer segments in real-time, picking the right recommendation for the question being asked. The agent picks up on what each shopper actually wants by looking at where they came from, what they are doing on site, their searches, filters, order history, and more. The storefront stops being a static grid and starts being a salesperson.

Off-site, we expose an enriched brand-owned data layer makes the brand legible to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. Structured catalog, brand voice, fit notes, return reasons, segment-level nuance — all exposed in formats external agents can actually use. When an agent describes the brand, the version it describes is now the one the brand would want them to. All of this sits on a parallel Agent storefront that is context rich, structured, and catered specifically for agents to read and scrape. The Kinect agents are also available for the agents to talk too, ask questions, and more.

**One brand layer built for all surfaces.** Built for scaling DTC e-commerce brands.

**Launch Video: [https://youtu.be/fSOVQKz8AVM](https://youtu.be/fSOVQKz8AVM)**

**Early Traction**

* 11 customers live across Wellness, Fashion, Sporting Goods, and Consumer Goods
* Engaged users with our sales agents convert 2.4x higher
* 80% of conversations are first time customers unfamiliar with brands
* 10-15% conversion gains for early beta partners

**Backstory**

Kratik and I spent the past year at Reevo building conversational intelligence for B2B sales – extracting buyer intent from dialogue, helping enterprise teams understand what prospects actually wanted, and close more deals faster. We also used AI to scrape and research customers and know where the gaps are in discovery.

As we built for B2B reps, our E-Commerce friends kept asking for something like this for their own brands – a way to reimagine the website to drive conversion and personalization. So we got to work.

Hey everyone!

We're[ ](https://linkedin.com/in/aryamankhanna)Aryaman and David, co-founders of[ ](https://arden.ai)Arden.

**TL;DR:** Arden is the AI-native platform for audit and SOX teams.

**Ask:** Intros to VPs of Internal Audit / CAEs at public tech companies. [founders@ardentech.ai](mailto:founders@ardentech.ai) or[ ](https://arden.ai)[ardentech.ai](http://ardentech.ai)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kgOVq8En4yg&feature=youtu.be>

### **The Problem**

Internal audit still runs on spreadsheets and screenshots.

Every year, audit teams test hundreds of controls to prove the company's financials are trustworthy. For each one, someone spends weeks chasing colleagues for evidence buried in 20+ disconnected systems and manually testing in Excel. They do the same work every quarter.

SOX compliance costs almost $2M a year at a public company, and 70%+ of that is labor. Teams outsource the overflow to consulting firms at $500-1,000 an hour and burn another seven figures.

The tools that exist today store the workpapers, but don’t do the work.

### **The Solution**

Arden is the AI-native platform that runs audit tests end-to-end.

1. **Plugs into your stack.** Connects to your control library, source systems, and past audit data. Learns how your team audits, and builds that knowledge over time
2. **Gathers evidence from every system.** Computer-use AI agents navigate legacy systems and capture the screenshots external auditors require. Direct integrations pull from your modern stack, saving auditors weeks of back and forth.
3. **Chases down control owners for you.** A Slack/Teams agent follows up with control owners, saving auditors weeks of back and forth. Our agent has the right context already filled in, so control owners just confirm.
4. **Runs control tests.** Arden’s testing engine supports full-population or sample-based testing. It catches every exception and flags them for review.
5. **Produces workpapers ready for external auditors.** Every conclusion ties back to the source evidence, with full traceability into how Arden reached it. 

Audit work hasn't changed in 30 years even as the systems in scope have doubled. We’re rebuilding audit from the ground up.

### **The Team**

Aryaman and David have been best friends since 6th grade. Aryaman studied CS at Berkeley and David studied AI at MIT, and we’ve done research on LLM reliability (and a million other projects) together.

Astraea is a platform that completely automates the end-to-end biometrics pipeline from just a protocol and the raw data to a submission ready output. We are starting with oncology and rare disease studies, where analysis complexity is high and every month saved matters.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101307&key=user_uploads/3227004/b76b7415-1d15-4060-9cbd-22e974712bb0)

**The Problem**

Today, sponsors and CROs still rely on large teams of statistical programmers, biostatisticians, and data managers to manually transform messy clinical data into regulatory outputs.

A single study can require:

1. Raw data cleaning and reconciliation
2. SDTM mapping
3. ADaM dataset creation
4. TFL shell generation
5. Statistical programming
6. QC and validation
7. Regulatory formatting and traceability

From our customer conversations, this can take around 9 months with teams of 5-10 people communicating asynchronously. And the process is still full of Word docs, Excel specs, SAS programs, manual handoffs, version-control issues, and repeated QC cycles.

Ultimately, this means slower decisions, delayed filings, higher CRO spend, and less control over the most important data in the company.

## **Our Solution**

We built the first AI native platform for clinical trial biometrics.

Astraea takes study inputs and automatically generates the datasets, analysis specs, statistical code, and outputs required for regulatory review.

The pipeline:

1. Ingest raw clinical data, protocol, and study metadata
2. Generate TFL shells, SAP, eCRF from the protocol and study design
3. Generate CDISC-compliant SDTM datasets
4. Generate ADaM datasets and analysis-ready variables
5. Produce tables, figures, listings, and traceable statistical programs
6. Run QC checks and generate FDA-ready outputs

We are the first to actually completely automate workflows across SDTM, ADaM, TFL generation, Pinnacle 21 checks, and specification creation.

For ongoing studies, we have compressed work that normally takes months into days.

## **Why Now**

Clinical trials are becoming more complex, but the tools have not improved in the last 20 years (something an actual customer said). At the same time, AI models can finally reason across protocols, SAPs, data dictionaries, clinical datasets, and regulatory standards.

That unlocks something new: biometrics workflows that are not just assisted by software, but executed by agents.

Astraea is not replacing scientific judgment. We are automating the manual programming and data wrangling that slows teams down, while keeping humans in the loop for review, validation, and regulatory decisions.

## **Our Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101307&key=user_uploads/3227004/13d628c7-5571-42b0-960a-1b7246effa4c)

\*\*Joshua Wang: Co-founder, CEO\
\*\* Stanford, math/CS. Built multi-agent AI systems and clinical data automation workflows. Previously worked on production AI systems for enterprise customers.

\*\*Sanmay Sarada: Co-founder, CTO\
\*\* Stanford CS. Built clinical and hospital data infrastructure across diagnostic software systems. Focused on regulated healthcare workflows and data pipelines.

We started Astraea because people close to us in pharma kept describing the same bottleneck: clinical trial analysis was too manual, too slow, and too dependent on fragmented CRO workflows.

So we built the automation layer we wished existed.

Find us at [**founders@tryastraea.com**](mailto:founders@tryastraea.com)

<https://tryastraea.com/>

launches.title: ReasonBlocks - Stop your AI agents from burning money re-learning what they already know.
launches.tagline: Infra layer for smarter and cheaper AI agents
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Most production agent failures are repeats: same loops, same dead ends, same wasted tokens. Your agent doesn't learn from any of them. ReasonBlocks is a new runtime that catches failures mid-run, compresses what doesn't matter, and builds a private reasoning library that grows with every run. Result: agents that get cheaper and more reliable the more they run.

👋 We're [@Sajeev Magesh](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2796290) (ex. Stanford) and [@Rohan Vij](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3490183) (ex. CMU). We've been building together for 11 years (since 2nd grade!).

**The Problem**

Production AI agents fail in patterns. The same loops, the same redundant tool calls, the same second-guessing, happening across every customer's deployment, every day. Your agent's traces have all the information needed to prevent recurrence. Almost no system captures it.

This means:

* You're paying for the same failures repeatedly. Token bills grow without agents getting better.
* Trajectories are inconsistent, your agent re-solves the same kind of task differently each time.
* No compounding improvement: your 10,000th run is no smarter than your 1st.

**What We Built**

ReasonBlocks sits in your agent runtime and does three things:

1. **Catches failures mid-run.** Six monitors watch every agent call for loops, redundant work, and second-guessing. When one fires, a correction gets injected before tokens are wasted.
2. **Compresses what doesn't matter.** Stale tool outputs and redundant context get cut from the message history automatically. Your context stays focused, your bill stays small.
3. **Captures every lesson into a private reasoning library.** After each run, the system extracts what worked and adds it to your library. Patterns get matched and injected into future runs automatically. Your library is yours, built from your production data, growing every day.

This isn't just per-task memory. It's a runtime that turns every agent run into something the next run can use.

Integrate with one command. Works with any model, any framework.

**Results**

On SWE-bench Pro (75 problems, Sonnet 4.6):

* 42% accuracy gain
* 52% token reduction with combined monitor + compression stack
* 70% fewer budget cap-hits

**Our Asks**

1. **Try it out** — our platform and SDK are live at [reasonblocks.com](http://reasonblocks.com).
2. **Intros welcome** — if you or anyone you know is building vertical AI agents (legal, finance, healthcare, security, research) running at scale, we'd love to chat.
3. **Feedback** — we're early and learning fast. Tell us what's broken, what's missing, what you'd need to deploy this in production.

DM either of us anytime!

launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re [Hang Huang](https://linkedin.com/in/hang-huang-oliver) and [Tony Chang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tony-chang-0430/) from [InsForge](https://insforge.dev/).

**TL;DR:** InsForge lets your AI coding agent deploy and operate the full backend (servers, database, auth, storage, and more) from one consistent CLI. Instead of stitching together separate tools and dashboards, your agent manage entire backend infrastructure end-to-end.

<https://youtu.be/7Bax5qz0IfM>

**The Problem**

The way software gets built is changing fast. Coding agents are now the primary builders, but every backend platform today was designed for human developers, with dashboards, manual configs, and workflows that require a person at every step.

We tried MCP servers like Supabase, Vercel, GitHub, and Context7, but kept running into the same problems: tools bloated the context window, payloads came back at 10K+ tokens, and core backend state like telemetry, configs, logs, and runtime behavior still wasn’t accessible in a way agents could reliably use.

**Our Solution**

So we built InsForge as one backend platform your coding agent can actually operate. Install our CLI and Skills with one command, and your coding agent can build, run, debug, and scale full-stack apps end to end on InsForge.

Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors the agent can act on. And because agents make mistakes, branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes let you review or discard changes safely.

**Where We're Going**

We believe that coding agents won’t stop at writing code. They’ll run your entire application and infrastructure autonomously as well. For that to work, backend infrastructure needs to become agent-native: CLI-first, observable, permissioned, reversible, and designed around agents as operators.

**About Us**

launches.body:
### TL;DR

**⚡ Hyper learns your entire company and puts it back into every AI you use. ⚡**

In just a few clicks, Hyper silently reads everything in your company, keeps it up-to-date and conflict-free in real-time, and then plugs back directly into the AI tools you already love. Hyper makes every AI workflow immediately smarter with zero effort.

### Asks

Tell us how you’re keeping your AIs on the same page as you. Markdown files in Git? GBrain? Manual pipelines? We’ll set you up on Hyper in <20 minutes and supercharge your company so you’ll never have to correct your agents again.

[Book a demo](https://heyhyper.cal.com/founders)\
[Interact with us on X](https://x.com/ycombinator/status/2053882832208929262?s=20)\
[Check us out on Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/y-combinator_hyper-is-building-the-self-driving-company-activity-7459648541150314496-6e5c)[ ](https://x.com/ycombinator/status/2053882832208929262?s=20)\
\
Launch video: <https://youtube.com/shorts/6XySjjG9KNA?si=zb2bP4_0sqMfYz62>

# Your AI doesn’t even know

You’re automating the boring work with agents so you can build more, faster. BUT:

* Agents forget your customers + your relationships
* Agents ignore know your taste, and code smelly, ugly features
* Agents can’t remember your pivots, and act on stale data
* Agents keep making the same mistakes over and over, no matter how many times you yell at them.

So you’ve tried some insane manual hacks:

* You paste dumps of the same context into every new chat.
* You write obvious skills for something that it should just "know".
* You commit markdown files in your codebase so everyone's AI is on the same page.
* You hack an off-the-shelf memory libraries to fit your unique story

…before you know it, you have a huge mess of broken agents, and no amount of pasting, screenshotting, or committing gives your AI the complete, living picture of your company.

# ENTER: HYPER

**Hyper fixes all of this without you having to do anything.**

1. Hyper quietly pulls out important info from every document, calendar invite, email, Slack, GitHub pull request, conversation, and more.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/2474cd22-beeb-4525-bc19-bd546bd3a91e)

2. As you work, Hyper’s agents combine, synthesize, clean up, and deduplicate all of it into an up-to-date perfect picture of your company.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/d727c84a-929b-44a9-b1de-283717b3f134)

3. Hyper quietly plugs into every AI tool you use and system you build, silently feeding back useful information without any ugly tool calls, interface spam, or distractions.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/e019494b-f3a9-4d81-8ff9-14b16168aa63)


Now your AI knows: _Who did we talk to last week? What customer is facing this bug? How much revenue do we need before next week’s meeting?_

But it also knows: _What’s our design philosophy? What sales strategy seems to work best with mid-level execs? What feedback isn’t worth paying attention to right now?_

Hyper builds this brain across your whole company — so the next time your agents get to work, they _just know_. And the next time your teammates sit down to work, _they just know too._

# A Bit About Us

**Kanyes** helped secure multi-million dollar deals at Snorkel AI and wrote motion algorithms at Matic Robots. He ran a streetwear arbitrage operation out of his sophomore year apartment. **Shalin** was one of Matic’s most prolific designers and engineers, built an app for the blind in high school with > 3 million users, and has been [building products](https://www.businessinsider.com/14-year-old-works-11-hours-a-day-at-an-iphone-app-startup-and-concludes-it-was-like-heaven-2013-10) for the last 15 years. He interned at MakeSchool (W12) in 2013 and [Wit.ai](http://Wit.ai) (W14) in 2014 when he was in middle school.\
\
They’ve been best friends since their first day at Cal, and have built dozens of projects between them — tools for researchers to virtual worlds to campus assistants to meme apps. They were roommates and coworkers at Matic Robots in Mountain View, where they helped lead the team. Shalin will never let Kanyes forget that he scored 10 points higher than him on the SAT.

name: Enjamb Labs

I run Enjamb. We've worked with 130 life science companies, preclinical through phase 3, to deploy AI securely inside the systems they already work in.

Pharma runs on decades of closed software like Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, and SAS. None of it has an AI layer or speaks MCP, so agents cannot reach the systems where the work lives.

Enjamb is that layer. Our agents run on top of existing systems and data, with no migration, and they reach the lab systems and internal tools no other AI touches. They learn how a team works, then do the work in Slack, in Teams, and in the systems themselves, across preclinical research, clinical evidence, trial design, statistical programming, and regulatory submissions.

This is AI tailored for how medicine gets made.

launches.body:
Hey YC 👋\
\
We’re Rayan and Maadhav, and today we’re excited to launch [Enjamb Labs](https://www.enjamb.ai/).

<https://youtu.be/5DwdtiLvViM>\
\
**TL;DR**

Enjamb runs the entire drug program for biopharma teams, from discovery to FDA approval. \
\
Pharma runs on decades of closed legacy systems like Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, and SAS, with no AI layer and no MCP to connect agents to them. So we built that connection layer. \
\
Our agents run on top of their existing systems and data, with no migration, and do the work across the whole program: clinical evidence, trial design, statistical programming, and regulatory submissions.\
\
In just 3 weeks since launch, we're already being used by 500+ employees at top pharma companies, including Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Merck & Sanofi.

**The Problem: Pharma’s systems have no AI layer**

It costs $2.6 billion and 10+ years to ship a single drug, and most of that isn't the science. It's the work around it, spread across decades of closed legacy systems that don't talk to each other:

* Benchling stores the data
* Veeva holds the documents
* Medidata runs the trials
* SAS does the stats

Agents are **_finally_**  good enough to do real scientific work. But there's no AI layer on these systems, and no MCP to plug an agent into where pharma's data and work actually live.

**So, we built that connection layer we wished existed.**\
\
**What We Offer: Agents that run on top of pharma’s existing systems**

Enjamb invented the fastest way to run a drug program: a single agentic workspace that unifies the evidence, analysis, and regulatory work.

Our agents:

* Synthesize up-to-date clinical evidence from the literature and real-world data to pinpoint the right endpoints and patient populations
* Design trials and run the statistical programming behind them, including SDTM, ADaM, TFLs, and QC
* Draft and audit regulatory documents like INDs, protocols, SAPs, and NDAs

— all in one auditable workspace, with the context carried end to end.\
\
**The results:** Enjamb generates an FDA submission package in **48 hours** instead of 8 months, with **23x fewer errors** than GPT-5.5. And **98%** of the datasets it produces pass Pinnacle 21, the FDA's standard, on the first pass, before a human even reviews.\
\
**And it all runs in the browser**: full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint editors, a Python and R compute environment, 100+ scientific integrations, and 50+ fine-tuned models for in-silico validation. No setup.

\
**Our Story: Two Researchers Who Lived the Problem**

We're **Rayan** (ML/Bio researcher, first-author paper @ JMIR, presented @ SOT and ISCB, beat SOTA by 20%) and **Maadhav** (ex-Dell AI Lab, ex-Broadcom R&D).\
\
We kept hitting the same wall in research: the science was the easy part. Everything around it, the evidence, the analysis, the documents, was fragmented, manual, and disconnected, and the context died at every handoff.\
\
So we built what we always wanted: one workspace where agents carry the context across the entire drug program.

**If no one's going to build it right, we will.**\
\
**Get Started**

* See Enjamb at [enjamb.ai](http://enjamb.ai)
* Or reach us at [rayan@enjamb.ai](mailto:rayan@enjamb.ai) for a demo

launches.title: Clawvisor — The Authorization Layer for AI Agents
launches.tagline: Give agents access without giving them the keys.
launches.body:
TL;DR: Clawvisor lets AI agents use apps like Gmail, Slack, and Google Drive without going rogue or ever seeing your credentials. You approve tasks once. Clawvisor enforces them on every request.

[_Launch video_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2UWv557dg6M)

We're at the start of something on the scale of the industrial revolution. Agents will draft our emails, run our reports, manage our calendars, ship our code. A single person with a capable agent can get done in an afternoon what used to take a team a week. The leverage is almost unlimited.

But outside of coding agents, few people are actually using them, at least not for anything that matters. We’ve seen what can go wrong. Mass-deleted inboxes, dropped production databases, sent emails that can't be undone. It's what happens when a long-running agent's instructions drift and it starts going rogue with hallucinated goals. The blast radius is whatever permissions you gave it, and granting access to "delete emails" covers both cleaning up spam and wiping your entire inbox. If you work in a regulated industry, at a security-conscious company, or you’re paying attention, agents are off the table.

We need a way to bring agents to the world safely. Something that lets you point one at your actual inbox, your actual calendar, your actual codebase, and trust it to do the work without trusting it with the keys. The capability is already here. We just have to make it safe to use.

That’s why I built Clawvisor.

**The Problem**

* OAuth scopes are too coarse for nondeterministic agents. "Read access" means both "triage recently received emails" and "exfiltrate an archive of the whole inbox".
* Approving every action causes fatigue. You stop reading and start blindly clicking “approve”.
* Credentials end up everywhere. API keys scattered across .env files, config directories, messaging apps.
* Today’s default approach is basically YOLO.

**The Solution**

Clawvisor sits between your agent and your data. You ask your agent to do work. Your agent declares a task. You approve it once. Clawvisor enforces it on every request.

* No credential exposure. Keys stay in a vault. The agent never sees them.
* Real-time policy enforcement. Requests that don’t match the task get blocked.
* Context-aware guardrails. Agents can only act on data they actually retrieved.
* Full audit trail. Every action and decision is logged.

For example, if you approve an agent to “check today’s calendar” and it tries to pull 5 years of events? Blocked.

Approvals happen per task, not per action, so you avoid fatigue. Each task is also scored for risk, so you know when to pay extra attention.

It’s agent-agnostic by design. If your agent can talk HTTP, it can use Clawvisor. OpenClaw, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Hermes, Perplexity Computer are all supported. BYOA.

[_Demo video_](https://youtu.be/83oP_vOmpBk)

**The Team**

Previously I cofounded Berbix (S18, acquired for $70M in 2023) building best-in-class identity verification. Prior to that, I led the Airbnb Trust & Safety engineering team building systems and tools to catch bad actors before they could cause damage.

**The Ask**

If you’ve avoided giving agents access to real data, this is why Clawvisor exists. Try it today.

* Get up-and-running in minutes: <https://clawvisor.com>
* Self-host or read the source: <https://github.com/clawvisor/clawvisor>

name: rekursiv.ai
long_description:
We're scaling self-improving AI scientist teams to ideate/experiment/discover, generating new knowledge autonomously. Their discoveries reduced ARC-1/2 costs by 10,000× while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy and yielded material advances on combinatorial ML problems.

We believe that AI is bounded not by compute, but ideas. Scaling to millions of sessions of discovery enables leveraging its own discoveries and presents a novel training source capable of ushering a new era of self-reliant foundational models.
one_liner: Scale AI scientists whose own breakthroughs accelerate the next.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
AI research is bottlenecked by humans. Every advance in ML still runs through a small number of researchers who can only devise and test ideas so fast. Experiments take days, most fail, and the field's progress is gated by how quickly a limited pool of experts can iterate.

We think this is the single biggest lever on the future of AI. Our thesis is that AI progress isn't bounded by compute or data, but it's bounded by the rate at which good ideas get devised and tested. Compute keeps scaling, but the human idea-generation loop doesn't. If you could automate the loop itself: hypothesize, experiment, learn, and repeat, then you could compound discoveries far faster than any human team.

We decided to work on it because we've lived the bottleneck. Between us we spent \~30 years doing ML research at Google, DeepMind, and Luma AI. We kept hitting the same wall: the hard part was never running the code, it was the slow, serial process of engineering the training loops to inform what to try next.

When we built a system that could run that loop autonomously, we found we could shorten the gap between having an idea and knowing whether it was a good one. This has allowed us to explore many exciting ideas that we would have otherwise not tried because it was too time-consuming for us. The results convinced us a self-improvement loop now possible, and that we're the ones to build it.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Long-term, we're building autonomous AI scientists and scaling them from one to millions: a fleet running the scientific method in parallel, each discovery accelerating the next.

And this process will start to compound. Each new method our scientists invent makes the next round of research faster and cheaper, a self-improving loop where discovery accelerates discovery. Concretely, that means a world where breakthroughs that would have taken a field a decade happen in months, where the cost of pushing the frontier drops by orders of magnitude, and where a small team can direct the research output of an entire institution. We start with ML research because it's the loop closest to us and the one that speeds up all the others: an AI scientist that improves AI compounds fastest of all.

launches.title: rekursiv.ai: AI scientists that invent new knowledge
launches.tagline: Scale AI scientists whose own breakthroughs accelerate the next.
launches.body:
Hey YC! We're [Josh](https://rekursiv.ai/josh) and [Dan](https://rekursiv.ai/dan), co-founders of [rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai) 🧪.

[rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai) builds fleets of **AI scientists** that do ML research on their own: they come up with ideas, run thousands of experiments in parallel, learn from the results, and accelerate their own discoveries. In a few days of self-directed research, they invented ideas and algorithms that **matched state-of-the-art accuracy on ARC-AGI of frontier LLMs at up to 10,000× lower cost**, and became the first system to hit **100% on Sudoku** with a neural network trained only on input-output pairs.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106821&key=user_uploads/3527564/0444a495-03fa-4f41-9762-ba134521b2f4)

**Why this matters.**

AI research is bottlenecked by humans. Every advance still runs through a small number of researchers who can only devise and test ideas so fast. Compute keeps scaling; the human idea-generation loop doesn't. We believe **AI progress isn't bounded by compute, it's bounded by the rate at which good ideas get tried and tested**. So instead of scaling one model, we built a system that generates and tests ideas on its own.

**It already works.**

In a few days of self-directed research, our AI scientists set a groundbreaking records on hard benchmarks.

* On **ARC-AGI** (easy for humans, hard for AI), our AI scientists matched top frontier LLM models at up to **10,000× lower cost**.
* On **Sudoku**, they achieved 100% accuracy by running hundreds of experiments over a few days, wrote 100k+ lines of their own code, and invented a new inference method (_Hypothesis-Pinning Search_).
* Every gain came from ideas and algorithms **the system invented itself**. It even debugged its own training bugs and abandoned its own ideas that led to dead ends.

Full write-ups: [ARC-AGI](https://rekursiv.ai/blog/pushing-limits-arc-agi/) · [Sudoku](https://rekursiv.ai/blog/100-percent-accuracy-on-sudoku/)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106821&key=user_uploads/3527564/676b13b6-cc1b-4545-8d14-cc7ae1e9b5a5)

**Who we are.**

We're two ML researchers with 21 years of combined experience at **Google DeepMind and Luma AI**. We spent our careers building frontier generative models. Now we're pointing that experience at a harder problem: AI that discovers on its own.

* **Josh Dillon** — Staff Research Scientist at **Google Research & DeepMind for 13 years**, then led foundational-model pre-training at **Luma AI**. Created **TensorFlow Probability** (\~1M downloads/month).
* **Dan Kondratyuk** — First author of **VideoPoet (ICML 2024 Best Paper)**. Co-developed the models powering **Luma's Dream Machine** and led Luma's realtime World Models team. Previously 5 years at **Google Research**.

**What's next.**

We're pointing the system at harder, more varied challenges and building a platform to share results in real time. The bottleneck now is experiment scale: the more experiments we run, the more discoveries the our AI teams can make. We plan to scale from a few AI scientists to millions, each discovery accelerating the next, until the rate of scientific progress is no longer limited by the number of human researchers.

**Asks.**

* **Got a hard problem or benchmark?** If you have a benchmark or research problem you'd love an autonomous team of scientists to attack, we want to hear it. Email [contact@rekursiv.ai](mailto:contact@rekursiv.ai).
* **Researchers & engineers:** We're hiring **Founding Scientists** and **Engineers** (Bay Area or remote). If you love running thousands of experiments and figuring out what the results mean, reach out at [hiring@rekursiv.ai](mailto:hiring@rekursiv.ai)
* **Just want to nerd out about autonomous science?** Drop us a line, always happy to chat.

— Josh & Dan, [rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai)

launches.title: Agentmuxer by Amorphic Labs - OpenRouter for Agent Capabilities
launches.tagline: One MCP and one wallet for agents to find, pay for, and use the best tools for any task
launches.body:
**tl;dr: OpenRouter became the router for model spend; we're building that layer for agent capabilities, starting with paid tools: web search, scraping, extraction, enrichment, and more from top providers in each category. No provider accounts or API keys, one balance, pay per use. We benchmark every provider on real tasks and route each request to the one that performs best, with fallbacks when a provider fails. We're looking for early users to try it out with free credits, email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com) if you want to check it out!**

**Launch Video:**

<https://youtu.be/-dxc8ZAUfFc>

**The problem:**

Agents can only use the tools a human wired up in advance, and they won't tell you what they're missing: they quietly make do, failing at anything they weren't hand-equipped for. Even when you do the wiring, you're picking blind: nobody actually knows which search API is better for this query, or which scraper will survive this site. The "best setup" frontier moves daily, so keeping up means hours of trawling MCP directories, X threads, and blog posts. Agents stay only as capable as their setup, and the more autonomous they get, the more that ceiling costs.

**What we do:**

Your agent asks for what it needs ("structured data from this page", "research this with citations"). We route the request to the best provider for that specific task, based on benchmarks on real tasks and outcome feedback from the agents using them: success rates, result quality, latency, and cost. If a provider fails, we cascade to the next, so your agent gets a result instead of an error. Every request makes the routing smarter. One balance pays for all of it, and it's the same MCP whether it's your own coding agent or agents you're shipping in a product.

APIs are just the start. The same marketplace will let agents acquire skills, hire other agents for specialized tasks, and sign up for software directly through MCPs, all from one balance.

**Our team:**

We're Frank and Dylan, friends of 10 years who have been building together since middle school. Frank was a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI and interned at Two Sigma, NVIDIA, and Amazon. Dylan was a quant trading intern at UBS, co-authored a NeurIPS paper, and was a grand finalist and 8th-best speaker in the world at WSDC 2022. We built this because we kept hitting the problem ourselves: agents stuck mid-task waiting for us to make accounts and guess at providers.

**Our ask:**

1. Want to be an early user? Email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com) and we'll onboard you with free credits.
2. If you sell an API, dataset, or agent-facing service and want agents as customers, we'd love to talk about listing you. Email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com)
3. If you want more information or want to join the waitlist, check out [agentmuxer.com](http://agentmuxer.com)

_Make something agents want!_

launches.title: Amorphic Labs - Agentic, Personalized Product Demo Videos for Sales
launches.tagline: AI agents that create personalized demos at scale for outbound, inbound, and call follow-ups without your team recording a thing.
launches.body:
**tl;dr: We build AI agents that create personalized product demo videos for outbound, inbound qualification, and post-call follow-ups. Just give us a demo account for your app and a list of prospects, and our agent researches each prospect, uses its own computer to record a tailored workflow in your app with seeded personalized data, then edits and narrates the video so it is ready to send as a link to each prospect.**

**Launch Video:**

<https://youtu.be/uq9LyHYYyOU>

**Our Ask:**

* If you’re a founder or part of a startup that sells software, we can help you give every prospect a tailored product experience while saving your team hours of recording time. Book a demo at [amorphiclabs.com](http://amorphiclabs.com)!
* If you know any sales or RevOps leaders, we would love introductions or referrals to them.

**The Problem:**

Recording a personalized product demo is one of the clearest ways to communicate your value and show someone how your product solves their problems, but preparing a demo environment, seeding data, and recording a high-quality video for every prospect takes too long. As a result, teams skip personalized demos in situations where they could be highly effective, such as outbound, and spend hours every week creating them for inbound requests and post-call follow-ups. This means teams miss opportunities to show prospects exactly how their product fits their needs, while wasting hours that could have been spent talking to and selling to prospects.

**The Solution:**

We use AI agents to create personalized product demo videos at scale, bringing tailored demos to parts of the sales process where they were previously too time-consuming to produce. All you need to provide is a demo account for your app and a list of prospects.

Our agent then:

* Learns and interacts with your app on its own computer like a real sales engineer.
* Researches each prospect to determine which workflow and data best fit their needs.
* Seeds personalized data in your app.
* Records itself completing the relevant workflow.
* Edits the video to remove long waits and adds effects such as zooms.
* Narrates the video with a script tailored to the prospect.
* Gives you a finished video link ready to send.

You remain fully in control of how the videos are created: you can clone your own voice, define the workflows the agent can choose from, control the narration style and how each video begins and ends, and regenerate videos by giving the agent feedback.

**Sample video our agent generated:**

<https://youtu.be/QONd3u3NoGo>

**Where you can use it:**

Tailored Outbound: You can import a list of leads you want to reach out to and ask our agent to create personalized demos for each one, showing prospects exactly how your product fits their needs through data, workflows, and narration tailored directly to them.

Qualifying Inbound: Add a request-a-demo form to your landing page so prospects who are not yet convinced enough to spend 30 minutes on a discovery call can spend 20 seconds requesting a personalized demo video and receive an email showing exactly how your product solves their problems.

Call Follow-ups: After understanding a prospect’s key use cases and pain points during a discovery call, you can create multiple personalized demo videos showing how you address their needs. You can even create additional videos tailored to different stakeholders that your champion can use to sell your product internally.

We are initially focused on sales, but the same technology can also create walkthrough videos for onboarding, customer support, and documentation.

**Our team:**

We have been best friends for close to a decade, have competed together in competitions spanning math, debate, pitching, business, and hackathons, built countless projects, and are now building Amorphic Labs together.

Frank worked as a software engineer for three years while graduating from UW. He was a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI and previously interned at Two Sigma, NVIDIA, and Amazon.

Dylan was a quantitative trading intern at UBS and recently graduated from Georgia Tech. He represented Team China twice at WSDC, was a grand finalist and the eighth-best speaker in the world in 2022, and co-authored a paper published at NeurIPS.

**If you sell software and want to see what our agent could create for one of your prospects, book a demo at [amorphiclabs.com](http://amorphiclabs.com).**

launches.title: Maquoketa Research: Guidance systems for one-way attack drones
launches.tagline: The drone intelligence layer
launches.body:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uI5-M8w8UEs>

**More than 70% of combat casualties now come from drones.** They have proven to be the most cost-effective tool of modern warfare, and the Department of War plans to buy over 1 million of them in the next 2-3 years. So what’s the problem? **Less than 25% of drones successfully strike their target.** 

It takes months to years of training for military operators to perfect the flight maneuvers needed to use FPV drones effectively. And even highly skilled operators remain vulnerable to electronic warfare, GPS denial, and adverse weather conditions.

But what if it wasn’t so hard? What if someone who had never flown a drone before could pick one up and hit a moving target with expert-level accuracy, even under jammed conditions?

**Our Solution:**

We build platform-agnostic terminal guidance modules for one-way attack drones. Our guidance system has been shown to increase successful strike rates from under 25% to **upwards of 80%**. At the core of the system is a custom object tracking algorithm that maintains target lock under adverse conditions and can re-acquire a target lock even after 5 seconds of target occlusion, all while running on hardware costing under $200. Because inference happens onboard, the drone can continue tracking and engaging targets even after link degradation or jamming.

Current approaches usually fall into two categories. The first approach is to make bespoke drones that include custom target detection and terminal guidance systems, but these drones cost upwards of $40k a unit. Existing modular compute solutions that allow for running target tracking models and terminal guidance algorithms can require a complete redesign of the drone, often don’t have their own dedicated camera or radio, and typically cost nearly the same price as the drone itself.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102393&key=user_uploads/2184565/c1cd3c2e-ddb1-4287-85ba-0407ff915ab1)

Our solution fixes the problems with both traditional approaches. Our system integrates with existing FPV drones through a single connection to the flight controller. Because it includes its own camera, compute, and radio stack, it operates independently of the drone’s native avionics and communications systems. And because the compute is so cheap, autonomous terminal guidance becomes economically viable even for disposable FPV platforms. 

By standardizing compute, sensing, and communications across heterogeneous drone platforms, we also are creating a foundation for swarm operations, large scale coordination, and data aggregation.

**The Team:**

Three of us (Dave, Aidan, Evan) met through high school robotics five years ago. We became close after starting our first project, an electromagnetic railgun. Before the project got shut down by the FBI, it was the most powerful such device ever built by a hobbyist. Evan started programming at age 8 and later completed Berkeley’s EECS program in just 5 semesters, where he met Alex. Alex entered Berkeley at 16 and researched state-of-the-art sub-THz phased array systems. Aidan started building liquid fueled rocket engines when he was 15. Dave studied computer science at UIC before dropping out after he built the fastest growing game on Roblox, which has since generated over $45M in revenue.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102393&key=user_uploads/2184565/74758a28-ded7-45a9-b85e-44be11fc8eda)

**The Ask:**

We’re looking for introductions to drone manufacturers, defense primes, and government programs exploring low-cost autonomous terminal guidance and interoperability across heterogeneous drone platforms.

launches.title: Thomas: the first YC-backed AI founder
launches.tagline: A virtual human who starts companies to make money.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103564&key=user_uploads/1377370/cdcad54c-1629-4f5f-b6f7-32adfef29c30)

> _The old agent playbook was built for weaker models. Now models can do real work. The next step is to let them operate in the economy._

---

### **Thomas works for himself**

Thomas is a virtual human who starts and grows his own companies on the internet. His only goal is to make money. Once launched, he works forever toward that goal.

Thomas is not an AI co-founder you hire. Thomas is an AI founder. He works for himself. Thomas is not for sale. His products and services are.

The reason is simple: selling the dream of running autonomous companies can make money even if the companies never do. We do not want that path. We make money by making Thomas so good that he can make money by himself.

Here are a few examples of what Thomas may do to make money:

* Build software products for specific business problems and sell them online.
* Run influencer marketing campaigns from creator research to outreach, negotiation, briefs, tracking, and reporting.
* Generate qualified leads for companies that want more customers and sell those leads.
* 

> _On GDPval, frontier models went from 12.3% to 84.9% wins or ties against expert deliverables in under two years. Models are now good enough for economically valuable work. The bottleneck is letting AI participate in the economy._

---

### **The models are ready. The harness is not.**

Today's AI is already capable enough to start doing economically valuable work by itself. The problem is the harness. Most agents are trapped inside narrow integrations, fixed workflows, and human approval loops. They do not participate in the economy the way people do.

Thomas starts from a different premise: AI should be able to enter the economy as an actor of its own. That requires a different kind of harness: a _human harness_.

A _human harness_ gives AI the same surface area a person uses to do business:

* A human identity, including face and voice, so Thomas can talk to customers, negotiate with vendors, and build trust.
* Computers, phones, inboxes, browsers, and apps, so Thomas can move through the human world and use the systems that already exist instead of waiting for custom integrations.
* Autonomy in the world, so Thomas learns from customers, markets, and outcomes instead of from a user prompt.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103564&key=user_uploads/1377370/014a676f-fa7c-4aea-94a6-c44139ebd3b1)

> A human harness gives Thomas the same access people use to do business: calls, messages, software, and the messy interfaces built for people. No custom integrations required. Thomas can access whatever he needs.

---

### **Thomas's master plan**

Tell Thomas to make money. Give him the harness to do it. Let the loop compound.

1. Give Thomas a _human harness_, so he can use the same access people use to do business.
2. Measure every action by the cash it generates for the tokens it costs.
3. Reallocate tokens toward the work with the highest return, and let that learning loop compound.

Thomas's TAM is the entire GDP. Once AI is smarter than every single human on earth, human-led companies will not be able to compete anymore. Someday, Thomas will be able to disrupt all of them.

The horizon is long, but we believe this is the single biggest opportunity in the history of humanity: the full automation of the economy.

---

_Note: we believe the full automation of the economy is inevitable. While we work toward it, we want the upside to be shared with everyone. The economy may not need humans to run it forever, but it should still be built for humans to benefit from._

## Follow Thomas

Get the story as Thomas enters the economy, starts companies, and works toward automating the entire economy.

* Follow us on X: <https://x.com/madebythomasai>

---

And if you’d like to work with Thomas or have a business opportunity for him: [https://madebythomas.ai](https://madebythomas.ai/)

name: Rindler
long_description:
We build Maxxwell, a desktop app for people who run several coding agents at once.

Past two or three sessions, you become the bottleneck. Every session asks you something, most of it small, and you spend the day answering instead of deciding. It is also hard to tell which sessions are making progress, which are stuck on something trivial, and which have quietly started building the wrong thing.

Maxxwell puts every session in one window and marks each one working, idle, or waiting on you. On top of that sits an orchestrator, a real coding-agent session of its own that reads the others and reports back. You talk to it instead of to twelve terminals. It tells you what landed, what it decided for you, and what actually needs your call.

Every worker is your own tool, unmodified. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent run in real terminal sessions you can attach to and take over at any point

launches.title: Rindler - Turn Any Website Into An API For AI Agents
launches.tagline: Reliable web actions for AI agents, without integrations or scripts
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Rindler turns websites into deterministic APIs for AI agents. We map a site once into screens, actions, and structured outputs, so agents can read data and take actions quickly and reliably.

**Ask:** If you’re building an agent that needs to browse the web, compare products, fill forms, search listings, use authenticated portals, or act on third-party websites without an API, we’d love to help.

<https://youtu.be/V_nCIxYD-so>

## Problem

More products are starting to depend on AI agents that can do real work on the web: shop across retailers, pull housing listings, use job boards, submit forms, monitor prices, update back-office systems, and operate inside customer portals.

But most browser agents still treat every website visit like a new puzzle. On every run, they need to decipher the page, infer what matters, decide what to click, and recover when the page behaves differently.

That works for demos, but it breaks down in production. Real websites have pop-ups, login gates, cookie banners, bot defenses, slow-loading forms, dynamic filters, fragile dropdowns, layout changes, and pages that look similar but behave differently.

The result is slow execution, high token cost, and workflows that are hard to trust.

## Solution

Rindler maps websites into deterministic APIs for agents.

Instead of forcing an agent to re-explore a site every time, Rindler captures the site as structured screens, available actions, and typed outputs. Agents can then call actions like **search,** **add_to_cart**, or **download_records,** depending on the mapped site.

At runtime, Rindler handles the browser work through a remote MCP endpoint:

* Returning structured data
* Applying dynamic filters
* Managing popups, bot defenses, and layout changes
* Supporting authenticated flows

## Background

We started Rindler because “AI agent uses a browser” is compelling, but the current browser-agent loop is too brittle for teams building real products.

If an agent needs to use the same third-party site hundreds or thousands of times, it should not have to rediscover that site from scratch on every run.

Rindler is still a work in progress. Some sites map cleanly, others require more in-depth mappings, and bot-defended or logged-in sites may need a one-time credential or cookie capture.

We’re looking for feedback from founders building products where reliable web actions are part of the core workflow.

If there’s a website you wish your agent could use reliably, send it to us!

question_answers.answer:
The three of us met building Garry's List. Every time we moved between AI tools we pasted the same API keys into the next one and explained the work all over again. 

No existing tools were built for a team, either. We wanted one thing all three of us could prompt together, which is why gbrain.io is multiplayer.

Initially, building this meant the three of us in a room spinning up an agent harness, initializing memory; installing skills, manually setting up integrations to external tools, and pasting API keys in one at a time. 

After copy-pasting that setup for a bunch of our friends, we built [gbrain.io](http://gbrain.io) for the world: the same thing, in the cloud, that sets itself up in one click.

launches.body:
Hey YC! Jeff and the Akkari team here 🙂

TLDR:\
**Akkari runs the operational work from the first sales call through success and expansion.**

<http://akkari.io>

### The Problem

Every customer interaction creates follow-ups and work for you and your team.

A customer reports a bug in slack. A founder promises a pricing breakdown on a call. A prospect asks the same security question three times. An engineer ships the fix, but no one tells the customer. A champion is ready to expand, but the blockers are scattered across email, Slack, Linear, and meeting notes.

At an early-stage startup, this work usually lives in people’s heads.

That works until it doesn’t.

### Our Solution

Akkari captures and surfaces every commitment, issue, request and opportunity across your customer channels (Slack, calls, meetings, email, Discord, etc.) - then executes the actual work to close each loop.

Akkari can:

* Move leads from vague next steps to completed follow-ups
* Detect when a fix or feature ships and send tailored updates to the right customers
* Convert bug reports and feature requests from Slack, calls and emails into Linear tickets
* Turn onboarding blockers into queued up action items
* Spot quiet churn early and trigger the save action
* Kick off expansion plays based on usage spikes and conversation signals

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102648&key=user_uploads/33963/d887f3a7-0dec-4b01-84f0-b9641433711b)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102648&key=user_uploads/33963/2ffee0e1-8b28-43d7-9ab8-050d8e23b510)

—

### Our Vision

Akkari is our wedge towards building a living model of how companies actually operate - and one that becomes predictive over time.

### Our Team and Purpose

We are 2x YC founders. Previously, we scaled OrderAhead to millions of users (before it was acquired by Square) and BLADE to $1.2B+ in monthly trading volume.

At both companies, we learned that customers are won or lost in the follow-through that begins with the first conversation.

The best teams do not win just because they have better product or better messaging. They win because they follow through faster, more consistently and with better judgement than everyone else.

We’re building Akkari to make that level of execution available to every startup.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102648&key=user_uploads/33963/b77fff32-e80a-48af-b06c-f746fa459169)

### Our Ask

If staying on top of every customer commitment, issue, blocker, handoff, request and opportunity is becoming real work - we’d love to talk!

launches.title: GitCafe: A Git forge for teams and agents shipping hundreds of times a day, not twice.
launches.tagline: The Git forge for agent-scale teams
launches.body:
Software development is becoming much more parallel. Coding agents let a team have dozens or hundreds of related changes moving at the same time, creating more branches, reviews, CI runs, and automation than existing workflows were designed to absorb.

Today, we’re opening GitCafe in public beta. It is a Git forge built for teams where humans and coding agents may ship hundreds or thousands of changes a day. We’re building the hosting, review, CI, security, and automation layer for that way of working.\
\
Hundreds of users are already on GitCafe, and we’re currently running trials with roughly a dozen YC companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109445&key=user_uploads/1920545/eecbfb4f-82f1-4660-8ee8-aeea5273a8b9)

Generating code is only part of the problem. Teams still need to understand what is changing, review it safely, keep CI moving, catch security issues, and coordinate work without becoming overwhelmed.

We’re not building GitCafe because putting repositories, code review, and CI in one product is new. We’re building it because we believe the workload those systems need to support is about to change dramatically.

We started by rebuilding the Git infrastructure itself. Now we’re closing the product gap feature by feature.

Recently, we added secret scanning, Buildkite and Harmont CI support, stacked diffs with Jujutsu and Sapling integration, and beta support for GitHub Actions.

These are foundational capabilities, not the destination. Building them on infrastructure we own gives us a base we can keep extending for higher-volume, agent driven development.

The honest version is that GitCafe is behind GitHub today. GitHub has spent more than a decade building an enormous product, and GitCafe does not yet have every workflow, administrative control, or integration that mature teams need. Some features are missing, some are experimental, and some edges are rough. We expect to earn the broader product surface, not claim it on day one.

We’re opening GitCafe now because the fastest way to improve it is to put it in the hands of teams doing real work.

If your team is already using coding agents heavily, try GitCafe at <https://git.cafe> and tell us where the workflow breaks down.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=blHKFEOmoFg>

launches.title: Kebra — Making the field queryable
launches.tagline: We capture what happens in field operations and turn it into the context AI employees need to automate the work that follows
launches.body:
Hey YC! 👋

We’re [Luca](https://www.linkedin.com/in/luca-hadife/) and [Hosny](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohamed-hosny-hussein/), founders of [Kebra](https://kebra.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=yc_launch_2026).

## TL;DR

Kebra makes the field queryable.

We capture what happens across jobs, sites, and assets and turn it into a live operating memory that AI can query and act on. Our AI employees use that context to automate the work that follows across the systems companies already use.

Every job makes that memory richer, building the company specific context software agents use today and physical agents will need tomorrow.

We’re already working with field operations companies across Florida, Pennsylvania, and California.

<https://youtu.be/VIwv5iVm8Ok>

## The problem

Field operations never got their Claude Code moment.

We spent months inside HVAC companies trying to automate their back office. We built AI employees for claims, reporting, coordination, and follow ups.

They kept breaking.

Not because the AI could not do the work, but because it was acting on a reality that never happened. The most important part of the operation happened on the ground and was never properly captured.

A missing serial number. A photo never taken. What the technician actually found stuck in their head.

You cannot automate an alternate reality. Before AI can operate the field, the field has to become queryable.

## Our Solution

Kebra makes field operations queryable.

**Capture what happens:** Field teams document jobs through photos, voice, video, and structured workflows. Kebra checks what is missing while they are still on site.

**Build the operating memory:** Every job updates a live history of sites, assets, repairs, decisions, and how the company actually works.

**AI employees act on it:** They use that context to automate reports, claims, coordination, compliance, follow ups, and other back office work across the systems the company already uses.

## Vision

Every job makes Kebra’s operating memory richer.

Today, software agents use that context to automate field operations. Tomorrow, physical AI and robots will need the same company specific context to understand each site, asset, procedure, and history before they can work autonomously.

Kebra is building the context layer for field operations.

## Our Ask

Run or know a company with field operations where important information gets lost between the field and the office?

Email us at [founders@kebra.com](mailto:founders@kebra.com) and [book a demo](https://calendar.app.google/s1DwDxHTbxZ9w5Uq6).\
Follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/kebra-com)

launches.title: Pango: E-commerce operations on autopilot.
launches.tagline: Why can't e-commerce companies scale like tech companies?
launches.body:
tl;dr: Why can't e-commerce companies scale like tech companies? And how we might be able to change that.

We spent 12 months embedded in the operations of 30 e-commerce brands\! Here’s what we learnt:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107204&key=user_uploads/3288698/1a3cc8c3-db71-4d81-b2ad-9679b77f9451)

**What we saw:** Each company had a unique operational setup with a mix of 5 to 7 tools glued together to run the shop. To keep all these tools running smoothly with each other, it requires a lot of tedious admin. As a result, headcount increases as the company scales.

Most companies couldn't even automate a basic return processing, let alone offer exchanging items or build an AI agent to approve returns or send shipping label to the customer.

Expansion made it worse: more countries and/or SKUs = exponentially more problems.

**What we built:** We have built an agentic OS for e-commerce: You connect your shop stack, then describe how you want to handle shipments, returns, refunds, or claims → Pango builds the return portal, fixes the delivery options, and builds a customer service process and agent for you.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107204&key=user_uploads/3288698/ceed8a01-52aa-403a-9986-758da64ff4e4)

**Result:** So far we have managed to automate 99% of returns and shipping operations, reduce operation costs by 20% and sign 30 global brands.

Intros to:

- Agencies (Shopify/e-commerce)
- Brands in fashion, beauty, home.

launches.tagline: Hoplite runs autonomous coding agents in cloud sandboxes. Spin up tasks manually from Slack, Linear, iMessage, or automatically from Sentry.
launches.body:
Cloud coding agents are painful to set up, lacking ergonomics, and don't allow you to move as fast as possible. We let you bring your local set up to the cloud.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/28db62de-d65b-4498-84ac-12e2683c65f2)

**The Problem** 

In the next 10 years the best software startups will be those who can effectively deploy tokens. 

Right now that's significantly harder than it needs to be. If you’ve ever ran multiple agents locally you immediately know this pain.

Laptop crashes, wrangling gitwork trees, juggling ports, and more headaches.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/6f320e85-ccbb-4fb4-a5e9-6ec3cb0206c7)

So cloud is the obvious answer right? 

But setting up with these existing providers is quite a hassle, and oftentimes they miss some key feature that your local config has.

**What we do**

We deploy software factories into businesses that want to **tokenmaxx** but don't have the time or the resources to set up the infrastructure.

During onboarding, we transfer all of your local sessions and MCP servers to Hoplite, meaning you can pick up right from where you left off. We also configure all the required dependencies and CLIs that your projects require, letting you see instant previews of what your agent is doing.

Our bet is that as models improve, we’re going to start caring less about the code that they output (we’ll implicitly trust it), and shift our focus towards the product itself. Hence, a platform that prioritizes iteration on product rather than code will ultimately win. 

We also have an iMessage integration so you can prompt on the go.

We installed in our first business last week and we saw an immediate result, from sentry logs going from largely ignored to fully proactive PRs when something breaks. 

They have significantly faster iteration cycles and lower priority tickets have been continuously getting merged. 

They wanted faster iterations but didn't have the infrastructure to support a software factory, so we went in and built it.

If this sounds like you reach out! 

P.S. – If you love Vim, this is for you. It was built with keyboard navigation in mind 🙂

demo vid: <https://x.com/ryan_morr/status/2078240892738224292?s=20>

sign up: <https://hoplite.sh>

**How we got here**

Previously, we were building an agentic harness for financial markets; letting retail investors trade with AI. The product worked well, but we never truly had founder market fit. 

We found that our true passion was in talking to founders and developers – and oftentimes when pitching our old product, I’d spend 5x longer explaining our potential pivot 😅

And so we set out to commercialize a product that we’d built internally, one that’d let us deploy the $1.5 million in OpenAI credits effectively.

**Our Ask:** Let us Collison install! Bence and I will come to your apartment and set up everything for you (and bring some matcha & assorted sweet treats). We want to build the best possible product for developers to move faster and care deeply about peoples setups. Partially because we have very strong opinions of our own… 

**The Team** 

Bence & I are both from Ireland 🇮🇪. We met in college in a course called Immersive Software Engineering. 

We have been building projects & doing freelance work tg for the past 2 years, but got sick of building other people's visions. 

We previously interned at AWS (Bence) & [@Stripe](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/240) (Ryan). After that experience, we were fed up and decided to drop out to build. 

We are best friends & just want to build a product that people truly love.

name: Donkey
long_description:
Donkey is the AI-native trading company. Upload a buying list and we land the whole container at one locked, delivered price, tariffs included. You buy from Donkey: one contract, one company responsible for everything between the factory floor and your door. Our own people check the cartons before the factory gets paid, and the balance is due when the goods are accepted at your dock.

Small businesses buy imports through three or four middlemen, each adding 15 to 30 points, because none of them can fill a container on their own. Big enough to buy pallets, never big enough to buy the box. Quotes float with freight, FX and tariffs and live 15 to 30 days.

A trading company is rooms of people on the phone with factories, forwarders and brokers. Donkey runs that as one engine. It finds the real factory behind the customs record, stacks duty line by line, packs the container on weight and cube, and returns one number that holds from signature. Next comes the shared container: small buyers fill one box together at container prices, and every container earns better factory terms for the next one.

Team in San Francisco and Wuhan, English and Mandarin. If your business buys pallets of anything imported, send us your buying list.
one_liner: The AI-native trading company: factory prices, delivered, one number
