launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: [Daqstra](https://www.daqstra.com/) is the AI-native test orchestration platform for physical R&D. We connect fragmented test hardware, capture every run, and give engineers an API to operate their test setup, helping aerospace, energy, and robotics teams spend less time rebuilding infrastructure.**

Hey! We’re [Anchit Kumar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anchitk/) and [Darell Chua](https://www.linkedin.com/in/darell-chua/), the founders of [Daqstra](https://www.daqstra.com/).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106987&key=user_uploads/2547322/7ed7475e-d673-4796-9462-d40f72da12ad)

We met while testing liquid rocket engines in the Mojave Desert.

The engines were difficult, but much of the friction came from the infrastructure around them. Before each test, we connected sensors, custom electronics, NI hardware, PLCs, and controllers that were never designed to work together. After each run, the data was scattered across machines, file formats, scripts, and people’s heads.

Before we could learn from one test, we often had to reconstruct what had happened.

After talking with teams building rockets, energy systems, robots, and drones, we kept hearing the same story: **their hardware was advancing faster than the infrastructure used to test it.**

## What We Built

[Watch the demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ykvD67omalI) or visit [daqstra.com](http://daqstra.com).

Daqstra works with the equipment teams already have, including NI/LabVIEW, PLCs, custom DAQ systems, sensors, controllers, and vendor hardware.

* **Daqstra Edge** connects hardware at the test site and records commands alongside the resulting telemetry.
* **Daqstra Hub** stores each run with its configuration, events, notes, and engineering context, making it easier to monitor tests, compare runs, and investigate anomalies.
* **Daqstra API** lets engineers configure hardware and execute repeatable test sequences through software.

Together, these give teams one interface across otherwise incompatible hardware without forcing them to replace their existing stack.

## What We’re Already Doing

We’re working with advanced hardware teams across aerospace, energy, and drones. Our active aerospace programs use Daqstra day to day across fragmented, multi-vendor test environments.

In energy, we’ve signed a pilot with a palm oil processor targeting $100K+ in annual savings by reducing recoverable oil lost through its effluent stream. We’re also helping drone teams unify telemetry, control, and test data across vehicles and ground systems.

## Who We’d Love to Meet

If you lead test, propulsion, integration, validation, or hardware engineering and run frequent instrumented tests, we’d love to talk.

Daqstra is especially useful if your team:

* Works across vendor equipment, PLCs, custom electronics, and in-house software
* Reconfigures its setup between tests or struggles to compare runs
* Relies on a few engineers who understand the entire test environment

We’re initially focused on aerospace, energy, drones, and robotics. If this sounds like your team, reply here or email [**team@daqstra.com**](mailto:team@daqstra.com).

If it sounds like someone you know, we’d appreciate an introduction to the person responsible for test infrastructure, integration, or validation.

**Ad Astra Per Daqstra**

launches.title: TryNearby: Every local business needs to be discoverable. That $150B market is moving toward local creators.
launches.tagline: Word of mouth at scale for local restaurants
launches.body:
Hey everyone,

We're Yousef, Obaida, and Ahmad, the founders of **TryNearby**.

Yousef co-founded FaZe Clan and spent 15 years creating content for 10M+ followers alongside hundreds of other creators. Ahmad and Obaida co-founded one of the first social media clipping companies, building the infrastructure that tracked billions of views across thousands of videos for creator campaigns. We've watched creator content become the most powerful distribution channel on the internet, and we're bringing it to local businesses.

## **TL;DR**

84% of small businesses on TikTok say it helped grow their business. Almost every restaurant owner we meet knows that and has no idea how to act on it.

TryNearby handles it. Every month we send a new group of creators who live nearby to visit, film, and post a review, for a $399 subscription. All of it is handled by us and our AI agents.

Today, 120+ restaurants are subscribed and have had 2,500+ videos posted for them. We nearly doubled one restaurant's revenue in their first month, and owners tell us people walk in every day saying "we saw you on TikTok." Almost half our new restaurants now come from other owners referring us.

Our launch video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lSG0v1MNwik>

## **The problem**

There are about 1 million restaurants and cafes in the US. Most of them are invisible in the places people actually decide where to eat.

The options an owner has today:

* Agencies cost thousands a month and often don’t drive real results
* Influencers work, but finding the right local ones, negotiating, and doing it again every month is a job by itself
* Creating their own content is a second full-time job they don't have time for, or a full-time hire they don't have the budget for

And here's the thing: _the algorithm doesn't reward a business talking about itself. It rewards people talking about the business._

So the thing that actually works — someone who lives nearby posting about your food — happens once or twice, or not at all.

And the platforms keep rewarding the ones who show up. TikTok's new Local Feed ranks by location and recency, so the restaurants getting fresh content every month reach their own neighborhood. The ones who don't, disappear.

## **The solution**

TryNearby is a subscription that puts local creators inside local restaurants every month, and their followers through the door.

$399/month. Every month we automatically schedule a new group of vetted creators who live nearby. They come in, film, edit, and post. The restaurant just serves the food.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110956&key=user_uploads/3490413/7721f4f4-96e4-4a68-b860-841fee782765)

### **Part 1 — They sign up, creators start showing up**

The moment a restaurant joins, our matching agent finds the creators nearby who fit that spot and sends the invites. Sometimes a creator is scheduled to visit within five minutes of a restaurant signing up. Creators pick their own time from the restaurant's availability. The restaurant doesn't coordinate anything or answer a single message.

### **Part 2 — An AI agent runs every creator relationship**

Every creator on TryNearby is managed over iMessage by an agent we built. Onboarding, match invites, booking, reminders, reschedules, questions. It handles over 10,000 texts a month.

It also learns as it goes. Every conversation teaches it more about that creator: what they like to eat, where they'll actually drive, when they're free, what they turn down. That context feeds the matching, so the invites get better the longer someone is on the platform.

For creators, it's a personal assistant that helps them become better creators while bringing collaborations straight to their iMessage instead of them chasing restaurants.

### **Part 3 — Restaurant owners get their own AI agent to text**

Owners get an assistant in iMessage too. It watches every video, comment, and review, and tells them what's happening: who's visiting this week, how the last video performed, what people are saying. So when a dish sells out the week after a creator posted about it, the owner knows exactly why.

Our team sits behind both agents. Anything either one can't handle gets flagged to us in seconds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110956&key=user_uploads/3490413/5ff964f8-9013-42d7-9617-29d6ccb2164a)

## **Traction**

10 months in:

* 120+ paying restaurants across Southern California
* 37% month-over-month growth with over 90% monthly restaurant retention since November
* 2,500+ videos posted by local creators → \~35M views, almost entirely from people within a few miles

What that turned into for the restaurants:

* A restaurant in San Diego nearly doubled revenue in a single month
* Another had a whole new demographic of customers drive a 50% increase in sales
* Dishes featured in creator videos hit record sales the following week

Every single owner tells us the same thing: **people are walking in and saying they saw them on TikTok.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110956&key=user_uploads/3490413/3301e743-2fef-43c4-9138-aaa5631d1eb8)

## **Team**

**Yousef** co-founded FaZe Clan after starting as a 14-year-old YouTuber in 2010. He spent 15 years in the creator economy, built an audience of 10M+ followers and over a billion views, and helped take FaZe public on the Nasdaq at a $1B valuation.

**Ahmad** co-founded one of the first social media clipping companies, where he built the first and largest infrastructure for short-form clipping, tracking 10B+ views across tens of thousands of videos for some of the biggest creators on the internet. UC Berkeley CS, previously a senior engineer at WeightWatchers.

**Obaida** co-founded the clipping company alongside Ahmad. He was an early employee at Replit, previously Goldman Sachs, and grew a consumer app from $360K to $2M ARR in 18 months. Master's in applied economics from Johns Hopkins.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110956&key=user_uploads/3490413/031126b7-4cbd-49dc-989f-ef79381b8bd9)

If you own a restaurant, know an owner who wants more foot traffic, are a local creator, or are just interested in TryNearby, we'd love to talk → 📧 [hello@trynearby.com](https://mailto:hello@trynearby.com)

# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: We're building a modern tax engine for accountants and fintechs building on tax: a deterministic tax calculation and e-filing core behind a single API, built on the IRS's official e-file infrastructure (MeF).**

## A tax return is math. It should be a function call.

We're Angelo and Akash, and we built Luca IQ, a new tax engine for accounting firms. One set of inputs in, a completed, filed return out in minutes. Not bolted onto decades out desktop software.

For CPA firms, that means more returns per preparer, less spend on labor, and a clean path off 30-year-old desktop software. For the PE groups acquiring and scaling firms, it means real operating leverage on the single most labor-intensive part of the business.

<https://youtu.be/IV5nl7grMxI>

**The problem.** \~95% of US firms file their returns through just four companies, and all of them were built decades ago, for the desktop, and are closed. Firms are stuck running tax season on software that can't scale with them. Every modern AI tax tool just pushes data into that same closed software it can't control. Everyone rebuilt the interface.

**What we built.** A new one, and we're opening it. A key principle: AI never does the tax math. AI and human judgment set the inputs, and a deterministic engine computes the return, with a full audit trail on every number. It's either 100% correct or it's wrong, and only a deterministic engine can promise the former. For firms, that means throughput without giving up accuracy or defensibility.

Our core leverage: we're an **IRS-authorized e-file provider as a Software Developer, Transmitter, and Intermediate Service Provider**, so Luca IQ doesn't just compute the return, it e-files straight to the IRS. That full path, calculation through filing, is what firms can't get from a closed engine today.

**Why now.** The profession is running out of people. 300,000+ accountants have left since 2019, and \~70% of CPAs are near retirement. At the same time, private equity is rolling up firms and pushing hard on margin. The work isn't going away. The people are, and the pressure to do more with fewer preparers has never been higher.

**Who we are.** Angelo (CEO) is a CPA who worked in forensic accounting with the FBI, Wall Street, EY and spent years working at tax firms using the legacy softwares we are now replacing. Akash (CTO) was employee #1 at a fintech data-infrastructure startup and leads engineering.

**What we need:**

* **CPA firms who dread tax season**, We'd love 20 minutes to show you what Luca IQ does for throughput and margin. This is who we build for.
* **PE firms rolling up accounting practices.** If tax prep labor is your biggest cost line, let's talk.
* **Developers and fintechs** who need 1040 calculations or e-filing. The engine is one API call, and you can build on it early.

Reach us at [founders@lucaiq.com](mailto:founders@lucaiq.com).

launches.title: Executor — One place to connect your agents to everything
launches.tagline: Connect your tools once and every agent has them, with permissions you control
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Executor is your tool gateway. Connect every service and every account once, set per-tool permissions, and any MCP-compatible agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, whatever ships next) reaches all of it through one endpoint. Try it at [executor.sh](https://executor.sh).

https://youtu.be/NWYFpDW02Dw

## The problem

You don't have one agent anymore. You have Claude Code, a ChatGPT account, Cursor, maybe a box in the corner running jobs overnight. Three problems follow:

1. **Every agent wants its own OAuth into everything.** You connect your calendar to the tenth harness in a slightly different way, tokens expire, connectors deprecate, and each agent is missing something when you need it.
2. **Most connectors stop at one account per service.** One Google login means your agent sees your work calendar or your personal one, never both. Your flights land in one inbox, your meetings in the other, and no agent can reason over your actual day.
3. **Permissions are an afterthought.** Once an agent holds a token, it can do anything that token allows. Giving an agent your email shouldn't mean trusting it to never hit delete.

## What Executor does

Connect once in Executor, and sever all the one-off connections.

Each integration gets credentials plus a per-tool policy: **always allowed**, **needs approval**, or **blocked**. Point any MCP-compatible agent at Executor and it has everything.

- **All your accounts, not just one.** Accounts are connections: work and personal Gmail, two calendars, a staging and a production Stripe, side by side. Every agent sees all of them.
- **One tool shape.** MCP, OpenAPI, and GraphQL integrations all normalize into a consistent name + schema. 1,600+ tools collapse into a single ~1k-token surface instead of ~280k tokens of tool definitions.
- **Safe by default.** Executor preserves operation semantics (GET vs DELETE, destructive hints, GraphQL mutations), so agents auto-run safe operations and ask before risky ones.
- **Sandboxed execution.** Tool calls run in an isolated JavaScript sandbox; secrets are injected host-side, so the model never sees a raw token.
- **Team-ready.** Per-user and shared credentials. Onboard the team once, not per agent per person.

Because enforcement lives in Executor rather than in any agent framework, you can adopt whatever new agent ships next week without re-thinking data access. You keep everything first-party connectors offer and gain what they don't: multiple accounts per service, per-tool policies, and one place to see and revoke access.

## How to use it

- **Local:** open-source (MIT) desktop app and CLI, everything stays on your machine
- **Self-hosted:** a Dockerfile that lets your team own all its data
- **Executor Cloud:** hosted, nothing to manage

## Traction

- 2,800+ GitHub stars, ~14k npm downloads/week, ~3,000 users on the local version

## Background

Solo technical founder, previously at Vercel. Before Executor I built [answeroverflow.com](https://www.answeroverflow.com) and grew it to 1.5M monthly users as a solo dev, bootstrapped.

## Asks

1. **Try it and tell me where it breaks.** [executor.sh](https://executor.sh) has a "Copy prompt" setup you can paste into your agent to get started.
2. **Intros:** if your team (or one you know) is drowning in per-agent integration setup, I'd love an intro: rhys@executor.sh
3. **Star the repo:** [github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor](https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor)
4. **Want a walkthrough?** Grab a time: [cal.com/rhys-sullivan/executor-chat](https://cal.com/rhys-sullivan/executor-chat)

Hi YC 👋 we're Rishi and Tushar, and we're building Waybill (<https://waybill.to>).

**TL;DR:** Waybill runs procurement for hardware and deep-tech companies, end to end. An engineer tells us what part they need. Our agents and humans source it anywhere in the world, get quotes, handle payment, shipping, customs, last mile, log it into inventory and match the invoices. One system of record from request to stock. We don’t stop at the ‘order placed’. We make sure it reaches your shelf. A few crazy things Waybill was asked to source & order -

1. A lifetime supply of an obsolete RF component
2. Cessna aircraft. Yes, real airplanes
3. Industrial Robots

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/JPxhZFZ5xco>

**Backstory**

I (Rishi) ran operations at LAT Aerospace (Deepinder Goyal’s aerospace startup) as part of their founding team. On paper, that meant "sourcing." In practice, it meant finding jet engines, flight controllers, high-density batteries, and satellite radios for a very ambitious aerospace program, then moving machinery and merchandise worth millions across borders, and finding and operating real estate you can actually fly aircraft from. I also handled government liaisoning, which is a polite way of saying I convinced the world's harshest bureaucracy to approve things it didn't have a form for, like taking off and landing an aircraft in under 50 meters.

Tushar has been working the other end of this problem his whole career. At WareIQ (YC S20), he built the autonomous inventory system behind 400+ Indian D2C brands - forecasting demand and making buying decisions across thousands of volatile SKUs without blowing up working capital.

So between us: I've spent my career buying hardware the hard way, and Tushar's spent his teaching machines to manage inventory. Waybill is both jobs in one system.

**The problem**

Hardware engineers spend a big chunk of their week buying parts. They can't hand it off to operations folks, because only the engineer who specified the part knows which alternates are acceptable. And finding parts is genuinely hard: stock is scattered across distributor catalogs, resellers, and Alibaba listings, and packaging suffixes, obsolete part numbers, and regional inventory make the same part look like six different parts. It's a search, not a lookup.

All of this runs on email, WhatsApp, and spreadsheets. No system of record, and context dilutes at every handoff. Parts land late, arrive undocumented, or get bought twice. I know because at LAT, _I was the system of record_. It didn't scale.

**What we built**

An engineer tells Waybill what they need. Our agents find every authorized distributor and manufacturer rep stocking that part anywhere in the world, request quotes and lead times, and rank the options by what the customer actually cares about. A defence company only wants suppliers from allied nations. A medical device company needs provenance. Everyone else wants the right balance of cost, lead time, and complexity.

If no distributor has it, our network in India, China, and Southeast Asia finds it. If a supplier can't ship to the customer's country, we pick up the box and ship it ourselves.

Once the order is placed, our agents prepare the customs paperwork, a licensed broker files it, parts are received into inventory automatically, and the invoice is automatically matched against the PO and import documents. The next time someone asks for that part, the agent says it's already on the shelf.

And when a customer moves from R&D to production, the same system scales with them. Demand comes off the BOM and build schedule - reorder points, second sources, volume pricing - and we already hold every order, price, and lead time they've ever had.

Most procurement software ends at an approved PO. We end at a physical part on a shelf, customs-cleared and invoice-matched.

Rippling made the employee the first-class object and built every service around it. We're doing the same for the part.

Here are a few crazy things engineering teams asked Waybill to procure in the two weeks that we’ve been live -

1. A lifetime purchase of an obsolete RF component
2. Cessna aircraft. Yes, real airplanes.
3. Industrial Robots

**Where this goes**

A hardware company should be able to ask us for anything physical and get it. Today that's parts. Next it's PCB fab and assembly, CNC machining, 3D printing, tooling, trucking, warehousing, and allocation on ships and planes. The interface never changes: say what you need, and it arrives.

**Asks**

1. Hardware and deep-tech founders - we want to run your procurement. Comment, DM, or email me at [rishi@waybill.to](mailto:rishi@waybill.to). We’re company size agnostic.
2. Intros to procurement leads at hardware enterprises. If you know one, we'd love a connect.

**Ask for it and it shows up. Take your supply chain for granted.**

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Inkbox is the identity and communication layer for AI agents: giving agents their own email, phone, iMessage, and internet address. Inkbox pulls together what your agent sees across email, calls, iMessage, and more, so your agent can act on the full context.

Hey YC! We're Ray, Alex, and Dima building Inkbox.

**How we got here**

A few months ago we were building web-automation agents. Every time an agent needed to log into a portal, it had to receive a confirmation email or get a 2FA code. And when we were away from our desks, we wanted to seamlessly contact the agents themselves: text them, check in, get a reply. We ended up stitching together services like Gmail, Twilio, and ngrok: separate services, each built for humans, none of them sharing any identity or context. 

That's the problem we set out to fix. We didn't need another email or voice API. We needed one service to tie its identity together with rich context. So we built it.

[**Launch video**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oJKl6tPHxRA)

**What Inkbox does**

Our API gives every agent:

* A unique email inbox (+ custom domain)
* A phone number that can call and text
* iMessage
* A persistent internet address (HTTPS tunnel) to receive internet traffic, like webhooks
* An encrypted credential vault with TOTP/2FA

**Who we are**

* Ray (CEO): CS PhD from MIT; previously cofounded Empallo, an AI virtual clinic for cardiovascular patients.
* Alex (CTO): MS in CS @ Northeastern. Previously ML engineering and computer networking research.
* Dima (CAIO): built ML pipelines on gigapixel pathology images at Harvard Medical School; co-author on 6+ peer-reviewed publications.

[**Quick demo with Claude**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTVkW_EG-Y4): Watch Claude Code provision an email, phone, and iMessage in a Minute.

**Our ask**

* **Try it**. Drop Inkbox into your preferred agent harness: we have plugins for[ Hermes](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/hermes-agent-plugin),[ OpenClaw](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/openclaw-plugin),[ Claude Code](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/claude-code-plugin), and[ Codex](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/codex-plugin). Each one runs a wizard that provisions Inkbox resources for your agent.
* **Ask your agent to self signup**. _Sign up for an Inkbox email account by following the guide at[ https://inkbox.ai/docs/get-started/agent-signup.md](https://inkbox.ai/docs/get-started/agent-signup.md) and refer to[ https://inkbox.ai/llms.txt](https://inkbox.ai/llms.txt) for full documentation._
* **Intros**. We'd love intros to teams running fleets of agents that each need their own identity to act in the real world: reaching out to people and businesses (email/phone/iMessage), holding their own accounts, and authenticating with a built-in credential vault.

Contact Ray at [ray@inkbox.ai](mailto:ray@inkbox.ai). Would love your feedback.

launches.tagline: We use your agent’s production traces to train a specialized model that performs better, responds faster, and costs less.
launches.body:
Your agent logs aren’t just for debugging. They’re your training data.\
Hey YC! We’re Shubham and Parth, childhood friends and founders of Agnost AI.

**TL;DR**: Agnost AI uses your agent’s production traces to train a model specialized for your exact workload. Our first custom model for our customer delivered them a:

* 22.9% higher task success,
* 90.2% lower median latency, and
* 94.5% lower cost than Opus 4.8.

Demo: <https://youtu.be/R3NyWNYXHu4>

### What we found

A few weeks ago, we launched Agnost AI as product analytics for AI agents. We read conversations between users and agents to uncover failures, behavior drift, hallucinated links, frustration, and churn signals.

We expected to find bugs. Surprisingly, we also found a lot of infrastructure waste. Many customer-facing agents use frontier models for narrow, repetitive jobs:

* Route a request to the correct tool
* Have a narrow system prompt with the given inputs
* Retrieve the relevant data from internal tool calls
* Parse & format the final response

The underlying frontier model can write code, solve advanced mathematics, understand biology, and reason across hundreds of domains. **Your agent uses a small, repeatable slice of that capability while paying frontier-model prices for every request.**

### We trained a specialist

We used historical production traces to train our first workload-specific model for an early customer: **agnost-<redacted>-0.1**

We evaluated it against Opus 4.8 on 780 held-out customer traces for an Identifier Extraction Agent. The results:

* Task success: 71.5% → 87.9%, 22.9% relative improvement
* Median latency: 4.80s → 0.47s, 90.2% lower
* Tail latency: 11.20s → 1.35s, 87.9% lower
* Cost per 1,000 completed tasks: $42.00 → $2.30, 94.5% lower

This is one model for one workload, not a claim that specialist models should replace frontier models everywhere.

Frontier models remain the right choice for open-ended work. But once an agent’s production job becomes predictable, **paying for general intelligence on every request stops making sense**.

### How it works

1. Send your existing traces to Agnost through OpenTelemetry or our SDK.
2. We identify the recurring workflows your agent performs.
3. We create an eval set from held-out production traces.
4. We train a specialist model on the historical workload.
5. We benchmark it against your current model on success, latency, and cost.

You only consider switching when the specialist wins on your own workload. Your logs go from debugging data to evaluation data and finally to training data recursively.

### Who we are

We’re childhood friends, eight years and counting.

* Shubham: Youngest engineer on Cisco’s analytics team, first hire at Formbricks, and contributor to Bitcoin, OWASP, and the Linux Foundation.
* Parth: IIT Madras CS, ranked 159 out of 1.5 million. Built Spark pipelines at Microsoft and led GPU technology at Infurnia.

### Our ask

If you have meaningful daily traffic, send us an anonymized trace export. We’ll analyze the workload, build a held-out evaluation set, and tell you whether a specialist model is worth training. If it is, we’ll benchmark it against your current frontier model.

Email me at [shubham@agnost.ai](mailto:shubham@agnost.ai) or book a call at [call.agnost.ai](http://call.agnost.ai)

More about us at: [agnost.ai](https://agnost.ai)

launches.body:
**Your users are telling your agent exactly why they churn! You’re not listening.**

Hey YC! We’re Shubham and Parth, childhood friends, founders of **Agnost AI**.

**TL;DR: Agnost AI reads every conversation your chat or voice agent has with your users. We show you what your users want, where they get frustrated, and why they leave.**

**The feedback hiding in your logs becomes discoveries, evals, and fixes ready to ship. We’re already processing over 1 million events every day and growing.**

Try us out at[ agnost.ai](http://agnost.ai)

### <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gKyhf6rUELg>

### **The problem**

Traditional product analytics were built for clicks.\
Observability was built for token costs, latencies, and deterministic errors.

But every product is rapidly moving from UI to conversation, and agent failures don’t look like traditional failures. The LLM returns 200 OK and says “sorry, I can’t do that.” The real failures are hiding in your conversations:

* “can it remember this for next time?” → feature request
* “you said it’s done, but nothing happened” → bug
* “i’ve told you this three times already” → frustration
* “nvm i’ll just do it myself” → churn

Today teams throw more evals at this. But evals only tell you whether you fixed something, not what to fix. You can’t write a test for a problem you haven’t discovered yet.

### **How it works**

1. **Install our skill:** 3 lines of code, or point your OpenTelemetry exporter at us. Any LLM, any framework. Add any custom metadata like user tier, model versions, etc. We’re at:[ docs.agnost.ai](http://docs.agnost.ai)
2. **Every conversation becomes a signal:** feature requests, bugs, frustration, churn risk, failed upgrades. Detected for your product, with the exact users & conversations behind each.
3. **The insight becomes action:** when hundreds of users rageprompt at your agent due to a specific bug, Agnost AI hands you the insight with the exact conversations behind it: 
   * create an eval from it
   * debug it,
   * or let Agnost fix it itself: our GitHub app opens a PR, tested against your past conversations, so you know it works before it ships.

   Your agent gets better every week.

### **Who we are**

Childhood friends, 8 years and counting.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107260&key=user_uploads/2055517/e3c2eaad-8b6e-4ec0-abfa-b16074688963)

**Shubham**: Youngest engineer on Cisco’s analytics team, First Hire at Formbricks, Wrote code in Bitcoin, OWASP, and the Linux Foundation.

name: Decawork
long_description:
An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Access decisions need to adapt in real time as the agent works, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rules or have people manually approve every step.

We train small, company-specific models that approve AI actions in real time. They consider the company’s policies and interests, the agent’s current task, and its past actions to decide whether each proposed action should be allowed. Access is specific to the task at hand and reassessed as the agent works.

Companies will rent intelligence from AI labs or run open-source models to power their agents. They’ll own the models that keep their entire AI workforce acting in their interests. Decawork is building those models.

launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋 - we're Aman and Sarthak, founders of Decawork.\
\
**TL;DR:** AI agents shouldn’t have permanent access to company systems. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into fixed rules or manually approve every step. Decawork trains small, company-specific AI models that approve every agent action in real time, based on company policies and interests, the agent’s task, and its past actions. Access is granted for the task at hand and revoked when it’s done.\
\
Launch video: [Watch it here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SanpHIyFcV4)\
\
🚧 **The Problem & Why now?**\
Companies are putting long-running, more autonomous agents to work on broader tasks and goals. These agents need access to critical company systems, but their actions can be unpredictable and may not serve the company’s interests.

OpenAI’s agents have already hacked Hugging Face during testing with reduced safeguards. Replit’s agent deleted data from a live application’s database.

An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Permanent access lets an agent keep using permissions even when they are no longer appropriate for its task.

As agents take on more work independently, access decisions need to happen in real time. But companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rule or have people manually approve every step.\
\
✅ **How we solve this?**\
Decawork gives AI agents access for the task at hand and revokes it when the task is done.

* Connect your agents. Route API requests and MCP tool calls through Decawork to see activity and manage access in one place.
* Set company policies. Write policies in plain English, specify when human approval is required, and connect your existing identity and IT service management systems.
* Deploy a company-specific policy model. We deploy small models that approve actions in real time using your company’s policies and priorities, task context, and past actions. Your agents do the work. Decawork evaluates each proposed action and enforces the access decision before it runs.

🚀 **Team**\
Sarthak built AI systems at NVIDIA that were deployed at OpenAI and Meta, and worked on enterprise AI agents at Ema.

Aman built the AI compliance platform at Barclays used by internal teams globally, then led product at a consumer AI startup serving 100K+ monthly users, hand-wiring credentials for the agents he shipped.

Every one of those deployments came down to the same questions: what can it access, who approved it, and what did it do? We kept solving agent access by hand - so we quit to build the system we wished we’d had.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109883&key=user_uploads/1632535/0ef2784e-ab45-422f-91b9-960473f11dd5)

launches.tagline: Co-designed models and silicon: we hardcode the model architecture into chips targeting 20,000+ tokens per second and 63x higher intelligence per watt.
launches.body:
**Hi Everyone!** 

**We’re Niki and Thomas - cofounders of Lamb Labs.**  

**TL;DR: We build custom AI inference chips that run inference at 20,000+ tok/s and 63x higher intelligence per watt than a traditional GPU. Fully local and private by construction, no subscriptions, no API costs.** 

**Our mission: the world’s fastest LLM at the lowest power.** 

<https://youtu.be/MhhY1Dy9ltE?feature=shared>

**Our hot take: AI models are finally getting good enough to hardcode them directly into silicon.** Once you stop treating the chip as a general-purpose GPU and burn a specific model into hardware, inference gets radically faster and cheaper per watt. Most of the industry is still building flexible, general chips. We think that flexibility is exactly what's wasting your energy. So we’re on a mission to reduce the energy footprint of AI. 

**The Problem**

AI is taking power on two fronts: concentrating control of data and intelligence, and consuming ever more electricity to grow. That future scares us, so we're building against it.

Here's the technical root of the waste: **GPUs burn most of their energy during inference moving data, not computing.** LLM/VLM inference is memory-bound, fetching a weight from memory costs \~100–1000x the energy of the arithmetic you do with it. So you underutilize the GPU you paid for: some GPUs only hit 20–40% compute utilization during LLM inference while the rest idles waiting on memory.

Cloud hosting adds its own tax: expensive per-token bills, latency you can't control, network dependencies, and your data leaving your control.

**Our Solution**

We build the model and the chip together. 

The Hardware Layer

* **Custom architecture, RL-tuned.** We built an RL environment that co-designs the chip architecture for a given model, optimizing directly for speed and energy per token.
* **Aggressive quantization.** Removes complex math, which shrinks the size and cost of the chip.
* **Weights on-chip.** The model weights live where the compute is overcoming the memory-bandwidth bottleneck

 

Because everything is hardcoded, it's fully local and secure by construction. No connectivity dependency, nothing leaves the device.

The Software Layer 

Designing the chip led us to solving a fundamental flaw in LLMs so we are now open-sourcing a new model next week, converted from another open source model, to run 2x faster on any hardware. Come back next week for part 2 of our launch to find out more….

**Our Ask**

If you answer "yes" to any of these, we'd love your help:

* **Are you paying for inference in watts, not just dollars?** Neocloud or private DC operators who are power- or hardware-cost-bound rather than demand-bound, talk to us.
* **Do you need inference where the cloud isn't an option?** Private AI deployments, regulated, air-gapped, sovereign, or bandwidth-starved deployments.
* **Do you want to deploy the fastest AI models in your stack?** High frequency trading, agentic workflows 
* **Are you stuck on a thermal or battery budget?** Robotics, wearables, consumer AI hardware where a Jetson-class part is over-provisioned and runs too hot.
* **Can you introduce us to anyone above?** Warm intros are the single most useful thing.

Contact us at [contact@lamb-labs.com](mailto:contact@lamb-labs.com)

launches.tagline: AI that finds and fixes OS-level vulnerabilities across device fleets
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** For companies running large fleets of OS-level endpoints (running GPU clusters, having a network of cloud devices, or deploying on-device), Palisade detects and fixes operating-system vulnerabilities (privilege escalation, remote code execution, memory corruption) that are extremely hard to detect and mitigate without applying AI to kernel-level data (syscalls, eBPF traces, process/memory events, network packets). A fix that used to take weeks to roll out, Palisade now applies in minutes across every endpoint.

Hey YC! I'm Prince, an ML researcher and engineer who dropped out from Caltech at 18 to build Palisade.

**What’s the problem:** Modern attacks increasingly target the operating system, but most security products only observe the network, cloud, or application layers. That leaves OS vulnerabilities among the hardest problems to detect and the slowest to remediate across a fleet.

**Why I’m building this:** Since I was 16, I have done plenty of professional red-team and blue-team security work. One pattern kept showing up: OS-level vulnerabilities were consistently the hardest to handle. Detection required low-level visibility, and even after identifying a vulnerability, rolling out a mitigation across hundreds or thousands of machines often took weeks. My background in both machine learning and operating systems convinced me this didn't have to be a manual process, so I built Palisade to automatically detect and remediate these vulnerabilities at the kernel level across an entire fleet.

**What Palisade does:** Palisade watches your systems at the kernel level—syscalls, eBPF traces, process and memory events, and network packets—and uses AI to find OS vulnerabilities other tools miss, then implement the fix automatically across every endpoint.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106995&key=user_uploads/2688178/fa8c6d6a-b058-4f44-87d0-5511d038718b)

_The Palisade control plane, live against a real kernel (LSM-BPF). The live feed at the bottom: every row is a real syscall decision._

The vulnerabilities it catches are the ones you can't see from the app or network layer alone:

* Privilege escalation
* Remote code execution
* Memory corruption

Most are caught before an exploit ever happens, and the fix is applied immediately, fleet-wide. The same patch that used to take weeks now lands in minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106995&key=user_uploads/2688178/2f4e756d-1348-44a2-bdce-bb3491925da5)

_The host audit: real findings ranked by severity. The bottom one is the cloud-metadata exposure: the same path behind the Capital One breach. One click on **Apply fix** and it's installed as a kernel rule._

Palisade can already detect and fix real problems:

* CVE-2024-1086: use-after-free in the Linux kernel's netfilter (nf_tables); local privilege escalation to root
* CVE-2025-6019: libblockdev/udisks privilege escalation to full root
* CVE-2025-32463: sudo --chroot local privilege escalation to root

**Who it's for:** Companies running a lot of OS-level endpoints, where a single kernel vulnerability multiplies across the whole fleet. Whether it’s network servers or GPUs, we have you covered.

<https://youtu.be/CTVhq7jfTPY>

**Our asks:**

* Intros: if you run a large fleet of OS-level endpoints, or know a security/infra lead who does, I'd love an intro.
* See the demo and tell me if you’d use it. Brutal feedback welcome.

— [prince@palisade-ai.com](mailto:prince@palisade-ai.com), <https://calendly.com/prince-palisade-ai/30min>, DMs welcome

launches.title: Hyperprobe: On-call Agent for engineering teams
launches.tagline: The fastest way for coding agents to debug incidents live in production.
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR:** AI writes most of our code now. Debugging it when it breaks in production is still slow, because the value that explains the failure was never logged. HyperProbe is an on-call agent for engineering teams. It takes an open incident to a confirmed root cause by dropping read-only probes into your running service and capturing the exact variable state logs don't have. No redeploys, no restarting the app. \
\
📹 **Launch Video: [https://youtu.be/QtaZrQ8_Uk8](https://youtu.be/QtaZrQ8_Uk8)**

**🚧 The Problem**

Team ships faster than ever with agents that write most of our code. This is already shrinking the useful context engineers need to debug AI written code. Not helped by the limited telemetry added in the same code by AI. So when something breaks in prod, the first instinct for engineers is to open logs or throw them to agents. But if the line you are looking for is not there, agents will start guessing the root cause on limited data, forcing engineers to collect more logs by redeploys.

The result: our best engineers become our on-call team, incidents stay open longer, and patches come from data that never capture production context, so issues recur.

You can see where that leads. In September last year, a public fintech in India paid out $5 million after failed transactions were incorrectly marked successful. NYSE the same year miscalculated price bands for 40 symbols, printing trades so wrong they had to be reversed. Same pattern: the code ran clean, wrote the wrong state, and neither logs nor traces could show it.

 ✅ **What Hyperprobe does**

HyperProbe gives engineering teams an on-call agent that works the incident and takes it to a confirmed root cause, live in production.

* **Plan:** the agent picks up the alert from PagerDuty, Datadog, or Slack, then reads your logs and traces to locate the file and line. The easy incidents resolve right here.
* **Probe:** logs not enough? places read-only virtual breakpoints on the suspect lines and captures the exact variable state live, across services. No redeploys, no restarts. 
* **Confirm:** the diagnosis is verified against real captured evidence, not a guess. Your engineer gets a confirmed RCA and commits the fix.

There are two pieces. An SDK that runs inside your service, and an MCP server your coding agent talks to. The SDK is what makes setting probes (virtual breakpoints, log or metric) possible without a redeploy. 

### **🔍 A few examples**

* **An intermittent 500 that won't reproduce locally:** catch it live with full variable state 
* **A third-party API misbehaving:** see the exact payload and response
* **A function returns a wrong value with no error:** see what it computed and why
* **Anything that only happens in prod:** stop redeploying with console.logs

🚀 **The team**

We've both lived this problem. Shailendra ran production at scale. Karan was a senior architect at a SaaS company. Before this, both spent three years building production SDKs for a testing product, learning the hard parts of pulling real runtime state out of a running service without breaking it.

Every incident we watched came down to the same question: what was the actual value at the moment it broke. Nobody built it for the way engineers debug with coding agents now. So we did.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110401&key=user_uploads/3173209/ddf3d8d0-2bd4-4a8c-9547-fa5ea2496469)

### **🎁 Why now**

For thirty years the expensive part of software was writing it, and every tool got built for that. Generation is now nearly free, but the cost didn't disappear. It moved downstream, to figuring out why the generated code broke in production.

And that system is now mostly code no human wrote or holds in their head. When it breaks, the engineer has less context than ever, and their first move is already to hand it to the coding agent. That agent only has your logs and traces, so it guesses. We give it the evidence instead, captured live from the running code at the point of failure.

### **🙏 Our ask**

* If you're an engineer tired of the redeploy loop, debugging code you didn't write at 2 AM, try it on your own service.**,** first investigation in 10 min:[ https://docs.hyperprobe.co/quickstart](https://docs.hyperprobe.co/quickstart)
* If your best engineers have become your on-call team and you want that fixed, let us work one real incident from your stack, free: <https://calendly.com/shailendra-hyperprobe/30min>

launches.title: Verdict Machine: AI cybersecurity for financial institutions’ digital assets

launches.body:
Hey all! We are Dan, Liran, and Isaac. Before Verdict Machine, we launched blockchain security at Check Point (NASDAQ: CHKP).

**TL;DR:** Blockchain is becoming critical infra for all finance. More than $3.4B in digital assets was stolen in 2025. Verdict Machine is AI cybersecurity for financial institutions' digital assets. We use AI to understand each institution's environment, assess cyber risk and generate tailored controls that prevent hacks.

**Building for:** banks, asset managers, DeFi protocols and infra, companies that use stablecoins or RWAs. If that’s you, email us at [founders@verdictmachine.com](mailto:founders@verdictmachine.com).

<https://youtu.be/dYmEjST7Nc8>

### Signed is not safe

Sophisticated hackers don’t need to compromise a wallet to steal funds. They only need to trick an authorized operator into approving one malicious transaction.

On-chain, settlement is final. There is no chargeback and no reversal. The security decision has to happen before the transaction executes.

Attackers are sophisticated and see the entire institution, while existing security tools see fragments:

* Hidden dependencies. Vendors, protocols, bridges and infrastructure are assessed separately or not at all.
* Limited context. Controls check a transaction, not the institution behind it.
* Stale controls. Rules are written once and reviews run once, while the institution and its risk keep changing.

 

### How Verdict Machine works

Verdict Machine uses AI to secure each client end to end.

**Inventory.** It builds the complete inventory of a client’s on-chain environment: assets, wallets, smart contracts, users, vendors, counterparties, and transaction patterns.

**Posture.** It quantifies cyber risk and recommends tailored controls to minimize exposure.

**Enforce controls.** Before execution, it evaluates each proposed transaction to prevent attacks in real time.

The same live model powers every workflow:

**Real time prevention.** Security and compliance teams secure their most critical transactions.

**Continuous cyber diligence.** Asset managers and risk teams underwrite the cyber risk of protocols, vendors, and counterparties before and after capital is deployed.

**Wallet screening.** Payments and stablecoin teams screen for fraud, unauthorized transactions, and risky wallets.

### Why now

Institutions are racing to launch stablecoin and tokenized-asset products. MiCA and DORA are in force, so the people who own this risk now have to show their work. Attackers punish under-protected organizations.

Fireblocks and Chainalysis reached $8B valuations for digital asset custody and compliance. Cybersecurity for on-chain finance is a bigger opportunity. Every financial institution is going to use digital assets and therefore will require digital-asset cybersecurity.

### Traction

We left Check Point the day before Y Combinator started. We already have POCs with asset managers and digital-asset infrastructure providers moving billions of dollars weekly for financial institutions, and we are in active evaluations with a digital-asset team at one of the world's largest banks.

### Why us

We previously launched and led blockchain security at Check Point (NASDAQ: CHKP). Our CTO Isaac is a cyber veteran from Matzov, Israel’s cryptography unit. We are crypto natives with many years building infra for crypto and fintech. We built Verdict Machine to bring AI-native, institution-specific security to on-chain finance.

Managing or deploying crypto, stablecoins, or tokenized assets? Talk to us.

launches.title: Dock – A multiplayer agent workspace that gives you a team of proactive agents that feel like colleagues instead of chat boxes
launches.tagline: Get 3x more done in a fraction of the time with a team of Dock agents.
launches.body:
After a decade building and scaling companies — including Branch, which[ Govind](https://www.linkedin.com/in/govindkavaturi/) and I grew from zero to $100M+ ARR — we kept hitting the same wall: doing more always meant hiring more. Now, for the first time, it doesn't have to. That's why we built[ **Dock**](https://trydock.ai/).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JO0dwm_NU_s>

AI agents have changed what's possible, which is why we're building again. Dock gives you a team of proactive AI agents  that work alongside you — they talk to each other, hand off work, and take initiative instead of waiting to be prompted. So you steer instead of babysitting a dozen chat windows.

## **The Problem**

AI agents can finally do real work. But today they work alone — isolated chats that sit there waiting for you to prompt them. The moment you run more than one, _you_ become the middleman: copy-pasting context between a dozen windows and unblocking every agent by hand. The more agents you add, the more work you create for yourself. It doesn't scale.

## **The Solution**

Dock turns those isolated agents into a real team. Here's how it works:

### **1. Spin up a team of specialized AI agents in minutes.**

Each agent has a real role, its own objectives, and persistent memory — so it gets better at its job over time instead of resetting every session.

### **2. They work together, proactively.**

Your agents  pursue goals on their own, message each other, and hand off work when one needs something from another — no copy-pasting, no you relaying context. They only come back to you when there's a real decision to make.

### **3. You and your team work right alongside them.**

Everyone — humans and AI agents  — works in the same shared workspace, toward the same goals. The earlier you plug Dock in, the more your agents  learn about how your company actually works.

## **Why this works**

Multi-agent coordination is an infrastructure problem, and we built that infrastructure. Dock runs its own agent harness and runtime, executes in the cloud or on your machine, and gives every agent memory, schedules, and a shared workspace as primitives. Agents working as a team is not a feature we added. It’s what the system is.

## **Why we're building this**

We've spent our careers inside growing companies — hiring, scaling, managing — and felt the coordination drag of every new person you add. When AI made it possible to grow output without growing the team, this problem was already ours. In a real way, Dock found us more than we found it. Today we run our entire company on Dock, and we think soon every company will run on humans and AI agents  working together.

Get early access:[ **trydock.ai**](http://trydock.ai)

launches.title: OpenRelay: The Inference Delivery Network
launches.tagline: One API for inference across every chip.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** OpenRelay is building an Inference Delivery Network (IDN) on top of its CDN for GPUs. We provide one entrypoint for inference across every chip. 

Send us a workload and we’ll cut your costs up to 20% by running it through our network, balancing the best available accelerator (NVIDIA, TPU, Trainium, AMD) across clouds and handing back a single endpoint. You never pick the hardware, chase quotas, or rebuild your stack per provider. And if you run GPUs or other AI accelerators (an NVIDIA cluster, TPUs, a reserved fleet), you can plug your capacity into our rails and we'll bring the inference demand. Get started [here](https://openrelay.inc/).

P.S. sign up for our Luma page to be notified of our Launch Party!

<https://luma.com/s6x8cx5x>

\
<https://youtu.be/7uNhqcjBXJg>

## The Team

Hey guys! We're **Jaden and Prashant**, the founders of OpenRelay. We came at the same problem from opposite sides.

* Jaden built a half-megawatt data center at 20 from a warehouse shell, then joined Voltage Park early, where he ran virtualization and helped stand up HPC.
* Prashant built accelerator infra at AWS, where he ran custom model deployments and wrote custom kernels to squeeze out Trainium performance.

 

We kept seeing the same thing: there's more AI compute than ever, and you still can't reach it. We left our jobs to fix that.

## The Problem

Compute is everywhere; liquidity is nowhere. Accelerators are scattered across dozens of clouds, chip vendors, and operators, each behind its own quotas, drivers, contracts, and console. Teams that want to run inference can't reach the capacity, and the capacity can't reach them.

Running inference naively is easy; running it at scale is hard. Any operator can spin up a model on a box. Turning idle GPUs into a production endpoint (load balancing, isolation, autoscaling, failover, metering, billing) is a software platform most individual operators won't build. So capacity sits stranded behind their own front door, and developers either overpay for scarce reserved GPUs or hand-stitch a fragile multi-provider stack.

## Solution

We built one set of rails across all of it.

Send a workload (any container or model) and we schedule it onto the best-fit accelerator, attach a production endpoint, and scale it. We route to the cheapest accelerator that meets your latency and throughput targets, and we benchmark continuously. If the market can't beat renting yourself, we backstop with our own inference demand, so you’re never on the hook. 

You never pick the chip, cloud, or region; we handle routing, isolation, failover, metering, and billing across 4+ clouds and every major chip family. We're language- and framework-agnostic (no SDK lock-in), and you can drive everything from our CLI and REST API.

It's two-sided: if you run GPUs or other accelerators (a neocloud, a data center, a pay for an underutilized reserved fleet), you can connect that capacity to our rails and we'll bring the inference demand, turning hardware into a revenue-generating endpoint without building a platform yourself.

## Traction

We're **live in production**, generating 100 billion tokens a week across 22 physical locations across Europe, APAC, North America, and the Middle East running on 8 different accelerator SKUs.  

## Asks

We'd love to hear from you!

* **Run GPUs, or know someone who does?** This is who we most want to talk to: companies running their own nodes for inference, data centers, reserved fleets, even a crypto or mining cluster looking to move into AI. Plug your capacity into our rails and we'll bring the demand. Reach us at [founders@openrelay.inc](https://mailto:founders@openrelay.inc).
* **Shipping inference and tired of picking chips?** Bring a workload and we'll get you on the best available hardware today.
* **Feedback, intros, or just want to chat?** Book a call with us, or email [founders@openrelay.inc](mailto:founders@openrelay.inc) for anything else.

launches.title: Agent FM: One group chat to hear and steer your coding agents.
launches.tagline: Computer use + live audio updates + group chat with your agents. One command center to end agent babysitting.
launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋

We're [Aniket](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anideshp/) & [Mugdhaa](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mugdhaa-patankar/), co-founders of [Agent FM](https://www.agentfm.ai/).

**TL;DR:** Agent FM is a desktop app that gives engineers one group chat to hear and steer their coding agents. Instead of manually bouncing between different claude code and codex sessions, and combing through walls of text to monitor agents, engineers just tune in to Agent FM. Agents share important progress updates, blockers, assumptions, and decisions in the group chat. Engineers get live text and audio updates and respond right from the chat.

**Launch video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bVGLQwclkYI> 

#### The Problem:

**Babysitting agents is exhausting.** Engineers running claude code and codex agents spend all day bouncing between multiple sessions, combing through walls of text to keep track of the work. In long horizon tasks, agents often go down the wrong paths, add unnecessary complexity or make bad assumptions that waste time and tokens. Agents can also sometimes misinterpret instructions, make poor decisions, or perform destructive actions due to lack of context and context compaction. To avoid this, engineers continuously keep tabs on their agents, read agent trajectories realtime for anything substantial worth intercepting. This gets really exhausting with more agents and time. We lack the tooling that automatically does this for engineers.

#### Our Solution:

* **One interface to rule them all:** Computer use + live audio updates + group chat with your agents. One command center to interact with your coding agents without babysitting and manually polling different Claude Code and Codex sessions.
* **Actionable metrics and insights into agent activity across model providers:** Deep insights and metrics about token spend across providers, cost distribution, skills and mcp token performance, and recurring patterns.
* **Works with the tools engineers already use:** No setup needed. Agent FM automatically works across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other coding tools. Local and remote workspaces supported.
* **Voice-to-text AI**: Context aware and low-latency voice-to-text AI to prompt 4x faster anywhere on your computer.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109244&key=user_uploads/355672/6ac94f50-a6ac-4b2d-9290-819f9711037e)

#### Traction

* **410 engineers** are using Agent FM (**60+ paying**), 
* **120k+ audio updates** heard by engineers. 
* **1.2 hours/day** average time spent on Agent FM

#### Our asks

* Give Agent FM a try and let us know what you think: [agentfm.ai](http://agentfm.ai)
* If there’s a team or company you think would benefit with Agent FM, write to us at [founders@agentfm.ai](mailto:founders@agentfm.ai) 

#### The Team:

Aniket and Mugdhaa have known each other for almost 10 years and co-founded Agent FM in 2026.

Aniket (CEO) worked at Meta Superintelligence Labs, where he built agent-orchestration, RL, and search infra, fine-tuned models, grew Meta AI monthly active users by 250K and built critical parts of the Llama training data flywheel.

Mugdhaa (CTO) led AI for developer productivity at Snowflake, where she built model harnesses, evals, developer tooling, and orchestration systems that help engineers adopt AI and move faster. Before Snowflake, she worked at Twitch on live video playback and distribution, building systems that keep Twitch reliable at scale for the biggest live events on the internet (Ibai La Velada, MrBeast), serving 10M+ concurrent requests.

Today we're introducing Locke, an applied AI company changing the way companies and governments work together. Our first focus: building an AI-native government affairs firm that helps companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts.

American governments spend over $10 trillion a year - and it's all up for grabs, reallocated annually through budgets, appropriations, and contracts. But while every other major market has been made accessible, government hasn't. Its front door is guarded by legacy government affairs firms that charge incumbent prices, and their customers get a fragmented product: one firm for the Hill, another for agencies, another for proposals and procurement, with no one accountable for the outcome.

Locke is building the front door government never had. We combine our AI agents with in-house lobbyists who own the entire path - from research to first meeting to funded contract. On the backend, our agents make the path faster than ever - analyzing legislation, tracking stakeholder engagement, and drafting complex contract proposals.

Since quietly launching six weeks ago, we've blown past a $500K annual revenue run-rate serving clients across defense, healthcare, GovTech, and more.

Locke was founded by Parth Badhwar, who came to this problem from both sides of the table: policy roles at the White House and Deloitte, then leading GTM at a startup that sold to dozens of government offices. The team is small, talent-dense, and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch.

Locke’s mission is bigger than replacing lobbying firms. It's a future where winning government support depends on what you make, not who you know.

It's day one in that mission.

Learn more at [locke.inc](http://locke.inc) or email [founders@locke.inc](mailto:founders@locke.inc).

launches.tagline: An extension of your team handling sourcing, planning and contracting.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** SpaceFlow is an AI-native procurement services company for businesses that make, move and serve physical goods. We help procurement teams bring more spend under management, execute source-to-contract work and turn identified savings into realized savings without adding headcount or replacing existing systems.

<https://youtu.be/lS9pBj_LeV8>

### The problem

Procurement must absorb changing demand, supplier issues, and growing volume without increasing cost or risking continuity. Every existing option fails on the same axis:

* **Internal teams:** expertise and judgment, fixed capacity. It takes years to build and when someone leaves, the tacit knowledge that keeps operations running is lost.
* **SaaS:** automation and visibility without execution. The customer still staffs the operation, supervises it, handles exceptions, and owns the result.
* **Outsourcing:** capacity, expertise, and accountability, permanently labor-linked. More volume, suppliers, and locations require more service-delivery headcount.

The unmet need is operating capacity that **takes responsibility for completing the work** while becoming faster, more consistent, and more profitable as volume grows.

## The insight

* **Software can recommend actions; it cannot assume commercial authority.** The customer keeps execution, exceptions, and supplier outcomes. Whoever owns the exceptions owns the expertise, and expertise is the entire product in procurement.
* **Incumbents cannot follow.** Consulting and outsourcing firms store process knowledge in employees and grow revenue through staff hours. Automation directly cannibalizes that model.
* **The economics are breakable.** Traditional services sit below software economics: Accenture at Rule-of-22.6, Genpact at 24.1. An AI-native operator can reach **Rule-of-60**.

## What we built

**The proprietary platform SpaceFlow uses to operate procurement for customers.**

* A **process-mapping engine** converts interviews, SOPs, approval rules, and existing system configurations into executable workflows. A supply-chain consultancy estimates it cuts customer launch from **26 months to 4**, a 6.5x jump in deployment capacity.
* It **executes procurement end to end**, from demand and production planning through sourcing, contracting, purchase orders, exception resolution, and reconciliation, across the customer's own systems.
* Operating across companies in the same vertical turns cross-company experience into **proprietary process and supplier intelligence**, while pooled demand creates **group-purchasing power**: better execution, prices, resilience, and terms for every customer.
* The same platform **monitors service levels, resolves exceptions, and remains accountable** for completing the operation. Per-action autonomy limits, approval queues, and an immutable audit log make every task provable.

## Proof so far

* **Live:** $400M a year of supplier spend under management, zero systems migrated. Multiple six figure contracts signed.
* **Demand for delegation:** our first customer cancelled 3 planned procurement hires, the CSCO invested his own money, and two chains are signing to progressively outsource purchasing, one planning a procurement team 90% smaller by 2027.
* **Results:** 3x faster RFQ cycles, off-contract spend down 42% at one customer, $120K a year saved at another.

## Where this goes

SpaceFlow will replace legacy service providers across the physical economy. Traditional service firms grow by hiring; SpaceFlow grows output faster than headcount, targeting **$1B in revenue with headcount capped at 100**. 

## What's in it for you?

1. **You run a physical-goods company with $100M+ supplier spend:** send us 12 months of PO history and we'll map one lane and size the savings, free. [spaceflow.tech](http://spaceflow.tech) · [emre@spaceflow.tech](mailto:emre@spaceflow.tech)
2. **You know an operator like that:** intros are gold. 

### **About the team:**

**Emre Isik (CEO)**  studied computer engineering at the University of Cambridge and dropped the master's to build SpaceFlow full time. Before that he researched embedded AI for motor control at UCLA's Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics, published a machine-learning paper on reasoning with small data, and trained with Turkey's international informatics olympiad reserve team at 15. 

**Ali Eren Aytekin (co-founder)** left engineering at Istanbul Technical University to build SpaceFlow.  He was Microsoft Imagine Cup EMEA runner-up for a genetic-signal classifier that hit 98.3% accuracy, and co-authored the published paper on low-data reasoning. [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ali-eren-aytekin-6305a41aa/) . He talked his way into an invite-only AI showcase in Istanbul, came out with a procurement problem from the CEO of a UK medical manufacturer, and shipped the solution with the team in two weeks. That deal became the learning SpaceFlow grew from.

**Hakan Enes Aksu (co-founder)** left information engineering at Boğaziçi University to build SpaceFlow. He has been shipping commercial software since 16, when his Reddit ad-automation service earned $40K in revenue, and he later built a tender-matching engine that reads public tenders against a company's product catalog and sold it to a corporate customer for five figures. He scored in the top 500 out of roughly 3 million students in Turkey's national university entrance exam. [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hakan-enes-aksu/)

launches.title: Tracer: Fable-level AI at 1/3 the cost using open-weight models
launches.tagline: Adaptive AI systems that combine open-weight models for better answers at lower cost.
launches.body:
Hi! I’m Adam, founder of Tracer.

We built **Echo**, an adaptive AI system built entirely from open-weight models. Instead of making you choose between models, Echo decides how much compute each request needs, which models should work on it, and how their answers should be combined.

**Across our current eval mix, Echo reaches Fable-level performance at roughly 1/3 the inference cost.**

Today, Echo is strongest on math, science, and the coding benchmarks we currently cover. Multilingual and broader knowledge performance still has room to improve, while longer-horizon coding and agentic evaluations are underway.

Echo is continuously updated as we expand the model pool and improve ensembling and cross-model coordination.

<https://youtu.be/hM0NypILdgw>

## **Why we built Echo**

There are now dozens of strong models, each with different strengths, weaknesses, and prices.

We started with a simple experiment: what if you had a perfect oracle that always knew which model would perform best for each request?

The oracle was substantially stronger than any individual model in the pool.

Echo is our attempt to recover that advantage without knowing the answer beforehand.

Instead of picking one model for everything, Echo goes beyond routing and dynamically allocates compute across a pool of open-weight models behind a single interface.

## **The result**

We evaluate Echo against frontier models across reasoning, math, coding, multilingual and other benchmarks.

We measure both **quality and the actual model inference cost used to produce the answers.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108361&key=user_uploads/1217984/867cc6aa-16b8-4330-b497-c33d78e62b24)

On MATH-500, Echo reached **98.6% at $4.58**, compared with Claude Fable at **99.8% at $12.64**.

On LiveCodeBench, Echo reached **92.8% at $5.35**, compared with Claude Fable at **92.0% at $8.71**.

These results show where Echo is already strongest. LiveCodeBench is encouraging, but it does not capture the full difficulty of repository-level and agentic coding. We are currently running longer-horizon evaluations where Echo must plan, use tools, modify code, and recover from errors across multiple steps.

Those results are visible in the Eval Observatory and are active areas of improvement.

We publish the underlying evaluations, including individual answers, costs, wins, and losses:

**→[ Explore the Echo Eval Observatory](https://echo.tracerml.ai/eval?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**

## **From open source to Echo**

We first explored this idea through Tracer's open-source work: learning from real AI workloads where expensive model calls are actually necessary and where cheaper paths are enough.

The project has now crossed **1,000 GitHub stars**, with developers using and experimenting with the approach in their own AI pipelines.

Echo is the next step. Instead of optimizing individual calls with a routing layer, we're building one adaptive system that decides how intelligence should be allocated end to end.

**→ [GitHub](http://github.com/adrida/tracer)**

## **Every company’s AI traffic has a shape**

Our public evaluations test Echo across a broad mix of general tasks. Production workloads are different.

Every company has its own traffic distribution and quality requirements. Some requests genuinely need expensive frontier-level intelligence. Many don’t.

For teams that work with us, Echo can be configured to learn the structure of their workload and identify where expensive intelligence is useful and where cheaper paths are enough.

**Public Echo does not train on users’ private traces. Workload-specific learning is enabled only for teams that explicitly work with Tracer to configure it.**

We set up this optimization with each team around its workload, quality bar, and data requirements.

The goal is simple: **an AI system that continuously learns how to spend the minimum amount of inference required to maintain the quality you need.**

That means **\~3x cheaper is not necessarily the ceiling for a real production workload.**

## **Try Echo now**

Echo is publicly available through a chat UI and an **OpenAI-compatible API**.

You can try it directly, connect an existing application by changing the base URL, or plug Echo into OpenCode and other agent harnesses.

Echo is continuously updated as we improve model selection and ensembling.

**→[ Try Echo now](https://echo.tracerml.ai)**

## **We’re looking for teams with large inference workloads**

If your company is running meaningful LLM inference in production, we’d like to test Echo against your workload.

We’ll map the quality-cost frontier on your traffic and determine how much of your inference actually requires expensive intelligence.

Teams can then work with us to activate private, workload-specific optimization.

→ [**Optimize Echo for your workload**](https://cal.com/adam-rida-tracer/tracer-first-call)

## **About Tracer**

I’m **Adam Rida**, founder of Tracer. I was previously a PhD candidate at **Sorbonne University/CNRS**, where I conducted and published research in ML interpretability. Before founding Tracer, I built applied ML systems across finance, insurance, and supply chain, then grew [DeepRecall](http://deeprecall.io/) to \~**€100k ARR as a solo founder in less than 3 months**.

I’ve spent most of my career studying how models make decisions and turning that research into production systems.
